9:1: This noble Surah is one of the last to be revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as Al-Bukhari said: Abu Al-Walid told us, Shu'bah told us on the authority of Abu Ishaq, who said: I heard Al-Bara' say: The last verse to be revealed was "They ask you for a legal opinion. Say: God gives you a legal opinion concerning those who are not yet born." And the last Surah to be revealed was Bara'ah. The reason why he did not mention the Basmalah at the beginning of it was because the Companions did not write the Basmalah at the beginning of it in the original Mushaf, but rather they followed the example of the Commander of the Faithful, Uthman bin Affan, may God be pleased with him and satisfy him, as Al-Tirmidhi said: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, Yahya bin Saeed, Muhammad bin Ja'far, Ibn Abi Uday, and Suhayl bin Yusuf told us: Awf bin Abi Jamila told us, Yazid Al-Farsi told me, Ibn Abbas told me: I said to Uthman bin Affan: What made you go to Al-Anfal, which is from the Mathani, and to Bara'ah, which is from the Mi'in, and you paired them together and did not write a line between them, In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, and you put it in the seven long ones? What made you do that? Uthman said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was one of those upon whom time would come, and surahs of many numbers would be revealed. Whenever something was revealed to him, he would call one of those who used to write and say: Place this verse in the surah in which such and such is mentioned. Al-Anfal was among the first to be revealed in Medina, and Bara’ah was among the last to be revealed of the Qur’an. Its story was similar to its story, and I thought it was part of it. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed away without explaining to us that it was part of it, so for that reason I combined them and did not write between them a line saying: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. I placed it in the seven long surahs. This is how Imam Ahmad, Abu Dawud, Al-Nasa’i, and Ibn Hibban narrated it in his Sahih, and Al-Hakim in his Mustadrak from other chains of transmission on the authority of Awf Al-A’rabi. Al-Hakim said: Its chain of transmission is sound, and they did not include it. The beginning of this noble surah was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he returned from the Battle of Tabuk and was on the Hajj. Then he mentioned that the polytheists were attending their year this season as was their custom, and that they would circumambulate the House naked. He disliked mixing with them, and he sent Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him, as the leader of the Hajj that year to establish People have their rituals and he teaches the polytheists not to perform Hajj after this year, and he calls out to the people, Disavowal from God and His Messenger. So when he returned, he followed him with Ali ibn Abi Talib to be a messenger from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, because he was a group of his, as will be explained. The Almighty’s statement: A declaration of immunity from God and His Messenger means this is a declaration of immunity, i.e. a declaration of innocence from God and His Messenger “to those of the polytheists with whom you made a treaty. So travel freely throughout the land for four months.” The commentators differed greatly here. Some said: This verse is for those with absolute, non-temporary treaties, or for those who have a treaty of less than four months, so they complete four months for them. As for those who have a temporary treaty, then their term is until its term, whatever it may be, because God the Almighty said: Then fulfill their treaty with them until their term Al-Baqarah 2:17, and because of what will come in the hadith. And whoever has a treaty between him and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, then his treaty is until its term. This is the best and strongest of the statements, and Ibn Jarir, may God have mercy on him, chose it, and it was narrated from Al-Kalbi, Muhammad ibn Ka’b Al-Qurazi, and more than one. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: “A declaration of immunity from God and His Messenger to those of the polytheists with whom you have made a treaty. So travel freely in the land for four months” Al-Akhir, he said: God’s limit for those who have made a treaty with His Messenger is four months, during which they can travel wherever they wish. He set a deadline for those who have no treaty until the end of Muharram, which is fifty nights. So God commanded His Prophet when the sacred months have passed to put the sword to those with whom he has no treaty, killing them until they enter Islam. He commanded those who have a treaty, when four months have passed, from the Day of Sacrifice until the tenth of Rabi’ al-Akhir, to put the sword to them also until they enter Islam. Abu Ma`shar al-Madani said: Muhammad ibn Ka`b al-Qurazi and others told us: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Abu Bakr as a leader of the Hajj season in the year nine, and he sent Ali ibn Abi Talib with thirty or forty verses from Bara`ah, and he recited them to the people, giving the polytheists four months to roam the earth. He recited them to them on the Day of Arafah, giving them the twentieth of Dhul-Hijjah, Muharram, Safar, the month of Rabi` al-Awwal, and ten days of Rabi` al-Akhir. He recited them to them in their homes and said: No polytheist shall perform Hajj after this year of ours, and no one shall circumambulate the House naked. Ibn Abi Nujayh said, on the authority of Mujahid, Disavowal from God and His Messenger to the people of the covenant, Khuza’ah, Mudlij, and whoever had a covenant or others. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned from Tabuk when he had finished. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wanted to perform Hajj, but he said: Only the polytheists will come and circumambulate naked, so I do not like to perform Hajj until that does not happen. So he sent Abu Bakr and Ali, may God be pleased with them, and they circumambulated the people in Dhu al-Majaz and in their places where they used to trade and in all the seasons. They gave permission to the people of the covenant to believe for four months, which are the consecutive months, twenty from Dhu al-Hijjah to ten days after which they will be free from Rabi’ al-Akhir, then they will have no covenant. He gave permission to all the people to fight unless they believe. This is how it was narrated from al-Suddi and Qatadah. Al-Zuhri said: The beginning of the postponement was from Shawwal and its end was at the end of Muharram. This statement is strange, and how can they be held accountable for a period whose ruling they did not receive, but rather its matter became clear to them on the Day of Sacrifice when the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called out for that. For this reason, God the Almighty said:

9:3: God Almighty says, and the notification from God and His Messenger and the progress and warning to the people on the greatest day of Hajj which is the Day of Sacrifice which is the best day of the rituals and the most apparent and the most gathering that God is free from the polytheists and His Messenger meaning He is also free from them. Then He called them to repent to Him, and He said, So if you repent meaning from what you are in of polytheism and misguidance it is better for you, and if you turn away meaning you continue in what you are doing then know that you will not frustrate God rather He is able to do you and you are in His grip and under His power and will, and give tidings to those who disbelieve of a painful punishment meaning in this world with disgrace and punishment and in the Hereafter with whips and shackles. Al-Bukhari, may God have mercy on him, said: Abdullah bin Yusuf told us, Al-Layth told us, Aqil told me on the authority of Ibn Shihab who said: Humayd bin Abd al-Rahman told me that Abu Hurayrah said: Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, sent me on that Hajj with the muezzins whom he sent on the Day of Sacrifice to call to prayer. In Mina, no polytheist should perform Hajj after this year and no one should circumambulate the House naked. Humayd said: Then the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) sent Ali ibn Abi Talib behind him and ordered him to proclaim Bara’ah. Abu Hurayrah said: So Ali proclaimed Bara’ah with us among the people of Mina on the Day of Sacrifice, and that no polytheist should perform Hajj after this year and no one should circumambulate the House naked. Al-Bukhari also narrated it: Abu Al-Yaman told us, Shu’ayb told us on the authority of Al-Zuhri, Humayd ibn Abd Al-Rahman told me that Abu Hurayrah said: Abu Bakr sent me with those who proclaimed on the Day of Sacrifice in Mina, that no polytheist should perform Hajj after this year and no one should circumambulate the House naked. The greater day of Hajj is the Day of Sacrifice. It was only called the greater because people say it is the lesser Hajj. So Abu Bakr announced to the people that year, so no polytheist performed Hajj in the year of the Farewell Pilgrimage in which the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) performed Hajj. This is the wording of Al-Bukhari in the Book of Jihad. Abdul Razzaq said: On the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Ibn Al-Musayyab, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, regarding his statement: A declaration of immunity from God and His Messenger, he said: When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was in the time of Hunayn, he performed the Umrah from Al-Juhranah, then he ordered Abu Bakr to perform that Hajj. Muammar said: Al-Zuhri said: Abu Hurairah used to narrate that Abu Bakr ordered Abu Hurairah to call the Adhan for the declaration of immunity during Abu Bakr’s Hajj. Abu Hurairah said: Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Ali after us and ordered him to call the Adhan for the declaration of immunity, and Abu Bakr was on the season as he was, or he said in his form. This context is strange in that the Emir of the Hajj in the year of the Umrah of Al-Juhranah was none other than Atab bin Asid, while Abu Bakr was the Emir in the year nine. Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of al-Sha`bi, on the authority of Muharrir ibn Abi Hurairah, on the authority of his father, who said: I was with Ali ibn Abi Talib when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent him to the people of Mecca with the declaration of innocence. He said: What were you calling out? He said: We were calling out that none shall enter Paradise except a believing soul, and no naked person shall circumambulate the House, and whoever has a treaty between him and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, his term or duration is four months. When the four months have passed, then God and His Messenger are free from the polytheists, and no polytheist shall perform Hajj to this House after this year of ours. He said: So I called out until my voice became hoarse. Al-Sha`bi said: Muharrir ibn Abi Hurairah told me, on the authority of his father, who said: I was with Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent him to call out. When he became hoarse, I called out, and I said: What were you calling out? He said: Four things: No one should circumambulate the House naked; whoever has a covenant with the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him), his covenant is valid for its term; none shall enter Paradise except a believing soul; and no polytheist shall perform Hajj after this year of ours. Narrated by Ibn Jarir from other chains of narration on the authority of Ash-Sha’bi, and narrated by Shu’bah on the authority of Mughirah on the authority of Ash-Sha’bi with it, except that he said: And whoever has a covenant between him and the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him), his covenant is valid for four months. And he mentioned the rest of the hadith. Ibn Jarir said: I fear that it is a mistake on the part of some of its narrators because the reports are in agreement regarding the term to the contrary. Imam Ahmad said: Affan told us, Hammad told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent him with the innocence of God with Abu Bakr. When he reached Dhu al-Hulayfah, he said: No one shall deliver it except me or a man from my family. So he sent it with Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him. Al-Tirmidhi narrated it in the interpretation: on the authority of Bandar on the authority of Affan and Abd al-Samad, both of them on the authority of Hammad bin Salamah, on his authority. Then he said: Hasan Gharib from the hadith of Anas, may God be pleased with him. Abdullah bin Ahmad bin Hanbal said: Muhammad bin Sulayman told us - Lawin - Muhammad bin Jabir told us on the authority of Samak on the authority of Hanash on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, who said: When ten verses of the innocence of God were revealed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, called Abu Bakr and sent him with them to read them to the people of Mecca. Then he called me and said: Catch up with Abu Bakr, and wherever you find him, take the letter from him, then go to the people of Mecca and read it to them. So I caught up with him at al-Juhfah and took the letter from him. Abu Bakr returned to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, God, did He send down something? He said, “No, but Gabriel came to me and said: ‘None shall perform it on your behalf except you or a man from you.’” This is a weak chain of transmission, and it does not mean that Abu Bakr may God be pleased with him returned immediately, but rather after he had completed the rituals that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) had commanded him to perform, as was explained in the other narration. Abdullah also said: Abu Bakr told me, Amr ibn Hammad told us, on the authority of Asbat ibn Nasr, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Hanash, on the authority of Ali may God be pleased with him, that when the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) sent him with the declaration of innocence, he said, O Prophet of God, I am not a good speaker or orator. He said, I must go with it myself or you must go with it. He said, If it is necessary, then I will go. He said, Go, for God will make your tongue firm and guide your heart. Then he put his hand on his mouth. Imam Ahmad said: Sufyan told us on the authority of Abu Ishaq on the authority of Zaid bin Yathi’, a man from Hamdan, we asked Ali, for what purpose have you been sent? He meant the day the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent him with Abu Bakr on the Hajj. He said: I have been sent with four things: None shall enter Paradise except a believing soul, none shall circumambulate the House naked, whoever has a treaty with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, his treaty shall last for its term, and neither the polytheists nor the Muslims shall perform Hajj after this year. At-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Qilabah on the authority of Sufyan bin Uyaynah and he said: It is good and authentic, thus he said. Shu’bah narrated it on the authority of Abu Ishaq and he said: Zaid bin Yathi’ made a mistake in it. Ath-Thawri narrated it on the authority of Abu Ishaq on the authority of some of his companions on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Wakee’ told us, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Zakariya, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Zaid bin Yathi’, on the authority of Ali, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent me when Bara’ah was revealed with four things: that no naked person should circumambulate the House, and no polytheist should approach the Sacred Mosque after this year of theirs, and whoever has a treaty between him and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, it shall be for its term, and none shall enter Paradise except a believing soul. Then Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Muhammad bin Abd al-A’la, on the authority of Ibn Thawr, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of al-Harith, on the authority of Ali, who said: I was commanded with four things, and he mentioned them. Israel said on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Zaid bin Yathi’, who said: Bara’ah was revealed, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Abu Bakr, then he sent Ali and took it. When Abu Bakr returned, he said: Was it revealed about something? He said: No, but I have been ordered to convey it, myself or a man from my family. So he set out for the people of Mecca and established four things among them: No polytheist shall enter Mecca after this year, no one shall circumambulate the House naked, no one shall enter Paradise except a Muslim soul, and whoever has a covenant between him and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, his covenant shall last for its term. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said on the authority of Hakim ibn Hakim ibn Abbad ibn Hanif on the authority of Abu Ja`far Muhammad ibn `Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn `Ali, who said: When Bara`ah was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he had sent Abu Bakr to establish the Hajj for the people, it was said: O Messenger of God, why don’t you send to Abu Bakr? He said: No one will carry it out on my behalf except a man from my family. Then he called Ali and said: “Go with this story from Surat Bara’ah and announce to the people on the Day of Sacrifice when they gather at Mina, that no disbeliever will enter Paradise, no polytheist will perform Hajj after this year, no naked person will circumambulate the House, and whoever has a covenant with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, it is his until its term.” So Ali, may God be pleased with him, went out on the Messenger of God’s she-camel, Al-Adhba’, until he caught up with Abu Bakr on the road. When Abu Bakr saw him, he said: Are you a leader or someone who is being commanded? He said: Rather, he was commanded. Then they went on and Abu Bakr established the Hajj for the people at that time in that year according to the Hajj positions they had in the pre-Islamic era. Then, when the Day of Sacrifice came, Ali ibn Abi Talib stood up and announced to the people what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had commanded him to do. He said: O people, no unbeliever will enter Paradise, and no polytheist will perform Hajj after this year, and no one will circumambulate the House naked. Whoever has a covenant with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, it is until its term. So no polytheist performed Hajj after that year, and no one will circumambulate the House naked. Then they came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. This was from the innocence of those who were from the polytheists, from the people of the general covenant and the people of the term until the appointed time. Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abdul-Hakam told us, Abu Zur’ah Wahb God ibn Rashid told us, Haywah ibn Shuraih told us, Ibn Sakhr told us that he heard Abu Mu’awiyah al-Bajali from the people of Kufa say: I heard Abu al-Sahba’ al-Bakri saying: I asked Ali about the greatest day of Hajj, and he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Abu Bakr ibn Abi Quhafah to lead the Hajj for the people, and he sent me with him with forty verses from Bara’ah until he came to Arafat and addressed the people on the Day of Arafat. When he finished his sermon, he turned to me and said: Get up, Ali, and deliver the message of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. So I got up and recited to them forty verses from Bara’ah, then we set out and came to Mina, threw stones at the Jamarat and slaughtered the camel, then shaved my head and I knew that not all of the people of the assembly had attended Abu Bakr’s sermon on the Day of Arafat, so I went around, following the tents with it, reciting it to them. From that I think you thought it was the Day of Sacrifice, but it is the Day of Arafat. Abd al-Razzaq said on the authority of Mu’ammar on the authority of Abu Ishaq: I asked Abu Juhaifa about the Day of The greatest pilgrimage. He said: The Day of Arafah. I said: Is he from among you or from the companions of Muhammad (peace be upon him)? He said: All of that. Abd al-Razzaq also said: On the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’, who said: The greatest day of pilgrimage is the Day of Arafah. Umar ibn al-Walid al-Shanni said: Shihab ibn Abbad al-Basri told us on the authority of his father, who said: I heard Umar ibn al-Khattab say: This is the Day of Arafah, this is the greatest day of pilgrimage, so no one should fast on it. He said: So I performed pilgrimage after my father, and I came to Madinah and asked about the best of its people. They said: Saeed ibn al-Musayyab. So I went to him and said: I asked about the best of the people of Madinah. They said: Saeed ibn al-Musayyab. Tell me about fasting on the Day of Arafah. He said: I will tell you about someone who is a hundred times better than me, Umar or Ibn Umar. He used to forbid fasting on it and used to say: It is the greatest day of pilgrimage. Narrated by Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim. It was also narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, Mujahid, Ikrimah, and Tawus that they said: The Day of Arafah is the greatest day of pilgrimage. It was narrated in it by a mursal hadith narrated by Ibn Jurayj, I was told on the authority of Muhammad ibn Qays on the authority of Ibn Makhramah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave a sermon on the Day of Arafah and said: This is the greatest day of Hajj. It was narrated from another source: on the authority of Ibn Jurayj on the authority of Muhammad ibn Qays on the authority of Al-Miswar ibn Makhramah on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he gave a sermon to them in Arafah and praised God and extolled Him and then said: As for what follows, this is the greatest day of Hajj. The second opinion is that it is the Day of Sacrifice. Hisham said on the authority of Ismail ibn Abi Khalid on the authority of Al-Sha’bi on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, who said: The greatest day of Hajj is the Day of Sacrifice. Ishaq Al-Sabi’i said on the authority of Al-Harith Al-A’war: I asked Ali, may God be pleased with him, about the greatest day of Hajj and he said: It is the Day of Sacrifice. Shu’bah said on the authority of Al-Hakam I heard Yahya ibn Al-Jazzar narrating on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, that he went out on the Day of Sacrifice on a white mule heading to the cemetery and a man came and took hold of the reins of his mount and asked him about the greatest day of Hajj and he said: It is this day of yours, let it go. Abd Al-Razzaq said: on the authority of Sufyan on the authority of Shu’bah on the authority of Abd Al-Malik ibn Umair on the authority of Abd God ibn Abi Awfa said: The greatest day of Hajj is the Day of Sacrifice. Shu’bah and others narrated something similar on the authority of Abd al-Malik ibn Umair. Hisham and others narrated it in the same way on the authority of al-Shaibani on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abi Awfa. Al-A’mash said on the authority of Abdullah bin Sinan: Al-Mughira bin Shu’ba addressed us on the day of Eid al-Adha on a camel and said: This is the day of Eid al-Adha, this is the day of sacrifice, and this is the day of the greater Hajj. Hammad bin Salamah said on the authority of Samak on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: The greater Hajj is the day of sacrifice. This was also narrated on the authority of Abu Juhayfah, Sa’id bin Jubayr, Abdullah bin Shaddad bin al-Haad, Nafi’ bin Jubayr bin Mut’am, al-Sha’bi, Ibrahim al-Nakha’i, Mujahid, Ikrimah, Abu Ja’far al-Baqir, al-Zuhri, and Abd al-Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam that they said: The greater day of Hajj is the day of sacrifice. Ibn Jarir chose this. The hadith on the authority of Abu Hurayrah was mentioned in Sahih al-Bukhari that Abu Bakr sent them on the day of sacrifice to call the adhan in Mina. Other hadiths have been reported on this matter, as Imam Abu Ja’far bin Jarir said: Sahl bin Muhammad al-Hasani told me, Abu Jabir al-Harami told us, Hisham bin al-Ghazi al-Jarshi told us on the authority of Nafi’ on the authority of Ibn Umar who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood on the day of sacrifice at the Jamarat in… The Farewell Pilgrimage, and he said: This is the greatest day of Hajj. This is how Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated it from the hadith of Abu Jabir, whose name is Muhammad ibn Abd al-Malik, and Ibn Mardawayh also narrated it from the hadith of al-Walid ibn Muslim, from Hisham ibn al-Ghazi, from him, then he narrated it from the hadith of Saeed ibn Abd al-Aziz, from Nafi’, from him, and Shu’bah said from Amr ibn Murrah from Murrah al-Hamadani from a man from the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood among us on a red, green she-camel and said: Do you know what day this is? They said: The Day of Sacrifice. He said: You have spoken the truth, it is the greatest day of Hajj. Ibn Jarir said: Ahmad ibn al-Muqaddam told us, Yazid ibn Zurai’ told us, Ibn Awn told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sirin, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakra, on the authority of his father, who said: When that day came, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sat on his camel and the people took hold of its reins or bridle, and he said: What day is this? We remained silent until we thought that he would give it a different name, and he said: Isn’t this the day of the greater pilgrimage? This is a sound chain of transmission and its original is included in Sahih. Abu al-Ahwas said, on the authority of Shabib ibn Gharqadah, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Amr ibn al-Ahwas, on the authority of his father, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, during the Farewell Pilgrimage, say: What day is this? They said: Today is the greater pilgrimage. It was narrated on the authority of Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab that he said: The day of the greater pilgrimage is the second day from the Day of Sacrifice. This was narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. Mujahid also said: The day of the greater pilgrimage is all the days of pilgrimage, and Abu Ubayd said the same. Sufyan said: The day of pilgrimage, the day of the camel, and the day of Siffin, meaning all its days. Sahl al-Siraj said: Al-Hasan al-Basri was asked about the day of the greater pilgrimage. He said: What do you have to do with the greater Hajj? That was the year in which Abu Bakr, whom the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had made the Hajj, performed it, and he led the people in Hajj. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Wakee’ told us, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Awn, I asked Muhammad, meaning Ibn Sirin, about the day of the greater Hajj, and he said: It was a day in which the Hajj of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, coincided with the Hajj of the people of the hair.
9:4: This is an exception to the four-month postponement period for someone who has an absolute, non-temporary covenant. His period is four months during which he roams the earth, going wherever he wants to save himself, except for someone who has a temporary covenant, whose period is until the specified period for which he was covenanted. The hadiths have been presented. Whoever has a covenant with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, his covenant is until its term, on condition that the covenantor does not break his covenant and does not support anyone against the Muslims, i.e., does not support anyone other than them against them. This is the one who is fulfilled in his covenant and pledge until its term, and for this reason God Almighty urged fulfilling that, saying, Indeed, God loves the righteous, i.e., those who fulfill their covenant.
9:5: The commentators differed on what is meant by the sacred months here. What are they? Ibn Jarir went to that which is mentioned in the saying of God Almighty: “Of them are four sacred months. That is the right religion, so do not wrong yourselves therein” 3:10. Abu Ja`far al-Baqir said, but Ibn Jarir said: The last of the sacred months in their case is Muharram. This is what he went to, narrated by Ali ibn Abi Talhah from Ibn Abbas, and Ad-Dahhak also went to it, but there is a problem with it. What appears from the context is what Ibn Abbas went to in the narration of Al-Awfi from him, and Mujahid, Amr ibn Shu`ayb, Muhammad ibn Ishaq, Qatadah, As-Suddi, and Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: What is meant by it are the four months of travel stipulated in His saying: So travel freely in the land for four months. Then He said: And when the sacred months have passed, meaning when the four months in which We have forbidden you to fight them and have granted them respite have passed, then wherever you find them, kill them, because returning to the covenant on what is mentioned is more appropriate than what is implied. Then the ruling on the four sacred months will come in another verse after in this noble surah. And his saying: Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them meaning on the ground, and this is general, and the famous opinion is to specify it with the prohibition of fighting in the sanctuary, with his saying: “And do not fight them at the Sacred Mosque until they fight you there. But if they fight you, then kill them.” And his saying: And take them meaning, and take them prisoner if you wish, by killing them, and if you wish, by taking them prisoner. And his saying: And besiege them and lie in wait for them at every place of ambush meaning, do not be satisfied with merely finding them, but rather target them by besieging them in their strongholds and fortresses and by lying in wait for them on their roads and paths until you constrict the spacious areas for them and force them to be killed or to convert to Islam. For this reason he said: “But if they repent and establish prayer and give zakah, then let them go on their way. Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful.” For this reason, the friend, may God be pleased with him, relied in fighting those who withheld zakah on this noble verse and others like it, as he prohibited fighting them on the condition of these actions, which are entering Islam and performing its duties, and he pointed out with the highest of them the lowest of them, for the most honorable pillars of Islam after the two testimonies is prayer, which is the right of God. Glory be to Him, and after that, performing zakat, which is a benefit that extends to the poor and needy, and it is the most honorable of actions related to creation. That is why God often pairs prayer with zakat. It was reported in the two Sahihs on the authority of Ibn Umar, may God be pleased with them, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: I have been commanded to fight the people until they testify that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God, establish prayer, and pay zakat. The hadith. Abu Ishaq said: On the authority of Abu Ubaidah, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, may God be pleased with him, who said: You have been commanded to establish prayer and pay zakat, and whoever does not pay zakat, his prayer is not valid. Abd al-Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam said: God refused to accept prayer without zakat, and he said: May God have mercy on Abu Bakr, how knowledgeable he was! Imam Ahmad said: Ali bin Ishaq told us, Abdullah bin Mubarak told us, Hamid al-Tawil told us on the authority of Anas that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I have been commanded to fight people until they testify that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God. So when they testify that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God, and face our Qiblah, eat our slaughtered animals, and pray as we pray, then their blood and property are forbidden to us except for a right. They have what the Muslims have and are subject to what they are subject to.” Al-Bukhari narrated it in his Sahih and the people of Sunan except Ibn Majah, on the authority of Abdullah bin Mubarak. Imam Abu Ja`far bin Jarir said: Abdul-A`la bin Wasil al-Asadi told us, Ubayd God bin Musa told us, Abu Ja`far al-Razi told us on the authority of al-Rabi` bin Anas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever departs this world with sincerity to God alone and worshipping Him without associating anything with Him, departs from it and God is pleased with him. He said: Anas said: It is the religion of God that the Messengers brought and conveyed from their Lord before the chaos of hadiths and the difference of desires. And the confirmation of that is in the Book of God in the last of what was revealed. God Almighty said: But if they repent and establish prayer and give zakah, then let them go on their way. He said: Their repentance is to abandon idols and worship their Lord and establish prayer and give zakah. Then He said in another verse: But if they repent and establish prayer and give zakah, then they are your brothers in religion. It was narrated by Ibn Mardawayh and by Muhammad ibn Nasr al-Marwazi in his book on prayer. Ishaq bin Ibrahim told us, Hakam bin Salamah told us, Abu Jaafar Al-Razi told us the same, and this noble verse is the verse of the sword about which Ad-Dahhak bin Muzahim said: It abrogated every covenant between the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and one of the polytheists, and every contract and every period. Al-Awfi said: On the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding this verse, no covenant or protection remained for any of the polytheists since Bara’ah was revealed, and the expiration of the sacred months and the period of whoever had a covenant from the polytheists before Bara’ah was revealed is four months, from the day he permitted Bara’ah to the tenth of the first of the month of Rabi’ al-Akhir. Ali bin Abi Talha said: On the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding this verse, he said: God Almighty commanded him to put the sword on those who had a covenant if they did not enter Islam, and he broke what was named for them of the covenant and pact, and removed the first condition. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ishaq bin Musa al-Ansari told us, Sufyan bin Uyaynah said: Ali bin Abi Talib said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent four swords to the polytheists among the Arabs. God Almighty said: Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them. This is how he narrated it in an abbreviated form. I think that the second sword is to fight the People of the Book, as God Almighty said: “Fight those who do not believe in God or the Last Day and do not consider unlawful what God and His Messenger have forbidden and do not adopt the religion of truth from among those who were given the Scripture - until they pay the jizyah with willing submission.” The third sword is to fight the hypocrites, as God Almighty said: O Prophet, strive hard against the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and the fourth is to fight the aggressors, as God Almighty said: “And if two parties among the believers should fight, then make peace between them. But if one of them oppresses the other, then fight the one that oppresses until it returns to the command of God.” Then the commentators differed regarding this verse about the sword. Ad-Dahhak and As-Suddi said that it was abrogated by God Almighty’s saying: Either as a favor or as a ransom. Qatada said the opposite.
9:6: God Almighty says to His Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, And if any of the polytheists seek your protection, that is, he asks you for safety, then answer his request so that he may hear the word of God, that is, the Qur’an, which you recite to him and mention to him something about the matter of religion by which you establish God’s proof against him. Then escort him to his place of safety, that is, while he is safe and secure until he returns to his country, home, and place of safety. That is because they are a people who do not know, that is, We only legislated safety for such people so that they may learn the religion of God and the call of God may spread among His servants. Ibn Abi Nujayh said on the authority of Mujahid in his interpretation of this verse: A person comes to you to hear what you say and what has been revealed to you, he is safe until he comes to you and you hear the words of God and until he reaches his place of safety where he came. From this, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would give safety to whoever came to him seeking guidance or with a message, as a group of messengers from Quraysh came to him on the day of Hudaybiyyah, among them Urwah ibn Mas`ud, Mukarraz ibn Hafs, Suhayl ibn `Amr and others, one after the other, hesitating about the case between him and the polytheists. They saw from the Muslims’ veneration of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, what dazzled them and what they had not seen from a king or a Caesar, so they returned to their people and informed them of this, and this and similar things were among the greatest reasons for the guidance of most of them. This is also why when the messenger of Musaylimah the Liar came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said to him, Do you bear witness that Musaylimah is the Messenger of God? He said yes, so the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) said: Were it not that messengers are not killed, I would have beheaded you. God had ordained for him the beheading during the emirate of Ibn Mas'ud over Kufa. He was called Ibn al-Nawahah. It became apparent during the time of Ibn Mas'ud that he testified to Musaylima's prophethood, so Ibn Mas'ud sent for him and said to him: You are not now on a mission, and he ordered him to be beheaded, may God not have mercy on him or curse him. The point is that whoever comes from the land of war to the land of Islam to deliver a mission, trade, or seek peace or a truce, or carry a tribute, or something similar, and asks the Imam or his deputy for security, is given security as long as he is in the land of Islam, and until he returns to his place of safety and homeland. However, the scholars said that it is not permissible to allow him to reside in the land of Islam for a year, but it is permissible to allow him to reside for four months, and in between that, for more than four months and less than a year, there are two opinions from Imam al-Shafi'i and other scholars, may God have mercy on them.
9:7: God Almighty shows His wisdom in disavowing the polytheists and looking at them for four months, then after that the sharp sword where they were found, so God Almighty said: How can there be a treaty for the polytheists meaning security and they are left in what they are doing while they are polytheists with God and disbelievers in Him and His Messenger except those with whom you made a treaty at the Sacred Mosque meaning the day of Hudaybiyyah, as God Almighty said: They are the ones who disbelieved and prevented you from the Sacred Mosque and the sacrificial animals, preventing them from reaching their destination the verse, So as long as they are upright with you, be upright with them meaning no matter how much you adhere to what you agreed upon and made a treaty with them to leave war between you and them for ten years, “be upright with them. Indeed, God loves the righteous” and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did that and so did the Muslims. The treaty and truce with the people of Mecca continued from Dhul-Qi'dah in the sixth year until Quraysh broke the treaty and sided with their allies, namely Banu Bakr, against Khuza'ah, the allies of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and killed them with them in the sanctuary as well. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, invaded them in Ramadan of the eighth year, and God opened the sacred land for him and gave him control over their forelocks, praise and thanks be to God. He released those of them who had converted to Islam after being subjugated and defeated, and they were called the freed ones, and they were close to two thousand. And whoever persisted in his disbelief and fled from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he sent to him security and freedom in the land for four months to go wherever he wanted, and among them were Safwan ibn Umayya, Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl and others. Then God guided them after that to complete Islam, and God is the Praiseworthy for all that He decrees and does.
9:8: The Almighty says, inciting the believers to be hostile to them and disavow them, and explaining that they do not deserve to have a covenant with them because of their associating partners with God the Almighty and their disbelief in the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and because if they were to prevail over the Muslims and be victorious over them, they would not leave anyone behind, nor would they observe any kinship or covenant with them. Ali bin Abi Talhah, Ikrimah, and Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The kinship is the kinship and the covenant is the covenant. And so said Ad-Dahhak and As-Suddi, as Tamim bin Muqbil said: People are corrupted by their successors, who have severed family ties and kinship ties. Hassan bin Thabit, may God be pleased with him, said: We found them lying, O God, and the One of God and the Covenant does not lie. Ibn Abi Nujayh said on the authority of Mujahid: They do not observe regarding a believer anything but God. He said: God is God. In another narration: They do not observe God or anyone else. Ibn Jarir said: Yaqub told me, Ibn Ulayyah told us on the authority of Sulayman on the authority of Abu Majlaz regarding the words of God Almighty: They do not observe regarding a believer any pact or covenant, like the words of Gabriel, Michael, Israfil, as if he was saying they do not observe God. The first statement is more apparent and famous, and most people agree with it. Also on the authority of Mujahid: God is the covenant. Qatada said: God is the oath.
9:9: God Almighty says, blaming the polytheists and urging the believers to fight them, They have exchanged the verses of God for a small price, meaning that they replaced following the verses of God with the base worldly matters that distracted them. So they turned away from His path, meaning they prevented the believers from following the truth. “Indeed, evil is what they have been doing. They do not observe towards a believer any pact of kinship or covenant.” Its interpretation has been presented, as has the verse that follows it, But if they repent and establish prayer, to the end of it, which has been presented. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar said: Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, Yahya bin Abi Bakr told us, Abu Jaafar Al-Razi told us, Al-Rabi’ bin Anas told us: I heard Anas bin Malik say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever departs from this world with sincerity towards God and worshipping Him, not associating partners with Him, and establishing prayer and giving zakat, departs from it and God is pleased with him.” This is the religion of God that the messengers brought and conveyed from their Lord, before the chaos of hadiths and the difference of desires and the confirmation of that in the Book of God. But if they repent, meaning if they abandon idols and their worship, and establish prayer and give zakat, then let them go on their way. And he said in another verse: But if they repent and establish prayer and give zakat, then they are your brothers in religion. Then Al-Bazzar said: The end of the hadith with me, and God knows best, he departed from it and God is pleased with him, and the rest of it with me is from the words of Al-Rabi’ bin Anas.
9:10: God Almighty says, blaming the polytheists and urging the believers to fight them, They have exchanged the verses of God for a small price, meaning that they replaced following the verses of God with the base worldly matters that distracted them. So they turned away from His path, meaning they prevented the believers from following the truth. “Indeed, evil is what they have been doing. They do not observe towards a believer any pact of kinship or covenant.” Its interpretation has been presented, as has the verse that follows it, But if they repent and establish prayer, to the end of it, which has been presented. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar said: Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, Yahya bin Abi Bakr told us, Abu Jaafar Al-Razi told us, Al-Rabi’ bin Anas told us: I heard Anas bin Malik say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever departs from this world with sincerity towards God and worshipping Him, not associating partners with Him, and establishing prayer and giving zakat, departs from it and God is pleased with him.” This is the religion of God that the messengers brought and conveyed from their Lord, before the chaos of hadiths and the difference of desires and the confirmation of that in the Book of God. 9:12: God the Almighty says: And if the polytheists with whom you have made a treaty for a specified period break their oaths, that is, their covenants and agreements, “and attack your religion, that is, they criticize it and belittle it. From here comes the killing of whoever insults the Messenger, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, or whoever attacks the religion of Islam or speaks ill of it. For this reason, He said: Then fight the leaders of disbelief, for indeed, they have no oaths, that perhaps they will desist, that is, they will return from their disbelief, stubbornness, and misguidance. Qatada and others said: The leaders of disbelief, such as Abu Jahl, Utbah, Shaibah, Umayyah ibn Khalaf, and a number of men. On the authority of Mus’ab ibn Sa’d ibn Abi Waqqas, he said: Sa’d ibn Abi Waqqas passed by a man from the Khawarij, so the Khawarij said: This one is from the leaders of disbelief. Sa’d said: You lied, rather I fought the leaders of disbelief. Narrated by Ibn Mardawayh. Al-A’mash narrated on the authority of Zaid ibn Wahb on the authority of Hudhayfah that he said: The people of this verse have not been fought after that. It was narrated on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him: something similar. The correct view is that the verse is general, and even if the reason for its revelation was the polytheists of Quraysh, it is general for them and others, and God knows best. Al-Walid ibn Muslim said: Safwan ibn Amr told us on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr ibn Nufayr, that during the reign of Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, when he sent them to the Levant, he said to the al-Nas 114:You will find people whose heads have been shaved, so strike the knots of Satan among them with swords, for by God, killing one man among them is more beloved to me than killing seventy of others, because God says: Fight the leaders of disbelief. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim.
9:13: This is also an incitement, incitement and temptation to fight the polytheists who broke their oaths and who intended to expel the Messenger from Mecca, as God Almighty said: And when those who disbelieved plotted against you to restrain you or kill you or expel you - and they plotted, and God plotted - and God is the best of plotters. And God Almighty said: They expel the Messenger and you because you believe in God, your Lord verse, and God Almighty said: And they almost provoked you from the land to expel you from it verse, and His statement: And they began against you the first time It was said that what was meant by that was: the day of Badr when they went out to support their caravan, but when it was saved and they knew about that, they continued on their faces, seeking to fight out of aggression and arrogance as was explained previously, and it was said that what was meant was their breaking of the covenant and their fighting with their allies Banu Bakr against Khuza'ah, the allies of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, until the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, marched against them in the year of the conquest, and what happened happened, and praise and thanks be to God. And His statement: Do you fear them? But God is more deserving that you should fear Him, if you are believers. God the Almighty says: Do not fear them, but fear Me, for I am worthy of being feared by the servants from My power and My punishment, for in My hand is the command, and whatever I will will be, and whatever I do not will will not be. Then He said, as a determination for the believers and a clarification of His wisdom in what He has prescribed for them of jihad, despite His ability to destroy the enemies by His command: Fight them; God will punish them by your hands and will disgrace them and give you victory over them and satisfy the hearts of a believing people. This is general for all believers. Mujahid, Ikrimah, and As-Suddi said regarding this verse: And satisfy the hearts of a believing people meaning Khuza’ah, and He repeated the pronoun in His statement: And remove the anger of their hearts to them also. Ibn Asakir mentioned in the biography of a muezzin for Omar bin Abdul Aziz, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of Muslim bin Yasar, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, that when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, became angry, he would take hold of her nose and say, O Awish, say, O God, Lord of the Prophet Muhammad, forgive my sin, remove the anger in my heart, and save me from the misleading trials. He narrated it through the path of Abu Ahmad al-Hakim, on the authority of al-Baghdadi, on the authority of Hisham bin Ammar, who told us, Abd al-Rahman bin Abi al-Jawza’, on his authority, And God accepts the repentance of whomever He wills, meaning of His servants, and God is Knowing, meaning of what is good for His servants, Wise in His cosmic and legal actions and words, so He does what He wills and rules as He wills, and He is the Just and Judge who never transgresses and does not waste an atom’s weight of good or evil, but rather He rewards for it in this world and the hereafter.
9:14: This is also an incitement, incitement and temptation to fight the polytheists who broke their oaths and who intended to expel the Messenger from Mecca, as God Almighty said: And when those who disbelieved plotted against you to restrain you or kill you or expel you - and they plotted, and God plotted - and God is the best of plotters. And God Almighty said: They expel the Messenger and you because you believe in God, your Lord verse, and God Almighty said: And they almost provoked you from the land to expel you from it verse, and His statement: And they began against you the first time It was said that what was meant by that was: the day of Badr when they went out to support their caravan, but when it was saved and they knew about that, they continued on their faces, seeking to fight out of aggression and arrogance as was explained previously, and it was said that what was meant was their breaking of the covenant and their fighting with their allies Banu Bakr against Khuza'ah, the allies of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, until the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, marched against them in the year of the conquest, and what happened happened, and praise and thanks be to God. And His statement: Do you fear them? But God is more deserving that you should fear Him, if you are believers. God the Almighty says: Do not fear them, but fear Me, for I am worthy of being feared by the servants from My power and My punishment, for in My hand is the command, and whatever I will will be, and whatever I do not will will not be. Then He said, as a determination for the believers and a clarification of His wisdom in what He has prescribed for them of jihad, despite His ability to destroy the enemies by His command: Fight them; God will punish them by your hands and will disgrace them and give you victory over them and satisfy the hearts of a believing people. This is general for all believers. Mujahid, Ikrimah, and As-Suddi said regarding this verse: And satisfy the hearts of a believing people meaning Khuza’ah, and He repeated the pronoun in His statement: And remove the anger of their hearts to them also. Ibn Asakir mentioned in the biography of a muezzin for Omar bin Abdul Aziz, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of Muslim bin Yasar, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, that when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, became angry, he would take hold of her nose and say, O Awish, say, O God, Lord of the Prophet Muhammad, forgive my sin, remove the anger in my heart, and save me from the misleading trials. He narrated it through the path of Abu Ahmad al-Hakim, on the authority of al-Baghdadi, on the authority of Hisham bin Ammar, who told us, Abd al-Rahman bin Abi al-Jawza’, on his authority, And God accepts the repentance of whomever He wills, meaning of His servants, and God is Knowing, meaning of what is good for His servants, Wise in His cosmic and legal actions and words, so He does what He wills and rules as He wills, and He is the Just and Judge who never transgresses and does not waste an atom’s weight of good or evil, but rather He rewards for it in this world and the hereafter.

9:16: God Almighty says: Or do you think, O believers, that We will leave you neglected and not test you with matters in which the people of true resolve will be distinguished from the liars? For this reason He said: And God has not yet made evident those among you who strive and have not taken besides God or His Messenger or the believers an intimate friend, meaning an inner circle and an insider, but rather they are, outwardly and inwardly, sincere to God and His Messenger. So He was satisfied with one of the two categories instead of the other, as the poet said: I do not know if I go to a land seeking good, which of the two is more suitable for me God the Almighty said in another verse: “Alif, Lam, Meem. Do people think that they will be left to say, ‘We believe’ and they will not be tested? And We have certainly tested those before them - so God will surely make evident those who are truthful and He will surely make evident the liars.” And God the Almighty said: Or do you think that you will enter Paradise while God has not yet made evident those among you who strive and made evident the steadfast? And God the Almighty said: God would not leave the believers in that state you are in until He distinguishes the wicked from the good. The gist of it is that when God the Almighty prescribed jihad for His servants, He made clear that He has wisdom in it, which is to test His servants, who will obey Him and who will disobey Him. And He the Almighty knows what was and what will be and what would not have been if it had been, how it would have been. So He knows a thing before it is and while it is as it is. There is no god but Him and no lord but Him, and there is no one who can prevent what He has decreed and carried out.
9:17: God Almighty says: It is not appropriate for those who associate others with God to maintain the mosques of God which were built in His name alone, with no partner for Him. And whoever recites the mosque of God means the Sacred Mosque, the most honorable of mosques on earth, which was built from the first day for the worship of God alone, with no partner for Him, and it was founded by the Friend of the Most Merciful. This is while they are witnessing against themselves that they are disbelievers, that is, by their state and their speech. Al-Suddi said: If you asked a Christian, What is your religion? he would say, Christian. And if you asked a Jew, What is your religion? he would say, Christian. If a Jew had said, a Sabean would have said a Sabean, and a polytheist would have said a polytheist, Their deeds have become worthless, meaning because of their polytheism, and in the Fire they will abide eternally. And God the Almighty said, “And what is the matter with them that God should not punish them while they hinder [people] from al-Masjid al-Haram, although they were not its guardians? Its guardians are only the righteous, but most of them do not know.” And for this reason God the Almighty said, The mosques of God shall be maintained only by those who believe in God and the Last Day. So God the Almighty testified to the faith of those who maintain mosques, as Imam Ahmad said: Shuraih told us, Ibn Wahb told us, on the authority of Amr ibn al-Harith, that Diraaj Abu al-Samh told him, on the authority of Abu al-Haitham, on the authority of Abu Sa’id al-Khudri, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, If you see a man frequenting the mosque, then testify to his faith. God the Almighty said, The mosques of God shall be maintained only by those who believe in God and the Last Day. And it was narrated by al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Wahb with it. Abdul Rahman bin Hamid said in his Musnad: Yunus bin Muhammad told us, Salih Al-Murri told us, on the authority of Thabit Al-Banani, on the authority of Maimun bin Siyah and Ja`far bin Zaid, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The only ones who maintain mosques are the people of God. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar narrated it on the authority of Abdul Wahid bin Ghiyath, on the authority of Salih bin Bashir Al-Murri, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The only ones who maintain mosques are the people of God. Then he said: We do not know of anyone who narrated it on the authority of Thabit other than Salih. Al-Darqutni narrated in Al-Afrad on the authority of Hakamah bint Uthman bin Dinar, on the authority of her father, on the authority of his brother Malik bin Dinar, on the authority of Anas, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: If God wills to afflict a people, He looks at the people of the mosques and turns them away from them. Then he said: It is strange. Al-Hafiz Al-Baha’i narrated in Al-Mustaqsa on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Umayyah Al-Tarsusi, Mansur bin Suqair told us, Salih Al-Murri told us, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: God says: By My glory and majesty, I will…” I am about to punish the people of the earth, but when I look at the people of my house, at those who love one another, and at those who seek forgiveness in the early hours of the morning, I will turn that away from them. Then Ibn Asakir said: A strange hadith. Imam Ahmad said: Ruh told us, Saeed told us, Qatada told us, Al-Ala’ bin Ziyad told us, Muadh bin Jabal told us that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Satan is a wolf to man, like a wolf to sheep, seizing the distant and isolated sheep. So beware of the valleys and stick to the congregation, the public and the mosque.” Abd al-Razzaq said: Muammar told us, Abu Ishaq told us, Amr bin Maymun al-Awdi told us: I met the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they were saying: The mosques are the houses of God on earth, and it is God’s right to honor those who visit Him in them. Al-Mas’udi said: Habib bin Abi Thabit and Adi bin Thabit told us, Saeed bin Jubair told us, Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, said: Whoever hears the call to prayer and does not respond, does not come to the mosque and pray, then his prayer is not valid and he has disobeyed God and His Messenger. God Almighty said: The mosques of God shall be maintained only by those who believe in God and the Last Day (al-Baqarah 2:170). Narrated by Ibn Mardawayh. It has been narrated with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, from another source, and there are corroborating reports from other sources, but this is not the place to elaborate on them. And His statement: And establishes prayer meaning which is the greatest of the bodily acts of worship and gives zakat meaning which is the best of deeds that extend to the goodness of creation, and His statement and fears none but God meaning and fears none but God the Most High and fears none but Him Then it is likely that those will be among the [rightly] guided. Ali ibn Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding His statement: The mosques of God shall be maintained only by those who believe in God and the Last Day meaning: whoever believes in the Oneness of God and believes in the Last Day, he means whoever believes in what God has revealed and establishes prayer meaning the five daily prayers and fears none but God meaning he worships none but God, then He said: Then it is likely that those will be among the [rightly] guided. God the Most High says: Indeed, those are the successful ones, as He said to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: It is possible that your Lord will raise you to a station of praise which is intercession, and every may in the Qur’an is obligatory, and Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar, may God have mercy on him, said: And may from God is true.

9:19: Al-Awfi said in his interpretation on the authority of Ibn Abbas in the interpretation of this verse, he said: The polytheists said: Maintaining the House of God and taking care of the water supply is better than believing and striving, and they were proud of the sanctuary and were arrogant about it because they were its people and its maintainers, so God mentioned their arrogance and their turning away, so He said to the people of the sanctuary from the polytheists: My verses were recited to you, but you were turning back on your heels, arrogant, spending time with it and neglecting it. He means that they were arrogant about the sanctuary. He said: Passing it they were spending time with it and neglecting the Qur’an and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so God preferred faith and striving with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, over the polytheists’ maintenance of the House and taking care of the water supply, and it did not benefit them with God with associating partners with Him, even though they used to maintain His House and perform the rituals of ihram with it. God Almighty said: They are not equal before God, and God does not guide the wrongdoing people. Meaning those who claimed that they were the people of construction, so God called them wrongdoers because of their polytheism, so construction did not benefit them at all. Ali ibn Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas in the interpretation of this verse: It was revealed about Al-Abbas ibn Abdul Muttalib when he was taken prisoner at Badr. He said: If you had preceded us in Islam, migration and jihad, we would have maintained the Sacred Mosque, provided water for the poor and freed the captives. God the Almighty said: “Have you considered the provision of water for the pilgrims and the maintenance of the Sacred Mosque equal to one who believes in God and the Last Day and strives in the cause of God? They are not equal in the sight of God. And God does not guide the wrongdoing people.” He means that all of that was in polytheism and I do not accept what was in polytheism. Ad-Dahhak ibn Muzahim said: The Muslims turned to Al-Abbas and his companions who were taken prisoner on the day of Badr, taunting them with polytheism. Al-Abbas said: By God, we used to maintain the Sacred Mosque, free the captives, cover the Kaaba and provide water for the pilgrims. Then God revealed: Have you considered the provision of water for the pilgrims? Abdul Razzaq said: Ibn Uyaynah told us on the authority of Ismail on the authority of Al-Sha’bi: He said: It was revealed about Ali and Al-Abbas, may God be pleased with them, regarding what they said about that. Ibn Jarir said: Yunus told me, Ibn Wahb told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told me on the authority of Abu Sakhr, he said: I heard Muhammad bin Ka’b Al-Qurazi say: Talha bin Shaiba from Banu Abd Al-Dar, Abbas bin Abdul Muttalib and Ali bin Abi Talib boasted, so Talha said: I am the owner of the house, I have its key, and if I wish I could spend the night in it. Al-Abbas said: I am the owner of the water-supply and the one who takes care of it, and if I wish I could spend the night in the mosque. Ali, may God be pleased with him, said: I do not know what you are saying. I prayed towards the qibla for six months before the people, and I am the owner of jihad. Then God Almighty revealed: Have you made the provision of water for the pilgrims? The whole verse, and this is what Al-Suddi said, except that he said: Ali, Al-Abbas, and Shaiba bin Othman boasted, and he mentioned something similar. Abdul Razzaq said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said: It was revealed about Ali, Al-Abbas, Othman, and Shaiba, who spoke about that, and Al-Abbas said: I do not see myself except that I will abandon our water-providers, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Stay in charge of your water-providers, for there is good for you in it. And Muhammad bin Thawr narrated it, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Al-Hasan, and he mentioned something similar. A hadith with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet was reported in the interpretation of this verse, so it is necessary to mention it here. Abdul Razzaq said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Yahya bin Abi Katheer, on the authority of Al-Nu’man bin Bashir, may God be pleased with him, that a man said: I do not care if I do not do any work after Islam except that I water the pilgrims. Another said: I do not care if I do not do any work after Islam except that I maintain the Sacred Mosque. And another said: Jihad in the way of God is better than what you have said. Omar, may God be pleased with him, rebuked them and said: Do not raise your voices at the pulpit of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and that was on Friday, but when we prayed Friday prayers we would go to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and ask him. Then the verse was revealed: Do you consider the provision of water to the pilgrims and the maintenance of the Sacred Mosque equal to one who believes in God and the Last Day and strives in the cause of God? They are not equal. Another way Al-Walid bin Muslim said: Muawiyah bin Salam told me on the authority of his grandfather Abu Salam Al-Aswad on the authority of Al-Nu’man bin Bashir Al-Ansari who said: I was at the pulpit of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) with a group of his companions and one of them said: I do not care if I do not do any work for God after accepting Islam except providing water to the pilgrims. Another said: Rather, maintaining the Sacred Mosque. And another said: Rather, jihad in the way of God is better than what you have said. So Umar bin Al-Khattab may God be pleased with him rebuked them and said: Do not raise your voices at the pulpit of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him), and that was on Friday. But when I have prayed the Friday prayer, I will go to the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) and ask him about what you differed about. He said: So he did, and then God the Almighty revealed: “Do you consider providing water to the pilgrims and maintaining the Sacred Mosque equal to one who believes in God and the Last Day and strives in the way of God? They are not equal in the sight of God. And God does not guide the wrongdoing people.” Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih, Abu Dawud and Ibn Jarir with this wording, Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn Abi Hatim in their commentaries and Ibn Hibban in his Sahih.

9:23: God Almighty commanded us to separate ourselves from the disbelievers in Him, even if they were our fathers or sons, and He forbade us from befriending them if we liked it, that is, if we chose disbelief over faith, and He threatened us for that, as in His Almighty saying: “You will not find a people who believe in God and the Last Day having affection for those who oppose God and His Messenger, even if they were their fathers or their sons or their brothers or their kindred. Those - He has inscribed faith in their hearts and supported them with spirit from Him - and He will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow.” [Al-Baihaqi], and Al-Hafiz Al-Bayhaqi narrated from the hadith of Abdullah bin Shawdhab, who said: Abu Abi Ubaidah bin Al-Jarrah kept describing the gods to him on the day of Badr, and Abu Ubaidah kept turning away from him, so when Al-Jarrah increased his son Abu Ubaidah went after him and killed him, so God revealed this verse about him: You will not find a people who believe in God and the Last Day having affection for those who oppose God and His Messenger. [Al-Baihaqi] Then the Almighty commanded His Messenger to threaten those who prefer their families, relatives and clan over God, His Messenger and jihad in His cause, saying: “Say: ‘If your fathers, your sons, your brothers, your wives, your clan, wealth that you have acquired, commerce in which you fear decline, and dwellings that please you,’” meaning, you love them for their goodness and beauty, meaning, if these things are dearer to you than God and His Messenger and jihad in His cause, then wait,’ meaning, wait for what will befall you of His punishment and chastisement. That is why He said, “until God brings about His command. And God does not guide the wicked people.” Imam Ahmad said: Qutaybah ibn Saeed narrated to us, Ibn Lahi’ah narrated to us, on the authority of Zuhra ibn Ma’bad, on the authority of his grandfather, who said: We were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he was holding the hand of Umar ibn al-Khattab, and he said: By God, O Messenger of God, you are dearer to me than everything except my own self. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: None of you will believe until I am dearer to him than his own self. Umar said: By God, now you are dearer to me than my own self. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Now, O Umar. Al-Bukhari alone transmitted it, and he narrated it on the authority of Yahya ibn Sulayman, on the authority of Ibn Wahb, on the authority of Haywah ibn Shuraih, on the authority of Abu Uqayl Zuhra ibn Ma’bad, that he heard his grandfather Abdullah ibn Hisham say this on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. It has been proven in Sahih that he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, none of you will believe until I am dearer to him than his father, his son, and all of mankind. Imam Ahmad and Abu Dawud narrated, and the wording is his, from the hadith of Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Khurasani, on the authority of Ata’ al-Khurasani, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “When you engage in `inah transactions and hold on to the tails of cows, And you are satisfied with the crops and abandon the jihad, God will send upon you humiliation that He will not remove until you return to your religion.” Imam Ahmad also narrated on the authority of Yazid bin Harun on the authority of Abu Janab on the authority of Shahr bin Hawshab that he heard Abdullah bin Amr on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar to that. This is evidence for what came before it, and God knows best.
