9:25: Ibn Jurayj said on the authority of Mujahid: This is the first verse revealed from Bara'ah, in which God Almighty mentions to the believers His favor upon them and His kindness to them in His victory for them in many of their battles with His Messenger, and that this is from Him Almighty and with His support and decree, not by their number or their number. He alerted them that victory is from Him, whether the group is small or large. On the day of Hunayn, their large number pleased them, but despite this, it did not benefit them at all, so they turned their backs, except for a few of them with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then He revealed His victory and support upon His Messenger and the believers who were with him, as we will explain in detail, God willing, to teach them that victory is from Him alone and with His support, even if the group is small. How many a small group has overcome a large group by God’s permission? And God is with the patient. Imam Ahmad said: Wahb ibn Jarir told us, my father told us, I heard Yunus narrating on the authority of Al-Zuhri on the authority of Ubaydullah on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The best of the Companions are four, the best of the raiding parties are four hundred, and the best of the armies are four thousand, and twelve thousand will not be defeated due to their small number.” This is how Abu Dawud and Al-Tirmidhi narrated it. Then he said: This is a very strange hasan hadith that no one has a chain of transmission for except Jarir ibn Hazim. Rather, it was narrated on the authority of Al-Zuhri on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, as a mursal. Ibn Majah, Al-Bayhaqi and others narrated it on the authority of Aktham Al-Jawni on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a similar manner, and God knows best. The Battle of Hunayn took place after the conquest of Mecca in Shawwal of the year eight of the Hijra. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had finished the conquest of Mecca and its affairs were prepared and most of its people had converted to Islam and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had released them, he was informed that Hawazin had gathered to fight him and that their leader was Malik ibn Auf ibn al-Nadr, and with him were Thaqeef in its entirety and Banu Jashm and Banu Saad ibn Bakr and Awza’ of Banu Hilal who were few in number and some of Banu Amr ibn Amir and Auf ibn Amir who had come with women and children and sheep and came with them all and all of them. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out to them with his army that had come with him for the conquest and it was ten thousand of the Muhajireen and Ansar and the tribes of the Arabs and with him were those who had converted from the people of Mecca who were the freed ones in two thousand. So he marched with them to the enemy and they met in a valley between Mecca and Taif called Hunayn and the battle took place there at the beginning of the day in the darkness of dawn. They descended into the valley and Hawazin had ambushed them. When they faced each other, the Muslims did not notice except that they had revolted against them and pelted them with arrows and drew their swords and charged as one man as their king had ordered them. Then the Muslims turned back, as God the Almighty said, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood firm while he was riding his gray mule that day, leading it towards the enemy, and his uncle Al-Abbas was holding its right stirrup, and Abu Sufyan ibn Al-Harith ibn Abdul Muttalib was holding its left stirrup, weighing it down so that it would not go too fast, and he was mentioning his name, may God bless him and grant him peace, and calling the Muslims to return and saying: To me, servants of God, to me, I am the Messenger of God. And he said in that state: I am the Prophet, there is no lie, I am the son of Abdul Muttalib. And with him stood close to a hundred of his companions, and some said eighty, among them were Abu Bakr and Umar, may God be pleased with them, and Al-Abbas and Ali and Al-Fadl ibn Abbas and Abu Sufyan ibn Al-Harith and Ayman ibn Umm Ayman and Usama ibn Zaid and others, may God be pleased with them. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered his uncle Al-Abbas, who had a loud voice, to call out at the top of his voice, O companions of the tree, meaning the tree of the Pledge of Ridwan under which the Muslims, the Muhajireen and Ansar, pledged allegiance to him that they would not flee from him, so he began to call out to them, O companions of the tree, meaning the tree of the Pledge of Ridwan under which the Muslims, the Muhajireen and Ansar, pledged allegiance to him that they would not flee from him. So he began to call out to them, O companions of the tree. Al-Samra, and he would say sometimes, O people of Surat Al-Baqarah, so they would say, Ya Labbayk, Ya Labbayk, and the people would turn and retreat to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, until if a man among them did not obey his camel to return, he would put on his armor, then get off it, send it, and return himself to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. When a group of them gathered at the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he ordered them to believe the attack and took a handful of dirt after he called upon his Lord and sought His help, and said, O God, fulfill for me what You promised me, then he threw it at the people and not a single person among them remained except that it struck him in his eye and mouth, distracting him from fighting. Then they were defeated and the Muslims followed their backs, killing and taking captives. The rest of the people did not retreat except that the captives were lying in the hands of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Imam Ahmad said: Affan told us, Hammad bin Salamah told us, Ya`la bin Ata` told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Yasar, on the authority of Abu Hammam, on the authority of Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Fahri, whose name is Yazid bin Asid, and it is said Yazid bin Anis, and it is said Karz, who said: I was with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the Battle of Hunayn. We set out on a very hot day, and we camped under the shade of the trees. When the sun had set, I put on my cloak and mounted my horse, and I went to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was in his tent. I said: Peace be upon you, O Messenger of God, and the mercy and blessings of God. Is it time to go back? He said: Yes. He said: O Bilal. So he rose from under a tamarisk tree whose shadow was like the shadow of a bird and said: At your service and your pleasure, I am your ransom. He said: Saddle my horse for me. So he brought out a saddle with two ribs made of palm fibers, in which there was neither arrogance nor pride. He said: So he saddled it and mounted it, and we mounted, and we fought them in the evening and the night. The two horses gloated, and the Muslims turned back in flight, just as God Almighty said: Then you turned back in flight. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O servants of God, I am the servant of God and His Messenger. Then he said: O company of the emigrants, I am the servant of God and His Messenger. He said: Then he jumped off his horse and took a handful of dirt. The one who was closest to him told me that he struck their faces with it and said: May your faces be disgraced. So God Almighty defeated them. Ya`la ibn `Ata` said: Their sons told me on the authority of their fathers that they said: There was not one of us left whose eyes and mouth were not filled with dust, and we heard a clang between the sky and the earth like the passing of iron over a new basin. This is how Al-Hafiz Al-Bayhaqi narrated it in Dalil Al-Nubuwwah from the hadith of Abu Dawud Al-Tayalisi on the authority of Hammad ibn Salamah. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Asim ibn `Umar ibn Qatada told me on the authority of `Abd Al-Rahman ibn Jabir on the authority of his father Jabir ibn `Abdullah who said: Malik ibn `Auf and those with him went out to Hunayn, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, reached him before them. They prepared and got ready in the narrows and bends of the valley, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions advanced until they descended into the valley in the blindness of dawn. When the people descended, the horses rushed at them and charged at them, and the people retreated in defeat, no one facing anyone else. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took a side to the right, saying: “O people, come to me. I am the Messenger of God, I am the Messenger of God, I am Muhammad ibn `Abdullah.” Nothing happened, and I rode. The camels were fighting each other. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw the people’s situation, he said: O Abbas, shout, O group of Ansar, O people of the samura. They replied, At your service, at your service. So a man went to turn his camel, but he was unable to do so, so he threw his armor around his neck, took his sword and bow, and followed the voice until a hundred of them gathered around the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The people reviewed and fought. The call was first made by the Ansar, then it was made last by the Khazraj. They were patient in the war. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, looked out in his mount and looked at the people fighting and said: Now the battle has heated up. He said: By God, the people did not return to him until the prisoners were lying with the Messenger of God. God killed those of them who were killed, and those of them who were defeated fled, and God gave their wealth and children to His Messenger. In the two Sahihs, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Bara’ bin Azib, may God be pleased with them both, that a man said to him: O Abu Ammarah, did you flee from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of Hunayn? He said: But the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not flee. Hawazin were a people of archers. When we met them and attacked them, they were defeated. The people turned to the spoils, but they met us with arrows, so the people were defeated. I saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith holding the reins of his white mule, and he was saying: “I am the Prophet, no lie. I am the son of Abdul Muttalib.” I said: This is the ultimate example of complete bravery. On a day like this, in the midst of battle, his army had fled from him, and he was on a mule that was not fast-running and was not suitable for fleeing, attacking, or escaping. He was also making it run towards them and mentioning his name so that those who did not know him would recognize him. May God’s prayers and peace be upon him forever until the Day of Judgment. All of this is nothing but trust in God and reliance on Him, and knowledge from Him that He will grant him victory and complete what He sent him with and make His religion prevail over all other religions. For this reason, God the Almighty said: Then God sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger, meaning His reassurance and steadfastness with His Messenger, and upon the believers, meaning those with him, and sent down… Soldiers you have not seen” and they are the angels as Imam Abu Jaafar Ibn Jarir said: Al-Hasan Ibn Arafa told me, Al-Mu’tamir Ibn Sulayman told me, on the authority of Awf, who is Ibn Abi Jamila Al-A’rabi, who said: I heard Abd Al-Rahman, the freed slave of Ibn Barthan, tell me that a man who was with the polytheists on the day of Hunayn said: When we and the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, met on the day of Hunayn, they did not stand up to milk a sheep for us. He said: So when we defeated them, we began to drive them in their footsteps until we reached the owner of the white mule, and it was the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: Then white men with handsome faces met us, and they said to us, O you with ugly faces, go back. He said: So we fled and they rode on our shoulders, and that was it. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bayhaqi said: Abu Abdullah Al-Hafiz informed us, Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Baluyeh told us, Ishaq bin Al-Hasan Al-Harbi told us, Affan bin Muslim told us, Abdul Wahid bin Ziyad told us, Al-Harith bin Hasira told us, Al-Qasim bin Abdul Rahman told us, on the authority of his father, who said: Ibn Masoud, may God be pleased with him, said: I was with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of Hunayn, and the people turned away from him, and I remained with him with eighty men from the Muhajireen and Ansar. We advanced and did not turn our backs on them, and they are the ones upon whom God sent down tranquility. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was on his white mule, moving forward, and his mule swerved, so he leaned away from the saddle, so I said: May God raise you up. He said: Give me a handful of dirt. So I gave it to him. He said: So he struck their faces with it, and their eyes were filled with dirt. He said: Where are the Muhajireen and Ansar? I said: They are there. He said: Call them. So I called them and they came with their swords in their right hands like meteors, and the polytheists turned their backs. Imam Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad on the authority of Affan with a similar wording. Al-Walid bin Muslim said: Abdullah bin Al-Mubarak told me on the authority of Abu Bakr Al-Hudhali on the authority of Ikrimah, the freed slave of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of Shaibah bin Othman, who said: When I saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, naked on the day of Hunayn, I remembered my father and my uncle and the killing of Ali and Hamza, so I said: Today I will take my revenge on him. He said: So I went to approach him from his right, and there I saw Al-Abbas bin Abdul Muttalib standing, wearing a white armor like silver, revealing the dust. I said: His uncle, and he will not let him down. I went to him from his left, and there I saw Abu Sufyan bin Al-Harith bin Abdul Muttalib. I said: His cousin, and he will not let him down. I approached him from behind, and there was nothing left but to surround him with a sword, when a flame of fire was raised between me and him like lightning. I feared that it would crush me, so I put it down. I covered my eyes with my hand and walked backwards. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, turned and said: “O Shaiba, O Shaiba, come closer to me. O God, remove Satan from him.” He said: So I raised my eyes to him, but his distraction was more beloved to me than my hearing and my sight. Then he said: O Shaiba, fight the infidels. Al-Bayhaqi narrated it from the hadith of Al-Walid, and he mentioned it. Then it was narrated from the hadith of Ayoub bin Jabir on the authority of Sadaqah bin Saeed on the authority of Mus`ab bin Shaibah on the authority of his father who said: I went out with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of Hunayn. By God, I did not go out because of Islam or knowledge of it, but I refused that Hawazin should prevail over Quraysh. So I said while I was standing with him: O Messenger of God, I see piebald horses. He said: O Shaibah, none sees them except an infidel. So he struck my chest with his hand and then said: O God, guide Shaibah. Then he struck it a second time and then said: O God, guide Shaibah. Then he struck it a third time and then said: O God, guide Shaibah. He said: By God, he did not lift his hand from my chest on the third day until no one among God’s creation was more beloved to me than him. He mentioned the rest of the hadith about the people meeting and the Muslims being defeated and the call of al-`Abbas and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, seeking help until God Almighty defeated the polytheists. Muhammad bin Ishaq said: My father, Ishaq bin Yasar, told me on the authority of someone who told him on the authority of Jubayr bin Mut`im, may God be pleased with him, who said: We were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of Hunayn and the people were fighting. When I looked at something like black carpets falling from the sky until they fell between us and the people, then there were scattered ants filling the valley. It was nothing but the defeat of the people, so we had no doubt that they were the angels. Saeed bin Al-Sa’ib bin Yasar said on the authority of his father: I heard Yazid bin Aamer Al-Suwai’i, who had witnessed Hunayn with the polytheists and then converted to Islam. We used to ask him about the terror that God had cast into the hearts of the polytheists on the day of Hunayn. He would take a pebble and throw it into a basin and it would buzz, saying: We used to find something like this in our hearts. A witness for it has been presented from the hadith of Yazid bin Abi Asid, and God knows best. In Sahih Muslim on the authority of Muhammad bin Rafi’ on the authority of Abd Al-Razzaq, Ma’mar informed us on the authority of Hammam, who said: This is what Abu Hurairah told us that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I was aided by terror and was given concise speech. For this reason God, the Most High, said: “Then God sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers, and sent down soldiers you did not see, and punished those who disbelieved. That is the recompense of the disbelievers.” And His statement: Then after that God will turn in mercy to whom He wills, and God is Forgiving. Rahim: God had forgiven the rest of Hawazin, so they converted to Islam and came to him as Muslims and caught up with him. He approached Mecca at Al-Juhfah, which was about twenty days after the battle. At that time, he gave them the choice between their captives and their wealth, and they chose their captives. They were six thousand captives, including boys and women. He returned them to them and divided the wealth among the conquerors, and gave some of the freedmen as a gift so that their hearts would be reconciled to Islam. He gave them one hundred camels, and among those who gave one hundred was Malik bin Auf Al-Nasri, who was appointed over his people as he had been. He praised him in his poem in which he says: I have never seen or heard of anyone like him among all the people like Muhammad He is loyal and gives to the generous when he is generous, and whenever you want, he tells you what will happen tomorrow. And if the battalion bares its fangs with the sword and strikes every warrior As if he were a lion among his cubs, asleep in the middle of the desert, in an observation post.
9:26: Ibn Jurayj said on the authority of Mujahid: This is the first verse revealed from Bara'ah, in which God Almighty mentions to the believers His favor upon them and His kindness to them in His victory for them in many of their battles with His Messenger, and that this is from Him Almighty and with His support and decree, not by their number or their number. He alerted them that victory is from Him, whether the group is small or large. On the day of Hunayn, their large number pleased them, but despite this, it did not benefit them at all, so they turned their backs, except for a few of them with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then He revealed His victory and support upon His Messenger and the believers who were with him, as we will explain in detail, God willing, to teach them that victory is from Him alone and with His support, even if the group is small. How many a small group has overcome a large group by God’s permission? And God is with the patient. Imam Ahmad said: Wahb ibn Jarir told us, my father told us, I heard Yunus narrating on the authority of Al-Zuhri on the authority of Ubaydullah on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The best of the Companions are four, the best of the raiding parties are four hundred, and the best of the armies are four thousand, and twelve thousand will not be defeated due to their small number.” This is how Abu Dawud and Al-Tirmidhi narrated it. Then he said: This is a very strange hasan hadith that no one has a chain of transmission for except Jarir ibn Hazim. Rather, it was narrated on the authority of Al-Zuhri on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, as a mursal. Ibn Majah, Al-Bayhaqi and others narrated it on the authority of Aktham Al-Jawni on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a similar manner, and God knows best. The Battle of Hunayn took place after the conquest of Mecca in Shawwal of the year eight of the Hijra. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had finished the conquest of Mecca and its affairs were prepared and most of its people had converted to Islam and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had released them, he was informed that Hawazin had gathered to fight him and that their leader was Malik ibn Auf ibn al-Nadr, and with him were Thaqeef in its entirety and Banu Jashm and Banu Saad ibn Bakr and Awza’ of Banu Hilal who were few in number and some of Banu Amr ibn Amir and Auf ibn Amir who had come with women and children and sheep and came with them all and all of them. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out to them with his army that had come with him for the conquest and it was ten thousand of the Muhajireen and Ansar and the tribes of the Arabs and with him were those who had converted from the people of Mecca who were the freed ones in two thousand. So he marched with them to the enemy and they met in a valley between Mecca and Taif called Hunayn and the battle took place there at the beginning of the day in the darkness of dawn. They descended into the valley and Hawazin had ambushed them. When they faced each other, the Muslims did not notice except that they had revolted against them and pelted them with arrows and drew their swords and charged as one man as their king had ordered them. Then the Muslims turned back, as God the Almighty said, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood firm while he was riding his gray mule that day, leading it towards the enemy, and his uncle Al-Abbas was holding its right stirrup, and Abu Sufyan ibn Al-Harith ibn Abdul Muttalib was holding its left stirrup, weighing it down so that it would not go too fast, and he was mentioning his name, may God bless him and grant him peace, and calling the Muslims to return and saying: To me, servants of God, to me, I am the Messenger of God. And he said in that state: I am the Prophet, there is no lie, I am the son of Abdul Muttalib. And with him stood close to a hundred of his companions, and some said eighty, among them were Abu Bakr and Umar, may God be pleased with them, and Al-Abbas and Ali and Al-Fadl ibn Abbas and Abu Sufyan ibn Al-Harith and Ayman ibn Umm Ayman and Usama ibn Zaid and others, may God be pleased with them. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered his uncle Al-Abbas, who had a loud voice, to call out at the top of his voice, O companions of the tree, meaning the tree of the Pledge of Ridwan under which the Muslims, the Muhajireen and Ansar, pledged allegiance to him that they would not flee from him, so he began to call out to them, O companions of the tree, meaning the tree of the Pledge of Ridwan under which the Muslims, the Muhajireen and Ansar, pledged allegiance to him that they would not flee from him. So he began to call out to them, O companions of the tree. Al-Samra, and he would say sometimes, O people of Surat Al-Baqarah, so they would say, Ya Labbayk, Ya Labbayk, and the people would turn and retreat to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, until if a man among them did not obey his camel to return, he would put on his armor, then get off it, send it, and return himself to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. When a group of them gathered at the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he ordered them to believe the attack and took a handful of dirt after he called upon his Lord and sought His help, and said, O God, fulfill for me what You promised me, then he threw it at the people and not a single person among them remained except that it struck him in his eye and mouth, distracting him from fighting. Then they were defeated and the Muslims followed their backs, killing and taking captives. The rest of the people did not retreat except that the captives were lying in the hands of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Imam Ahmad said: Affan told us, Hammad bin Salamah told us, Ya`la bin Ata` told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Yasar, on the authority of Abu Hammam, on the authority of Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Fahri, whose name is Yazid bin Asid, and it is said Yazid bin Anis, and it is said Karz, who said: I was with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the Battle of Hunayn. We set out on a very hot day, and we camped under the shade of the trees. When the sun had set, I put on my cloak and mounted my horse, and I went to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was in his tent. I said: Peace be upon you, O Messenger of God, and the mercy and blessings of God. Is it time to go back? He said: Yes. He said: O Bilal. So he rose from under a tamarisk tree whose shadow was like the shadow of a bird and said: At your service and your pleasure, I am your ransom. He said: Saddle my horse for me. So he brought out a saddle with two ribs made of palm fibers, in which there was neither arrogance nor pride. He said: So he saddled it and mounted it, and we mounted, and we fought them in the evening and the night. The two horses gloated, and the Muslims turned back in flight, just as God Almighty said: Then you turned back in flight. Then he said: O company of the emigrants, I am the servant of God and His Messenger. He said: Then he jumped off his horse and took a handful of dirt. They were six thousand captives, including boys and women. He returned them to them and divided the wealth among the conquerors, and gave some of the freedmen as a gift so that their hearts would be reconciled to Islam. He gave them one hundred camels, and among those who gave one hundred was Malik bin Auf Al-Nasri, who was appointed over his people as he had been. He praised him in his poem in which he says: I have never seen or heard of anyone like him among all the people like Muhammad He is loyal and gives to the generous when he is generous, and whenever you want, he tells you what will happen tomorrow. And if the battalion bares its fangs with the sword and strikes every warrior As if he were a lion among his cubs, asleep in the middle of the desert, in an observation post.
9:27: Ibn Jurayj said on the authority of Mujahid: This is the first verse revealed from Bara'ah, in which God Almighty mentions to the believers His favor upon them and His kindness to them in His victory for them in many of their battles with His Messenger, and that this is from Him Almighty and with His support and decree, not by their number or their number. He alerted them that victory is from Him, whether the group is small or large. On the day of Hunayn, their large number pleased them, but despite this, it did not benefit them at all, so they turned their backs, except for a few of them with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then He revealed His victory and support upon His Messenger and the believers who were with him, as we will explain in detail, God willing, to teach them that victory is from Him alone and with His support, even if the group is small. How many a small group has overcome a large group by God’s permission? And God is with the patient. Imam Ahmad said: Wahb ibn Jarir told us, my father told us, I heard Yunus narrating on the authority of Al-Zuhri on the authority of Ubaydullah on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The best of the Companions are four, the best of the raiding parties are four hundred, and the best of the armies are four thousand, and twelve thousand will not be defeated due to their small number.” This is how Abu Dawud and Al-Tirmidhi narrated it. Then he said: This is a very strange hasan hadith that no one has a chain of transmission for except Jarir ibn Hazim. Rather, it was narrated on the authority of Al-Zuhri on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, as a mursal. Ibn Majah, Al-Bayhaqi and others narrated it on the authority of Aktham Al-Jawni on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a similar manner, and God knows best. The Battle of Hunayn took place after the conquest of Mecca in Shawwal of the year eight of the Hijra. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had finished the conquest of Mecca and its affairs were prepared and most of its people had converted to Islam and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had released them, he was informed that Hawazin had gathered to fight him and that their leader was Malik ibn Auf ibn al-Nadr, and with him were Thaqeef in its entirety and Banu Jashm and Banu Saad ibn Bakr and Awza’ of Banu Hilal who were few in number and some of Banu Amr ibn Amir and Auf ibn Amir who had come with women and children and sheep and came with them all and all of them. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out to them with his army that had come with him for the conquest and it was ten thousand of the Muhajireen and Ansar and the tribes of the Arabs and with him were those who had converted from the people of Mecca who were the freed ones in two thousand. So he marched with them to the enemy and they met in a valley between Mecca and Taif called Hunayn and the battle took place there at the beginning of the day in the darkness of dawn. They descended into the valley and Hawazin had ambushed them. When they faced each other, the Muslims did not notice except that they had revolted against them and pelted them with arrows and drew their swords and charged as one man as their king had ordered them. Then the Muslims turned back, as God the Almighty said, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood firm while he was riding his gray mule that day, leading it towards the enemy, and his uncle Al-Abbas was holding its right stirrup, and Abu Sufyan ibn Al-Harith ibn Abdul Muttalib was holding its left stirrup, weighing it down so that it would not go too fast, and he was mentioning his name, may God bless him and grant him peace, and calling the Muslims to return and saying: To me, servants of God, to me, I am the Messenger of God. And he said in that state: I am the Prophet, there is no lie, I am the son of Abdul Muttalib. And with him stood close to a hundred of his companions, and some said eighty, among them were Abu Bakr and Umar, may God be pleased with them, and Al-Abbas and Ali and Al-Fadl ibn Abbas and Abu Sufyan ibn Al-Harith and Ayman ibn Umm Ayman and Usama ibn Zaid and others, may God be pleased with them. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered his uncle Al-Abbas, who had a loud voice, to call out at the top of his voice, O companions of the tree, meaning the tree of the Pledge of Ridwan under which the Muslims, the Muhajireen and Ansar, pledged allegiance to him that they would not flee from him, so he began to call out to them, O companions of the tree, meaning the tree of the Pledge of Ridwan under which the Muslims, the Muhajireen and Ansar, pledged allegiance to him that they would not flee from him. So he began to call out to them, O companions of the tree. Al-Samra, and he would say sometimes, O people of Surat Al-Baqarah, so they would say, Ya Labbayk, Ya Labbayk, and the people would turn and retreat to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, until if a man among them did not obey his camel to return, he would put on his armor, then get off it, send it, and return himself to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. When a group of them gathered at the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he ordered them to believe the attack and took a handful of dirt after he called upon his Lord and sought His help, and said, O God, fulfill for me what You promised me, then he threw it at the people and not a single person among them remained except that it struck him in his eye and mouth, distracting him from fighting. Then they were defeated and the Muslims followed their backs, killing and taking captives. The rest of the people did not retreat except that the captives were lying in the hands of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Imam Ahmad said: Affan told us, Hammad bin Salamah told us, Ya`la bin Ata` told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Yasar, on the authority of Abu Hammam, on the authority of Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Fahri, whose name is Yazid bin Asid, and it is said Yazid bin Anis, and it is said Karz, who said: I was with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the Battle of Hunayn. We set out on a very hot day, and we camped under the shade of the trees. When the sun had set, I put on my cloak and mounted my horse, and I went to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was in his tent. I said: Peace be upon you, O Messenger of God, and the mercy and blessings of God. Is it time to go back? He said: Yes. He said: O Bilal. So he rose from under a tamarisk tree whose shadow was like the shadow of a bird and said: At your service and your pleasure, I am your ransom. He said: Saddle my horse for me. So he brought out a saddle with two ribs made of palm fibers, in which there was neither arrogance nor pride. He said: So he saddled it and mounted it, and we mounted, and we fought them in the evening and the night. The two horses gloated, and the Muslims turned back in flight, just as God Almighty said: Then you turned back in flight. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O servants of God, I am the servant of God and His Messenger. Then he said: O company of the emigrants, I am the servant of God and His Messenger. He said: Then he jumped off his horse and took a handful of dirt. The one who was closest to him told me that he struck their faces with it and said: May your faces be disgraced. So God Almighty defeated them. Ya`la ibn `Ata` said: Their sons told me on the authority of their fathers that they said: There was not one of us left whose eyes and mouth were not filled with dust, and we heard a clang between the sky and the earth like the passing of iron over a new basin. This is how Al-Hafiz Al-Bayhaqi narrated it in Dalil Al-Nubuwwah from the hadith of Abu Dawud Al-Tayalisi on the authority of Hammad ibn Salamah. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Asim ibn `Umar ibn Qatada told me on the authority of `Abd Al-Rahman ibn Jabir on the authority of his father Jabir ibn `Abdullah who said: Malik ibn `Auf and those with him went out to Hunayn, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, reached him before them. They prepared and got ready in the narrows and bends of the valley, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions advanced until they descended into the valley in the blindness of dawn. When the people descended, the horses rushed at them and charged at them, and the people retreated in defeat, no one facing anyone else. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took a side to the right, saying: “O people, come to me. I am the Messenger of God, I am the Messenger of God, I am Muhammad ibn `Abdullah.” Nothing happened, and I rode. The camels were fighting each other. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw the people’s situation, he said: O Abbas, shout, O group of Ansar, O people of the samura. They replied, At your service, at your service. So a man went to turn his camel, but he was unable to do so, so he threw his armor around his neck, took his sword and bow, and followed the voice until a hundred of them gathered around the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The people reviewed and fought. The call was first made by the Ansar, then it was made last by the Khazraj. They were patient in the war. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, looked out in his mount and looked at the people fighting and said: Now the battle has heated up. He said: By God, the people did not return to him until the prisoners were lying with the Messenger of God. God killed those of them who were killed, and those of them who were defeated fled, and God gave their wealth and children to His Messenger. In the two Sahihs, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Bara’ bin Azib, may God be pleased with them both, that a man said to him: O Abu Ammarah, did you flee from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of Hunayn? He said: But the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not flee. Hawazin were a people of archers. When we met them and attacked them, they were defeated. The people turned to the spoils, but they met us with arrows, so the people were defeated. I saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith holding the reins of his white mule, and he was saying: “I am the Prophet, no lie. I am the son of Abdul Muttalib.” I said: This is the ultimate example of complete bravery. On a day like this, in the midst of battle, his army had fled from him, and he was on a mule that was not fast-running and was not suitable for fleeing, attacking, or escaping. He was also making it run towards them and mentioning his name so that those who did not know him would recognize him. May God’s prayers and peace be upon him forever until the Day of Judgment. All of this is nothing but trust in God and reliance on Him, and knowledge from Him that He will grant him victory and complete what He sent him with and make His religion prevail over all other religions. For this reason, God the Almighty said: Then God sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger, meaning His reassurance and steadfastness with His Messenger, and upon the believers, meaning those with him, and sent down… Soldiers you have not seen” and they are the angels as Imam Abu Jaafar Ibn Jarir said: Al-Hasan Ibn Arafa told me, Al-Mu’tamir Ibn Sulayman told me, on the authority of Awf, who is Ibn Abi Jamila Al-A’rabi, who said: I heard Abd Al-Rahman, the freed slave of Ibn Barthan, tell me that a man who was with the polytheists on the day of Hunayn said: When we and the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, met on the day of Hunayn, they did not stand up to milk a sheep for us. He said: So when we defeated them, we began to drive them in their footsteps until we reached the owner of the white mule, and it was the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: Then white men with handsome faces met us, and they said to us, O you with ugly faces, go back. He said: So we fled and they rode on our shoulders, and that was it. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bayhaqi said: Abu Abdullah Al-Hafiz informed us, Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Baluyeh told us, Ishaq bin Al-Hasan Al-Harbi told us, Affan bin Muslim told us, Abdul Wahid bin Ziyad told us, Al-Harith bin Hasira told us, Al-Qasim bin Abdul Rahman told us, on the authority of his father, who said: Ibn Masoud, may God be pleased with him, said: I was with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of Hunayn, and the people turned away from him, and I remained with him with eighty men from the Muhajireen and Ansar. We advanced and did not turn our backs on them, and they are the ones upon whom God sent down tranquility. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was on his white mule, moving forward, and his mule swerved, so he leaned away from the saddle, so I said: May God raise you up. He said: Give me a handful of dirt. So I gave it to him. He said: So he struck their faces with it, and their eyes were filled with dirt. He said: Where are the Muhajireen and Ansar? I said: They are there. He said: Call them. So I called them and they came with their swords in their right hands like meteors, and the polytheists turned their backs. Imam Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad on the authority of Affan with a similar wording. Al-Walid bin Muslim said: Abdullah bin Al-Mubarak told me on the authority of Abu Bakr Al-Hudhali on the authority of Ikrimah, the freed slave of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of Shaibah bin Othman, who said: When I saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, naked on the day of Hunayn, I remembered my father and my uncle and the killing of Ali and Hamza, so I said: Today I will take my revenge on him. He said: So I went to approach him from his right, and there I saw Al-Abbas bin Abdul Muttalib standing, wearing a white armor like silver, revealing the dust. I said: His uncle, and he will not let him down. I went to him from his left, and there I saw Abu Sufyan bin Al-Harith bin Abdul Muttalib. I said: His cousin, and he will not let him down. I approached him from behind, and there was nothing left but to surround him with a sword, when a flame of fire was raised between me and him like lightning. I feared that it would crush me, so I put it down. I covered my eyes with my hand and walked backwards. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, turned and said: “O Shaiba, O Shaiba, come closer to me. O God, remove Satan from him.” He said: So I raised my eyes to him, but his distraction was more beloved to me than my hearing and my sight. Then he said: O Shaiba, fight the infidels. Al-Bayhaqi narrated it from the hadith of Al-Walid, and he mentioned it. Then it was narrated from the hadith of Ayoub bin Jabir on the authority of Sadaqah bin Saeed on the authority of Mus`ab bin Shaibah on the authority of his father who said: I went out with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of Hunayn. By God, I did not go out because of Islam or knowledge of it, but I refused that Hawazin should prevail over Quraysh. So I said while I was standing with him: O Messenger of God, I see piebald horses. He said: O Shaibah, none sees them except an infidel. So he struck my chest with his hand and then said: O God, guide Shaibah. Then he struck it a second time and then said: O God, guide Shaibah. Then he struck it a third time and then said: O God, guide Shaibah. He said: By God, he did not lift his hand from my chest on the third day until no one among God’s creation was more beloved to me than him. He mentioned the rest of the hadith about the people meeting and the Muslims being defeated and the call of al-`Abbas and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, seeking help until God Almighty defeated the polytheists. Muhammad bin Ishaq said: My father, Ishaq bin Yasar, told me on the authority of someone who told him on the authority of Jubayr bin Mut`im, may God be pleased with him, who said: We were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of Hunayn and the people were fighting. When I looked at something like black carpets falling from the sky until they fell between us and the people, then there were scattered ants filling the valley. It was nothing but the defeat of the people, so we had no doubt that they were the angels. Saeed bin Al-Sa’ib bin Yasar said on the authority of his father: I heard Yazid bin Aamer Al-Suwai’i, who had witnessed Hunayn with the polytheists and then converted to Islam. We used to ask him about the terror that God had cast into the hearts of the polytheists on the day of Hunayn. He would take a pebble and throw it into a basin and it would buzz, saying: We used to find something like this in our hearts. A witness for it has been presented from the hadith of Yazid bin Abi Asid, and God knows best. In Sahih Muslim on the authority of Muhammad bin Rafi’ on the authority of Abd Al-Razzaq, Ma’mar informed us on the authority of Hammam, who said: This is what Abu Hurairah told us that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I was aided by terror and was given concise speech. For this reason God, the Most High, said: “Then God sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers, and sent down soldiers you did not see, and punished those who disbelieved. That is the recompense of the disbelievers.” And His statement: Then after that God will turn in mercy to whom He wills, and God is Forgiving. Rahim: God had forgiven the rest of Hawazin, so they converted to Islam and came to him as Muslims and caught up with him. He approached Mecca at Al-Juhfah, which was about twenty days after the battle. At that time, he gave them the choice between their captives and their wealth, and they chose their captives. They were six thousand captives, including boys and women. He returned them to them and divided the wealth among the conquerors, and gave some of the freedmen as a gift so that their hearts would be reconciled to Islam. He gave them one hundred camels, and among those who gave one hundred was Malik bin Auf Al-Nasri, who was appointed over his people as he had been. He praised him in his poem in which he says: I have never seen or heard of anyone like him among all the people like Muhammad He is loyal and gives to the generous when he is generous, and whenever you want, he tells you what will happen tomorrow. And if the battalion bares its fangs with the sword and strikes every warrior As if he were a lion among his cubs, asleep in the middle of the desert, in an observation post.
9:29: God the Almighty commanded His believing servants who are pure in religion and in person to banish the polytheists who are impure in religion from the Sacred Mosque and not to approach it after the revelation of this verse. It was revealed in the year nine, and for this reason the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) sent Ali with Abu Bakr may God be pleased with them both that year and commanded him to announce to the polytheists that no polytheist should perform Hajj after this year and no one should circumambulate the House naked. So God completed that and decreed it by law and destiny. Abdul Razzaq said: Ibn Jurayj told us, Abu al-Zubayr told me that he heard Jabir ibn Abdullah say about the words of God the Almighty: The polytheists are impure, so let them not approach the Sacred Mosque after this year of theirs unless he is a slave or one of the People of the Covenant. It was narrated from another chain of transmission, and Imam Ahmad said: Hussain told us, Sharik told us, from Al-Ash'ath, meaning Ibn Suwar, from Al-Hasan, from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: No polytheist will enter our mosque after this year of ours except the people of the covenant and their servants. Imam Ahmad alone transmitted it from the Prophet, and the Mawquf narration is more authentic in its chain of transmission. Imam Abu Amr Al-Awza'i said: Umar ibn Abdul Aziz, may God be pleased with him, wrote to prevent the Jews and Christians from entering the mosques of the Muslims, and he followed his prohibition with the words of God, the Most High: The polytheists are unclean. Ata' said: The entire Haram is a mosque, because God, the Most High, said: So let them not approach Al-Masjid Al-Haram after this year of theirs. This noble verse indicates the impurity of the polytheist, as mentioned in the Sahih: The believer does not become impure. As for the impurity of his body, the majority are of the view that he is not impure in body and soul, because God, the Most High, permitted the food of the People of the Book. Some of the Zahiris held that their bodies are impure. Ash'ath said from Al-Hasan: Whoever shakes hands with them should perform ablution. Narrated by Ibn Jarir. And His statement, And if you fear poverty, God will enrich you from His bounty, Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: This is because the people said that the markets will be cut off from us, trade will be destroyed, and the amenities we used to gain from them will be taken away from us. So God revealed, And if you fear poverty, God will enrich you from His bounty, from another source, If He wills, until His statement, while they are humbled, meaning this is in exchange for what you feared from the cutting off of those markets. So God compensated them for what He had cut off from the matter of polytheism by giving them from the necks of the People of the Book the jizya. And thus it was narrated from Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ikrimah, Saeed ibn Jubayr, Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak, and others: Indeed, God is Knowing, meaning what is good for you, Wise, meaning in what He commands and forbids, because He is perfect in His actions and words, just in His creation and command, blessed and exalted be He. For this reason, He compensated them for those earnings with the jizya money that they take from the People of the Covenant. And the Almighty said: “Fight those who do not believe in God or in the Last Day and do not consider unlawful what God and His Messenger have made unlawful and do not adopt the religion of truth from among those who were given the Scripture - until they pay the jizyah with willing submission while they are subdued.” In fact, when they disbelieved in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, they no longer had true faith in any of the messengers or in what they brought. Rather, they follow their opinions, their whims, and their fathers in what they are doing, not because it is the law of God and His religion. Because if they had true faith in what they had in their hands, it would have led them to believe in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, because all the prophets gave glad tidings of him and commanded them to follow him. But when he came and they disbelieved in him, and he is the most honorable of messengers, it was known that they were not adhering to the law of the earlier prophets because it is from God. Rather, it is their luck and their whims, so their belief in the rest of the prophets does not benefit them, and they disbelieved in their master, the best of them, the last of them, and the most perfect of them. That is why He said: “Fight those who do not believe in God or in the Last Day and do not consider unlawful what God and His Messenger have made unlawful and do not adopt the religion of truth from among those who were given the Scripture.” This noble verse is the first command to fight the People of the Book after the affairs of the polytheists were prepared and people entered the religion of God in droves and the Arabian Peninsula was set straight. God and His Messenger commanded to fight the People of the Book, the Jews and the Christians. That was in the year nine. That is why the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prepared to fight the Romans and called the people to that and showed it to them. He sent to the Arab tribes around Medina and urged them, so they prepared with him and about thirty thousand fighters gathered, and some people from the people of Medina and those around it from the hypocrites and others stayed behind. That was in a year of drought and a time of intense heat and scorching sun. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out intending to go to Syria to fight the Romans, so he reached Tabuk and settled there and stayed there for about twenty days. Then he sought God’s guidance in returning, so he returned. This is generally due to the straitened circumstances and the weakness of the people, as will be explained later, God willing. This noble verse has been used as evidence by those who believe that the jizya should only be taken from the People of the Book or those similar to them, such as the Magians, as is authentically reported in the hadith that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took it from the Magians of Hajar. This is the view of al-Shafi’i and Ahmad, according to the well-known view of Abu Hanifa, may God have mercy on him. Rather, it should be taken from all non-Arabs, whether they are People of the Book or polytheists, and it should not be taken from the Arabs except from the People of the Book. Imam Malik said: Rather, it is permissible to impose the jizya on all infidels, whether they are people of the Book, Zoroastrian, pagan, or others. The sources of these doctrines and the mention of their evidence are not mentioned in this place, and God knows best. And his saying: Until they pay the jizyah means if they do not submit by hand meaning by force and domination while they are humiliated meaning humiliated, despised and disgraced. Therefore, it is not permissible to honor the People of the Covenant or raise them above the Muslims. Rather, they are humiliated, despised and miserable, as came in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Do not initiate the greeting of peace with the Jews and Christians, and if you meet one of them on the road, force him to its narrowest part.” For this reason, the Commander of the Faithful, Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, imposed on them those well-known conditions in humiliating, belittling and degrading them. This is what the imams and preservers of hadith narrated from the narration of Abd al-Rahman ibn Ghanim al-Ash’ari, who said: I wrote to Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, when he made peace with the Christians of the people of Ash-Sham: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. This is a letter from Abdullah Umar, the Commander of the Faithful, from the Christians of such-and-such city. When you came to us, we asked you for safety for ourselves, our children, our wealth and the people of our religion, and we stipulated for you upon ourselves that we would not incite any evil in our city. Nor shall we have a monastery, church, cell, or monk’s cell around it, nor shall we renew what has been destroyed in it, nor shall we revive what was planned for the Muslims, nor shall we prevent any Muslim from entering our churches, day or night, nor shall we widen their doors for passersby and wayfarers, nor shall we provide food for any Muslim who passes by us for three days, nor shall we shelter a spy in our churches or homes, nor shall we conceal any deception from the Muslims, nor shall we teach our children the Qur’an, nor shall we display polytheism, nor call anyone to it, nor shall we prevent any of our relatives from entering Islam if they wish to do so, nor shall we respect the Muslims, nor shall we stand up for them from our gatherings if they wish to sit, nor shall we resemble them in any of their clothing, in a skullcap, turban, sandals, or parting of the hair, nor shall we speak their language, nor shall we adopt their nicknames, nor shall we ride saddles, nor gird ourselves with swords, nor shall we take any weapon, nor carry it with us, nor engrave our rings in Arabic, nor shall we sell alcohol, nor shall we cut the front of our heads, nor shall we adhere to our dress wherever we are, nor shall we tie our belts on our heads, nor shall we be afraid of the evil... Our midst and that we do not display the cross on our churches and that we do not display our crosses or our books in any of the roads or markets of the Muslims and that we do not ring our bells in our churches except lightly and that we do not raise our voices in reading in our churches in any of the presence of the Muslims and that we do not go out to the palm groves or the ba’oth and that we do not raise our voices with our dead and do not display fires with them in any of the roads or markets of the Muslims and that we do not live with them with our dead and that we do not take from the slaves what the arrows of the Muslims have been made upon and that we guide the Muslims and do not spy on them in their homes. He said: So when I brought the letter to Omar, he added to it and we do not strike any of the Muslims. We stipulated that for you on ourselves and the people of our religion and we accepted security on it. If we contradicted anything of what we stipulated for you and imposed on ourselves, then we have no covenant and what is permissible for you from us is permissible from the people of opposition and discord.
9:30: This is an enticement from God Almighty to the believers to fight the infidels from the Jews and Christians for their heinous statement and slander against God Almighty. As for the Jews, they said about Ezra: He is the son of God, God is far above that. Al-Suddi and others mentioned that the doubt that occurred to them in that regard was that when the Amalekites defeated the Children of Israel and killed their scholars and took their elders captive, Ezra remained weeping over the Children of Israel and the loss of their knowledge until his eyelids fell out. While he was one day passing by a cemetery, he saw a woman weeping at a grave and saying: Oh, my food and vineyards! He said to her: Woe to you, who fed you before this? She said: God. He said: Verily, God is Ever-Living and does not die. She said: O Ezra, who taught the scholars before the Children of Israel? He said: God. She said: Then why are you weeping over them? He knew that it was something that he had been admonished about. Then he was told to go to such-and-such a river, wash in it, and pray two rak’ahs there, for you will meet an old man there. Whatever he feeds you, eat it. So he went and did what he was told. Then the old man said to him: Open your mouth. So he opened his mouth and threw something in it like a huge coal three times. Then Ezra returned, and he was the most knowledgeable of people about the Torah, and said: O Children of Israel, I have come to you with the Torah. They said: O Ezra, you are not a liar. So he tied a pen to one of his fingers and wrote the Torah with his entire finger. When the people retreated from their enemy and the scholars returned, they were informed about Ezra, so they extracted the copies that they had deposited in the mountains and compared them with them. They found what he had brought to be correct. Some of their ignorant ones said: He only did this because he was the son of God. As for the Christians’ misguidance regarding Christ, it is clear. That is why God Almighty denied the two groups, saying: That is their statement with their mouths, meaning they have no basis for what they claim except their fabrications and inventions. They imitate, meaning they resemble the statement of those who disbelieved before, meaning the nations before them who went astray just as these people went astray. May God destroy them, Ibn Abbas said: May God curse them. How are they deluded? meaning how do they go astray from the truth when it is clear and turn to falsehood? And his saying: They have taken their rabbis and monks as lords besides God, and the Messiah, son of Mary. Imam Ahmad, Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Jarir narrated through various chains of transmission on the authority of Adi bin Hatim, may God be pleased with him, that when the call of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, reached him, he fled to Ash-Sham. He had become a Christian in the pre-Islamic era, and his sister and a group of his people were taken prisoner. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took his sister and gave her a gift, so she returned to her brother and encouraged him to convert to Islam and to come to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Adi came to Madinah and he was a chief among his people, Tayy, and his father Hatim Al-Ta’i was famous for his generosity. The people talked about his arrival, so he entered upon the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and around Adi’s neck was a silver cross, and he was reciting this verse: They have taken their rabbis and monks as lords besides God. He said: I said: They did not worship them. He said: Yes, they made lawful for them what was lawful and made lawful for them what was unlawful, so they followed them, and that is their worship of them. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O Adi, what do you say? Does it harm you if it is said, God is Greater? Do you know anything greater than God? What harm does it harm you if it is said, There is no god but God? Do you know any god other than God? Then he called him to Islam, so he became Muslim and bore witness to the truth. He said, I saw his face beaming with joy. Then he said, Indeed, the Jews have incurred wrath and the Christians are astray. This is what Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, Abdullah ibn Abbas, and others said in the interpretation of They have taken their rabbis and monks as lords besides God. They followed them in what they permitted and prohibited. Al-Suddi said, They sought advice from men and threw the Book of God behind their backs. For this reason, God the Almighty said, And they were commanded only to worship one God, meaning, the One who, if He forbids something, it is forbidden, and what He permits is permissible, and what He legislates is followed, and what He rules is implemented. “There is no god but Him. Glory be to Him above what they associate with Him,” meaning, He is exalted and sanctified and is free from partners, peers, helpers, opposites, and children. There is no god but Him and no lord but Him.

9:32: God the Almighty says: These infidels from the polytheists and the People of the Book want to extinguish the light of God that is, what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent with of guidance and the religion of truth, simply by their arguments and fabrications. Their example in this is like someone who wants to extinguish the sun's rays or the light of the moon by blowing on it, and there is no way to do this. Likewise, what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent with must be completed and made apparent. For this reason, God the Almighty said, in response to what they sought and wanted: But God refuses except to perfect His light, although the disbelievers dislike it. The disbeliever is the one who conceals and covers something, and from this the night is called a disbeliever because it conceals things, and the farmer is called a disbeliever because he covers the seed in the ground, as He said: The disbelievers marvel at its growth. Then God the Almighty said: It is He who has sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth. Guidance is what he brought of true report, correct faith, and beneficial knowledge, and the religion of truth is the righteous, correct deeds that are beneficial in this world and the hereafter. To make it prevail over all religions, meaning over all other religions, as is proven in the Sahih on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: God has folded the earth for me, its easts and its wests, and the kingdom of my nation will reach what He folded for me of it. Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Ya`qub, I heard Shaqiq ibn Hayyan narrating on the authority of Mas`ud ibn Qubaysah or Qubaysah ibn Mas`ud saying: This tribe of Muharrib prayed the dawn prayer, and when they had prayed, a young man from among them said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: The easts and wests of the earth will be opened to you, and its workers will be in the Fire, except for those who fear God and fulfill their trust. Imam Ahmad said: Abu al-Mughira told us, Safwan told us, Salim ibn `Amir told us, on the authority of Tamim al-Dari, may God be pleased with him, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “This matter will reach as far as the night and day reach, and God will not leave a house of mud or hair except that He will make this religion enter it, honoring the honorable and humiliating the humiliated, honor by which God honors Islam and humiliation by which God humiliates.” Disbelief.” So Tamim al-Dari used to say: “I have known that, my family. Those of them who converted to Islam were granted goodness, honor, and glory, while those of them who were disbelievers were granted humiliation, degradation, and tribute.” Imam Ahmad said: Yazid bin Abd Rabbah told us, Al-Walid bin Muslim told us, Ibn Jabir told me, I heard Salim bin Aamer say, I heard Al-Miqdad bin Al-Aswad say, I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say, “There will not remain on the face of the earth a house of mud or hair except that the word of Islam will enter it, honoring the honorable and humiliating the humiliated. Either God will honor them and make them among its people, or He will humiliate them and they will submit to it.” Also in Al-Musnad, Muhammad bin Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Ibn Awn, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, on the authority of Abu Hudhayfah, on the authority of Uday bin Hatim, who heard him say, “I entered upon the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said, ‘O Uday, convert to Islam and you will be safe.’ I said, ‘I am of the people of religion.’ He said, ‘I know more about your religion than you.’ I said, ‘Do you know more about my religion than I?’” He said: Yes, aren't you from the Rukousiyyah and you eat the food of your people? I said: Yes! He said: This is not permissible for you in your religion. He said: He did not say it again, so I humbled myself to it. He said: "As for me, I know what prevents you from Islam. You say that only the weak and the powerless follow it, and the Arabs have attacked them. Do you know Al-Hirah?" I said: I have not seen it, but I have heard of it. He said: "By the One in Whose hand is my soul, God will complete this matter until a woman travels from Al-Hirah and circumambulates the House without being protected by anyone, and the treasures of Kisra bin Hurmuz will be opened." I said: Kisra bin Hurmuz? He said: Yes, Kisra bin Hurmuz, and money will be spent until no one will accept it. Adi bin Hatim said: This woman travels from Al-Hirah and circumambulates the House without being protected by anyone. I was among those who opened the treasures of Kisra bin Hurmuz. By the One in Whose hand is my soul, it will be the third time because the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said it. Muslim said: Abu Ma'n Zaid bin Yazid al-Raqashi told us, Khalid bin al-Harith told us, Abdul Hamid bin Ja'far told us, on the authority of al-Aswad bin al-Ala', on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Night and day will not pass until al-Lat and al-'Uzza are worshipped. So I said: O Messenger of God, I used to think when God Almighty revealed the verse, It is He who has sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, that that would be complete. He said: "Indeed, there will be of that what God Almighty wills, then God will send a good wind and take the souls of everyone in whose heart there was the weight of a mustard seed of faith, and there will remain those in whom there is no good, and they will return to the religion of their fathers."
