9:34: Al-Suddi said: The rabbis are from the Jews and the monks are from the Christians, and it is as he said, for the rabbis are the scholars of the Jews, as God the Almighty said: Why do not the rabbis and the priests forbid them from their sinful speech and their consumption of what is unlawful? The monks are the worshippers of the Christians and the priests are their scholars, as God the Almighty said: That is because among them are priests and monks. The purpose is to warn against the evil scholars and worshippers of misguidance, as Sufyan ibn Uyaynah said: Whoever among our scholars became corrupt had some resemblance to the Jews, and whoever among our worshippers became corrupt had some resemblance to the Christians. And in the authentic hadith: You will follow the ways of those who came before you, step by step. They said: The Jews and the Christians? He said: Then who? And in the narration: The Persians and the Romans. He said: Then who are the people except these? The result is a warning against imitating them in their words and actions. That is why God Almighty said: To devour the wealth of people unjustly and avert [people] from the way of God. This is because they devour the world with religion, and their positions and leadership over people, they devour their wealth with that, just as the Jewish rabbis had honor over the people of ignorance, and they had tribute, gifts, and taxes that came to them. So when God sent His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, they continued in their misguidance, disbelief, and stubbornness, hoping that those leaderships would remain for them, so God extinguished them with the light of prophethood and took them away from them and replaced them with humiliation and disgrace, and they incurred the wrath of God Almighty. God the Almighty says: And they hinder [people] from the way of God meaning that along with their eating what is forbidden, they hinder people from following the truth and they mix truth with falsehood and they appear to those who follow them from the ignorant that they are calling them to goodness, but they are not as they claim. Rather, they are callers to the Fire and on the Day of Resurrection they will not be helped. God the Almighty says: And those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend it in the way of God - give them tidings of a painful punishment These are the third group of leaders of the people, for the people are dependent on the scholars, the servants and the wealthy. So if the conditions of these people are corrupted, the conditions of the people will be corrupted, as Ibn al-Mubarak said: Did anyone corrupt the religion except the kings, the bad rabbis, and the monks? As for the treasure, Malik said on the authority of Abdullah bin Dinar on the authority of Ibn Umar, it is the money for which zakat is not paid. Al-Thawri and others narrated on the authority of Ubaidullah on the authority of Nafi’ on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: That which zakat is paid on is not a treasure even if it is under seven earths, and that which is visible and zakat is not paid on it is a treasure. This has been narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Jabir, and Abu Hurairah, both with and without chains of transmission. Umar bin Al-Khattab said something similar: Any money for which zakat is paid is not a treasure even if it is buried in the ground, and any money for which zakat is not paid is a treasure with which its owner is branded even if it is on the surface of the earth. Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Al-Zuhri on the authority of Khalid bin Aslam, who said: We went out with Abdullah bin Umar, and he said: This was before zakat was revealed, but when it was revealed, God made it a purification for wealth. Umar bin Abdul Aziz and Arak bin Malik said the same, and it was abrogated by the words of God the Almighty: Take from their wealth a charity verse. Saeed bin Muhammad bin Ziyad said on the authority of Abu Umamah that he said: The adornment of swords is from treasure. I will not tell you except what I heard from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Thawri said on the authority of Abu Hasin on the authority of Abu Ad-Dhaha on the authority of Ja'dah bin Hubayrah on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, who said: Four thousand or less is a provision, and anything more than that is a treasure. This is strange. There are many hadiths that praise the small amount of gold and silver and condemn the large amount of them. We will mention here a part that indicates the rest. Abdul Razzaq said: Al-Thawri told us, Abu Hasin told me on the authority of Abu Ad-Dhaha on the authority of Ja'dah bin Hubayrah on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, regarding the verse: And those who hoard gold and silver the verse. The Prophet said: Perish the gold, perish the silver, he said it three times. This upset the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they said: What kind of money should we take? Omar, may God be pleased with him, said: I know that for you. He said: O Messenger of God, your companions have found it difficult and they said: What kind of wealth should we acquire? He said: A tongue that remembers God, a grateful heart, and a wife who helps each one of you in his religion. Another Hadith Imam Ahmad said: Abdullah bin Amr bin Murrah told us, on the authority of Abu Muhammad Ja`far, Shu`bah told us, Salim bin Abdullah told us, Abdullah bin Abi Al-Hudhayl told us, a friend of mine told me that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, Perish gold and silver. He said, and my friend told me that he went with Umar bin Al-Khattab and said: O Messenger of God, your saying, Perish gold and silver, what should we save? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A tongue that remembers God, a grateful heart, and a wife who helps in the Hereafter. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Waki` narrated to us, Abdullah bin Amr bin Murrah narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Salim bin Abi al-Ja`d, on the authority of Thawban, who said: When what was revealed about gold and silver was revealed, they said: What kind of wealth should we acquire? Umar said: I will tell you that. So he put it on a camel and caught up with him, and I was following him. He said: O Messenger of God, what kind of wealth should we acquire? He said: A grateful heart, a remembering tongue, and a wife who helps one of you in the matter of the Hereafter. At-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah narrated it through other chains of transmission on the authority of Salim bin Abi al-Ja`d, and at-Tirmidhi said: It is hasan. It was narrated on the authority of al-Bukhari that Salim did not hear it from Thawban. I said: That is why some of them narrated it from him as a mursal. And God knows best. Another hadith Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Hamid bin Malik told us, Yahya bin Ya’la al-Maharibi told us, my father told us, Ghailan bin Jami’ al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Uthman Abi al-Yaqzan, on the authority of Ja’far bin Abi Iyas, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: When this verse was revealed, And those who hoard gold and silver, the verse, it was difficult for the Muslims and they said: None of us can leave money for his children that will last after him. So Umar said: I will relieve you. So Umar set out and Thawban followed him and came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Prophet of God, this verse has been difficult for your companions. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God did not impose zakat except to purify what remains of your wealth, and He only imposed inheritance from the wealth that will remain after you. He said: Umar said: God is great, then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: Shall I not tell you of the best thing that a man hoards? A righteous woman who pleases him when he looks at her, obeys him when he commands her, and protects him when he is away from her. Narrated by Abu Dawud, al-Hakim in his Mustadrak, and Ibn Mardawayh from the hadith of Yahya bin Ya’la, and Al-Hakim said: It is authentic according to their conditions, but they did not include it. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Ruh told us, Al-Awza’i told us, on the authority of Hassan bin Atiyah, who said: Shaddad bin Aws, may God be pleased with him, was on a journey and stopped at a place, so he said to his servant: Bring us a knife so we can play with it. She objected to him, so he said: I have not spoken a word since I became Muslim except that I have stopped and restrained it except for this word of mine, so do not keep it to myself, but keep what I say to you. I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “When people hoard gold and silver, then hoard these words: O God, I ask You for steadfastness in the matter and determination to follow the right path, and I ask You for gratitude for Your blessings, and I ask You for the best of Your worship, and I ask You for a sound heart, and I ask You for a truthful tongue, and I ask You for the best of what You know, and I seek refuge in You from the worst of what You know, and I ask Your forgiveness for what You know, for You are the Knower of the unseen.” And the Almighty said: “On the Day when it will be heated in the fire of Hell, and their foreheads, their flanks, and their backs will be branded with it. This is what you hoarded for yourselves, so taste what you used to hoard.” That is, this statement will be said to them as a rebuke, rebuke, and mockery, as in His statement: “Then pour over his head from the punishment of scalding water. Taste. Indeed, you are the mighty, the noble.” That is, this is for that, and this is what you used to hoard for yourselves. For this reason it is said that whoever loves something and gives it precedence over obeying God will be punished with it. And these people, since collecting this wealth was more important to them than pleasing God with them, they were punished with it, just as Abu Lahab, may God curse him, was striving in his enmity towards the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his wife helped him in that. On the Day of Resurrection, she will also be an aid to his punishment. Around her neck, that is, her neck, will be a rope of palm fiber, that is, she will gather firewood in the fire and throw it over him, so that this will be more effective in his punishment than the one who was most compassionate toward him in this world. Just as this wealth, since it was the most precious thing to its owners, was the most harmful thing to them in the Hereafter, so it will be heated with it in the fire of Hell. And its sea is enough for their foreheads, sides and backs to be branded with it. Sufyan said on the authority of Al-A’mash on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr bin Murrah on the authority of Masruq on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud: By the One besides whom there is no god, no servant will be branded with a treasure, touching dinar by dinar or dirham by dirham, but his skin will be spread out and each dinar and dirham will be placed separately. Ibn Mardawayh narrated it on the authority of Abu Hurayrah with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, but its chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet is not authentic, and God knows best. Abdul Razzaq said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Ibn Tawus, on the authority of his father, who said: It has reached me that on the Day of Resurrection, the treasure will turn into a brave man, following its owner while he flees from him and saying: I am your treasure, and he will not attain anything from it except that he takes it. Imam Abu Ja`far Ibn Jarir said: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Sa`id told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Salim Ibn Abi al-Ja`d, on the authority of Ma`dan Ibn Abi Talhah, on the authority of Thawban, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: “Whoever leaves behind a treasure, it will appear to him on the Day of Resurrection as a bald-headed serpent with two raisins, following him and saying: Woe to you, what are you? It will say: I am your treasure that you left behind, and it will continue to follow him until it puts its hand in it and he bites it, then the rest of his body will follow it.” Ibn Hibban narrated it in his Sahih from the hadith of Yazid from Sa`id with it. The origin of this hadith is in the two Sahihs from the narration of Abu al-Zinad from al-A`raj from Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him. In Sahih Muslim from the hadith of Suhayl Ibn Abi Salih from his father from Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There is no man who does not pay the zakat of his wealth except that plates of fire will be made for him on the Day of Resurrection, with which his sides, forehead, and back will be branded on a day the length of which is fifty thousand years, until judgment is passed among the servants, then he will see his path, either to Paradise or to Hell.” And he mentioned the rest of the hadith. Al-Bukhari said in his interpretation of this verse: Qutaybah bin Saeed told us, Jarir told us, on the authority of Hisin, on the authority of Zaid bin Wahb, who said: I passed by Abu Dharr in Ar-Rabdhah and I said: What brought you to this land? He said: We were in Ash-Sham and I read: And those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend it in the way of God, give them tidings of a painful punishment. Muawiyah said: This is not for us. This is only for the People of the Book. He said: I said: It is for us and for them. Ibn Jarir narrated it from the hadith of Abthar bin Al-Qasim from Hisin from Zaid bin Wahb from Abu Dharr, may God be pleased with him, and he mentioned it and added, so the talk rose between me and him, so he wrote to Uthman complaining about me, so Uthman wrote to me to come to him. He said: So I came to him, and when I arrived in Madinah, the people rode me as if they had never seen me before that day, so I complained about that to Uthman, so he said to me: Move away quickly. I said: By God, I will not abandon what I used to say. I said It was from the school of thought of Abu Dharr, may God be pleased with him, that it was forbidden to save what is in excess of the expenses of one’s family, and he used to issue fatwas to that effect and urge them to do so and command them to do so and be strict in contradicting it, so Muawiyah forbade him, but he did not stop, so he feared that this would harm the people, so he wrote complaining to the Commander of the Faithful, Uthman, and that he should take him to him. Uthman summoned him to Madinah and housed him alone in Ar-Rabdhah. And he died there, may God be pleased with him, during the caliphate of Uthman. And Muawiyah, may God be pleased with him, tested him while he was with him to see if his actions would agree with his words, so he sent him a thousand dinars and distributed them that day, then he sent to him the one who brought them to him and said: Muawiyah sent me to someone other than you and I made a mistake, so bring the gold. He said: Woe to you, it has gone out, but when my money comes, we will hold you accountable for it. And thus Ali bin Abi Talhah narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that it is general. Al-Suddi said: It is for the people of the Qiblah. Al-Ahnaf bin Qais said: I came to Medina and while I was in a circle in which there were a group of Quraysh, a man with rougher clothes, a rougher body, and a rougher face came and stood over them and said: Give the treasurers good report of a hot coal that will be heated in the fire of Hell and placed on the nipple of one of them until it comes out of the hollow of his shoulder and is placed on the hollow of his shoulder until it comes out of the nipple of his breast and he shakes. He said: So the people lowered their heads and I did not see any of them respond to him with anything. He said: He turned away, so I followed him until he sat by a pillar and I said: I did not see these people except that they disliked what I said to them. He said: These people do not know anything. And in the Sahih it is narrated that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: And he said to Abu Dharr: It would not please me to have as much gold as Mount Uhud for three days and still have nothing of it except a dinar that I set aside for a debt. And God knows best, this is what prompted Abu Dharr to say this. He said: My friend commanded me that any gold or silver that I put on it is like live coals for its owner until he spends it in the way of God Almighty. And he narrated it on the authority of Yazid on the authority of Hammam, and he added spending it. Al-Hafiz Ibn Asakir said, on the authority of Abu Bakr al-Shibli, in his biography, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Mahdi, who said: Umar ibn Abi Salamah told us, on the authority of Sadaqah ibn Abdullah, on the authority of Talhah ibn Zayd, on the authority of Abu Farwah al-Rahawi, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Abu Sa’id, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Meet God poor, and do not meet Him rich. He said: O Messenger of God, how can I do that? He said: Whatever you are asked for, do not refuse, and whatever you are provided with, do not hide. He said: O Messenger of God, how can I do that? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: That is it, otherwise Hellfire. Its chain of transmission is weak. This has been narrated through other chains of transmission. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la said: Mahmoud bin Khidash told us. 9:35: Al-Suddi said: The rabbis are from the Jews and the monks are from the Christians, and it is as he said, for the rabbis are the scholars of the Jews, as God the Almighty said: Why do not the rabbis and the priests forbid them from their sinful speech and their consumption of what is unlawful? The monks are the worshippers of the Christians and the priests are their scholars, as God the Almighty said: That is because among them are priests and monks. The purpose is to warn against the evil scholars and worshippers of misguidance, as Sufyan ibn Uyaynah said: Whoever among our scholars became corrupt had some resemblance to the Jews, and whoever among our worshippers became corrupt had some resemblance to the Christians. And in the authentic hadith: You will follow the ways of those who came before you, step by step. They said: The Jews and the Christians? He said: Then who? And in the narration: The Persians and the Romans. He said: Then who are the people except these? The result is a warning against imitating them in their words and actions. That is why God Almighty said: To devour the wealth of people unjustly and avert [people] from the way of God. This is because they devour the world with religion, and their positions and leadership over people, they devour their wealth with that, just as the Jewish rabbis had honor over the people of ignorance, and they had tribute, gifts, and taxes that came to them. So when God sent His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, they continued in their misguidance, disbelief, and stubbornness, hoping that those leaderships would remain for them, so God extinguished them with the light of prophethood and took them away from them and replaced them with humiliation and disgrace, and they incurred the wrath of God Almighty. God the Almighty says: And they hinder [people] from the way of God meaning that along with their eating what is forbidden, they hinder people from following the truth and they mix truth with falsehood and they appear to those who follow them from the ignorant that they are calling them to goodness, but they are not as they claim. Rather, they are callers to the Fire and on the Day of Resurrection they will not be helped. God the Almighty says: And those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend it in the way of God - give them tidings of a painful punishment These are the third group of leaders of the people, for the people are dependent on the scholars, the servants and the wealthy. So if the conditions of these people are corrupted, the conditions of the people will be corrupted, as Ibn al-Mubarak said: Did anyone corrupt the religion except the kings, the bad rabbis, and the monks? As for the treasure, Malik said on the authority of Abdullah bin Dinar on the authority of Ibn Umar, it is the money for which zakat is not paid. Al-Thawri and others narrated on the authority of Ubaidullah on the authority of Nafi’ on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: That which zakat is paid on is not a treasure even if it is under seven earths, and that which is visible and zakat is not paid on it is a treasure. This has been narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Jabir, and Abu Hurairah, both with and without chains of transmission. Umar bin Al-Khattab said something similar: Any money for which zakat is paid is not a treasure even if it is buried in the ground, and any money for which zakat is not paid is a treasure with which its owner is branded even if it is on the surface of the earth. Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Al-Zuhri on the authority of Khalid bin Aslam, who said: We went out with Abdullah bin Umar, and he said: This was before zakat was revealed, but when it was revealed, God made it a purification for wealth. Umar bin Abdul Aziz and Arak bin Malik said the same, and it was abrogated by the words of God the Almighty: Take from their wealth a charity verse. Saeed bin Muhammad bin Ziyad said on the authority of Abu Umamah that he said: The adornment of swords is from treasure. I will not tell you except what I heard from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Thawri said on the authority of Abu Hasin on the authority of Abu Ad-Dhaha on the authority of Ja'dah bin Hubayrah on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, who said: Four thousand or less is a provision, and anything more than that is a treasure. This is strange. There are many hadiths that praise the small amount of gold and silver and condemn the large amount of them. We will mention here a part that indicates the rest. Abdul Razzaq said: Al-Thawri told us, Abu Hasin told me on the authority of Abu Ad-Dhaha on the authority of Ja'dah bin Hubayrah on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, regarding the verse: And those who hoard gold and silver the verse. The Prophet said: Perish the gold, perish the silver, he said it three times. This upset the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they said: What kind of money should we take? Omar, may God be pleased with him, said: I know that for you. He said: O Messenger of God, your companions have found it difficult and they said: What kind of wealth should we acquire? He said: A tongue that remembers God, a grateful heart, and a wife who helps each one of you in his religion. Another Hadith Imam Ahmad said: Abdullah bin Amr bin Murrah told us, on the authority of Abu Muhammad Ja`far, Shu`bah told us, Salim bin Abdullah told us, Abdullah bin Abi Al-Hudhayl told us, a friend of mine told me that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, Perish gold and silver. He said, and my friend told me that he went with Umar bin Al-Khattab and said: O Messenger of God, your saying, Perish gold and silver, what should we save? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A tongue that remembers God, a grateful heart, and a wife who helps in the Hereafter. Umar said: I will tell you that. So he put it on a camel and caught up with him, and I was following him. He said: O Messenger of God, what kind of wealth should we acquire? He said: A grateful heart, a remembering tongue, and a wife who helps one of you in the matter of the Hereafter. 9:36: Imam Ahmad said: Ismail told us, Ayoub told us, Muhammad bin Sirin told us, on the authority of Abu Bakrah, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, delivered a sermon during his Hajj and said: “Behold, time has come back to the way it was on the day God created the heavens and the earth. The year is twelve months, four of which are sacred, three of which are consecutive: Dhul-Qa'dah, Dhul-Hijjah and Muharram, and Rajab of Mudar, which is between Jumada and Sha'ban.” Then he said: What day is this? We said: God and His Messenger know best. He remained silent until we thought he would call it by another name. He said: Is it not the Day of Sacrifice? We said: Yes. Then he said: What month is this? We said: God and His Messenger know best. He remained silent until we thought he would call it by another name. He said: Is it not Dhul-Hijjah? We said: Yes. Then he said: What city is this? We said: God and His Messenger know best. He remained silent until we thought he would call it by another name. He said: Is it not the town? We said: Yes. He said: “Your blood, your wealth - and I think he said - and your honor are sacred to you, as sacred as this day of yours, in this month of yours, in this country of yours. And you will meet your Lord, and He will ask you about your deeds. Do not return after me to misguidance, striking the necks of one another. Have I not conveyed the message? Let the one among you who is present convey it to the one who is absent, for perhaps the one who conveys it will be more receptive to it than some of those who hear it.” Narrated by Al-Bukhari in the interpretation and elsewhere. Muslim narrated from the hadith of Ayoub on the authority of Muhammad, who is Ibn Sirin, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman Ibn Abi Bakra, on the authority of his father, with it. Ibn Jarir said: Muammar narrated to us, Ruh narrated to us, Ash’ath narrated to us, on the authority of Muhammad Ibn Sirin, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Time has come back to the way it was on the day He created the heavens and the earth. The number of months with God is twelve months in the Book of God on the day He created the heavens and the earth, of which four are sacred: three consecutive months - Dhul-Qa’dah, Dhul-Hijjah, and Muharram - and Rajab of Mudar, which is between Jumada and Sha’ban.” Al-Bazzar narrated it on the authority of Muhammad Ibn Muammar with it. Then he said: It is not narrated from Abu Hurairah except from this source, and Ibn Awn and Qurra narrated it from Ibn Sirin from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakra from his father with it, and Ibn Jarir also said: Musa ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Masruqi told me, Zaid ibn Habbab told us, Musa ibn Ubaydah al-Rabdhi told us, Sadaqah ibn Yasar told me from Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, delivered a sermon during the Farewell Pilgrimage in Mina in the middle of the days of Tashreeq, and he said: “O people, time has come full circle, and today it is as it was on the day God created the heavens and the earth. The number of months with God is twelve months, four of which are sacred, the first of which is Rajab of Mudar between Jumada and Sha’ban, and Dhul-Qa’dah, Dhul-Hijjah and Muharram.” Ibn Mardawayh narrated from the hadith of Musa ibn Ubaydah from Abdullah ibn Dinar from Ibn Umar something similar or similar to it, and Hammad ibn Salamah said: Ali ibn Zaid told me from Abu Hamza al-Raqashi from his uncle, and he was a companion, who said: I was holding the reins of the Messenger of God’s camel, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the middle of the days of Tashreeq, fending off the camels. People said about him, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Behold, time has returned to its original state as it was on the day God created the heavens and the earth, and the number of months with God is twelve months in the Book of God on the day He created the heavens and the earth, of which four are sacred, so do not wrong yourselves during them.” Saeed bin Mansour said, Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Al-Kalbi, on the authority of Abu Saleh, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, of which four are sacred, he said, Muharram, Rajab, Dhul-Qa’dah, and Dhul-Hijjah. And his saying, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the hadith: Time has returned to its original state on the day God created the heavens and the earth, is a confirmation from him, may God bless him and grant him peace, and a confirmation of the matter as God made it, at the beginning, without advancing or delaying, without increasing or decreasing, without interfering or changing, as he said in the prohibition of Mecca: This city was made sacred by God on the day He created the heavens and the earth, so it is sacred by the sanctity of God Almighty until the Day of Resurrection. And thus he said here: Time has returned to its original state on the day God created the heavens and the earth, meaning the matter today is legally as God innovated it in His Book on the day He created the heavens and the earth. Some commentators and speakers on this hadith have said that what is meant by his saying, It has become round as it was on the day God created the heavens and the earth, is that it happened that the pilgrimage of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, occurred in that year in Dhu al-Hijjah, and that the Arabs had postponed the pilgrimage in many years, and most of them were in years other than Dhu al-Hijjah. They claimed that the pilgrimage of Abu Bakr in the year nine was in Dhu al-Qi’dah, and there is a view on this, as we will explain when we talk about the postponement. What is stranger than that is what al-Tabarani narrated on the authority of some of the predecessors in a hadith that it happened that the pilgrimage of the Muslims, Jews, and Christians occurred on one day, which was the Day of Sacrifice in the year of the Farewell Pilgrimage, and God knows best. Chapter Sheikh Alam Al-Din Al-Sakhawi mentioned in a volume he collected called Al-Mashhur fi Asmaa Al-Ayyam wa Al-Shohor that Muharram was named thus because it is a forbidden month. I believe that it was named thus to emphasize its prohibition because the Arabs would alternate in it, making it permissible one year and prohibiting it the next. He said: The plural is Muharramat, Muharim, and Muharim. Safar was named thus because their houses were empty of them when they went out to fight and travel. It is said that a place is Safar if it is empty, and the plural is Asfar like Jamal and Ajmal. The month of Rabi’ Al-Awwal was named thus because they would spend the night in it, and spending the night in a quarter’s building, and the plural is Arba’a like Naseeb and Ansaba’, and Arba’a like Raghif and Raghifah. Rabi’ Al-Akhir is like Al-Awwal. Jumada was named thus because the water froze in it. He said: The months in their calculations did not revolve. There is a consideration in this, since their months were tied to the crescent moons, so they had to revolve, so perhaps they named it thus when the water froze in the cold, as the poet said: A night of Jumada with clubs, in whose darkness the servant does not see the trumpet The dog does not bark except once until he wraps his tail around his trunk. The plural is Jamadiyyat like Hubara and Habariyyat. It can be masculine or feminine, so it is said Jumada al-Ula and al-Awwal, Jumada al-Akhir and al-Akhira. Rajab is from Tarjeeb, which means to glorify, and it is pluralized as Arjab, Rajab, and Rajabat. Sha’ban is from the branching out of tribes and their dispersal for raids, and it is pluralized as Sha’bain and Sha’banat. Ramadan is from the intensity of the heat, and it is said that the camels became thirsty when they became thirsty, and it is pluralized as Ramadanat, Ramadhin, and Armadah. He said: The statement of those who said that it is one of the names of God is a mistake that should not be considered or heeded. I said: A hadith has been reported about it, but it is weak, and I explained it at the beginning of the Book of Fasting. Shawwal is from the camels’ lifting their tails for the sake of the path. He said: It is pluralized as Shawawil, Shawawil, and Shawalat. Al-Qa’dah, with the opening of the qaf, I said: And with the breaking of the qaf, because they sit down from fighting and traveling, and it is pluralized as Dhat al-Qa’dah. The argument with the kasra of the ha’, I said and the fatha, it was named thus because they performed the Hajj in it, and the plural is Dhat al-Hijjah. The names of the days begin with Sunday, and the plural is Ahad, Awhad, and Wujud, then Monday, and the plural is Athanayn, Tuesday is extended and is masculine and feminine and the plural is Thalaathawat and Athlath, then Wednesday with the extension and the plural is Arba’awat and Arba’i’, and Thursday is pluralized as Akhmasa and Akhamis, then Friday with the damma of the meem, its sukoon, and its fatha as well, and the plural is Jama’ and Jama’at, Saturday is taken from Sabt, which is the cut-off because the number ends with it, and the Arabs used to name the days Awal, then Ahwan, then Jabbar, then Dabar, then Mu’nis, then Al-‘Uruba, then Shiyar. A poet from the early Arab Arabs, the Arab Arabs, said: I hope to live, even if my day is better, easier, or tougher. Or the next one is Dabar, if he gives you a fatwa, then it is Munis, or Arouba, or Shiyar And the Almighty’s saying: Of them, four are sacred. This is something that the Arabs also used to forbid in the pre-Islamic period, and it is what the majority of them did, except for a group of them called Al-Basl, who used to forbid eight months of the year, in order to be more thorough and strict. As for his saying, “Three consecutive months: Dhul-Qa’dah, Dhul-Hijjah, and Muharram, and Rajab of Mudar, which is between Jumada and Sha’ban,” he only added it to Mudar to show the correctness of their saying about Rajab that it is the month between Jumada and Sha’ban, not as Rabi’ah thought, that Rajab al-Muharram is the month between Jumada and Sha’ban, not as Rabi’ah thought, that Rajab al-Muharram is the month between Sha’ban and Shawwal, which is Ramadan today. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, explained that it is Rajab of Mudar, not Rajab of Rabi’ah. Rather, the sacred months were four, three consecutive and one separate, for the purpose of performing the rituals of Hajj and Umrah. So a month was forbidden before the months of Hajj, which is Dhul-Qa’dah, because they would sit back from fighting in it, and the month of Dhul-Hijjah was forbidden because they would perform Hajj in it and be busy performing the rituals in it, and another month was forbidden after it, which is Muharram, so that they would return to the furthest part of their country in it. Safe, and Rajab was made sacred in the middle of the year for the purpose of visiting the House and performing Umrah in it for those who come to it from the farthest reaches of the Arabian Peninsula, so they visit it and then return to their homeland in it safely. And his saying: That is the upright religion meaning this is the straight law of obeying the command of God in what He has made of the sacred months and following them according to what was mentioned in the first Book of God. God the Almighty said: So wrong not yourselves therein meaning in these sacred months because they are more serious and more severe in sin than in others, just as sins in the sacred land are doubled according to the saying of God the Almighty: And whoever intends therein to commit an act of injustice - We will make him taste a painful punishment. Likewise, sins are made more severe in the sacred month, and for this reason, the blood money is made more severe in it according to the Shafi’i school of thought and a large group of scholars, and likewise in the case of one who kills in the sacred sanctuary or kills a mahram. Hammad bin Salamah said on the authority of Ali bin Zaid on the authority of Yusuf bin Mihran on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his saying: So wrong not yourselves therein he said: in all the months. Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his saying: Indeed, the number of months is with God the verse, so do not wrong yourselves therein in all of them. Then He singled out four months from that and made them sacred and magnified their sanctity. And He made the sin in them greater and the righteous deed and reward greater. Qatada said about His statement: So do not wrong yourselves therein that injustice in the sacred months is a greater sin and burden than injustice in other months, even though injustice is great in any case, but God magnifies whatever He wills of His command. He said that God has chosen the best of His creation. He chose messengers from the angels and messengers from the people, and He chose His remembrance from speech, and He chose mosques from the earth. He chose Ramadan and the sacred months from the months, and He chose Friday from the days, and He chose the Night of Decree from the nights, so magnify what God has magnified. Indeed, matters are glorified by the way God has glorified them among the people of understanding and reason. Al-Thawri said on the authority of Qais bin Muslim on the authority of Al-Hasan on the authority of Muhammad bin Al-Hanafiyyah that they should not be forbidden as they are forbidden. Muhammad bin Ishaq said: So do not wrong yourselves therein meaning do not make what is forbidden permissible nor what is permissible forbidden as the polytheists did. Rather, the intercalation that they used to do was an increase in disbelief. Thus those who disbelieve go astray verse. This statement is the choice of Ibn Jarir. And his saying: And fight the polytheists all together meaning all of you as they fight you all together meaning all of them and know that God is with the righteous. The scholars differed about the prohibition of initiating fighting in the sacred month, is it abrogated or decisive according to two opinions one of them and the most famous is that it is abrogated because the Almighty said here so do not wrong yourselves therein and ordered fighting the polytheists, and the apparent context indicates that he ordered that as a general order, and if it had been forbidden in the sacred month, he would have almost restricted it to its expiration, and because the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, besieged the people of Taif in a sacred month, which is Dhul-Qa’dah, as is proven in the two Sahihs that he went out to Hawazin in Shawwal, and when he defeated them and took their wealth and returned, they took refuge in Taif, so he went to Taif and besieged them for forty days and returned and did not conquer it, so it is proven that he besieged it in the sacred month. The other opinion is that initiating fighting in the sacred month is forbidden and that it did not abrogate the prohibition of the sacred month because the Almighty said: O you who believe, do not make lawful the land of your Lord except in the month of Dhul-Qa’dah. The rites of God and the sacred month. He said: “The sacred month for the sacred month, and the sacred things are retaliation. So whoever transgresses against you, transgress against him in proportion to his transgression against you.” The verse. He said: So when the sacred months have passed, kill the polytheists. The verse. It was previously mentioned that they are the four prescribed in every year, not the months of circulation according to one of the two opinions. As for the Almighty’s saying: And fight the polytheists all together as they fight you all together, it is possible that it is disconnected from what came before it and that it is a renewed ruling and is from the category of incitement and incitement, i.e. just as they gather to fight you if they fight you, then you also gather against them if you fight them and fight them in the same way as they do. It is possible that he gave permission to the believers to fight the polytheists in the sacred month if they were the ones who started it, as the Almighty said: The sacred month for the sacred month, and the sacred things are equal in retaliation. And the Almighty said: “And do not fight them at the Sacred Mosque until they fight you there. But if they fight you, then kill them.” And thus the answer to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, besieging the people of Taif and continuing the siege until the sacred month came, is from the completion of the fight against Hawazin and its allies from Thaqeef, for they are the ones who started the fight and gathered the men and called for war and combat, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, targeted them as mentioned above, so when they fortified themselves in Taif, he went to them to bring them down from their fortresses, so they attacked the Muslims and killed a group, and it continued. The siege with catapults and other means lasted nearly forty days. It began in a lawful month and the forbidden month began, so it continued for a few days, then it was closed off to them, because what is forgiven in its continuity is not forgiven in its beginning. This is an established matter and has many parallels, and God knows best. Let us mention the hadiths that have been reported on this, and we have explained that in the biography, and God knows best.
9:37: This is what God Almighty condemned the polytheists for, for their manipulation of God's law with their corrupt opinions, and their changing of God's rulings with their cold whims, and their making permissible what God has forbidden and forbidding what God has permitted. They had in them such a strong anger, chivalry and zeal that they extended the three-month period of prohibition that prevented them from fulfilling their desires by fighting their enemies. They had innovated before Islam a period of permitting the forbidden month, so they delayed it to Safar, making permissible the forbidden month and forbidding the permissible month, in order to match the number of what God has forbidden, the four months, as their poet, Umair bin Qais, known as Jadhal al-Ta'an, said: I have learned that my people are noble people and that they have noble people. Aren't we the ones who forget the months of permissibility and make them forbidden? Which people did we not know Potter and which people did we not bridle? Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: The postponement is only an increase in disbelief. Al-Nasi said that Junada bin Awf bin Umayya Al-Kinani used to come to the season every year and he was called Abu Thamama and he would call out: Abu Thamama is not to be answered nor criticized. “The first year’s Safar is permissible,” so he would make it permissible for the people and forbid Safar one year and forbid Muharram one year. This is the statement of God: The postponement is only an increase in disbelief. He said: They leave Muharram one year and forbid it another year. Al-Awfi narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Laith bin Abi Salim said on the authority of Mujahid: “A man from Banu Kinana used to come every year to the season on his donkey and say: O people, I am not to be criticized nor answered nor rejected for what I say. We have forbidden Muharram and postponed Safar.” Then the next year comes after him and he says the same thing as he said and he says we have forbidden Safar and delayed Muharram so his saying to make up the number of what God has forbidden he said meaning the four so they make permissible what God has forbidden by delaying this sacred month, and it was narrated from Abu Wa'il, Ad-Dahhak and Qatadah something similar to this, and Abdurrahman bin Zaid bin Aslam said in his saying The postponement is only an increase in disbelief the verse, this is a man from Banu Kinanah called Al-Qalmas and they were in the pre-Islamic era and they did not attack each other in the sacred month, a man would meet the killer of his father and not extend his hand to him, so when it was him he said go out with us they said to him this is Muharram he said we postpone it this year they are two Safar year, so when the next year we have completed it we make them forbidden, he said so he did that and when it was the next year he said do not fight in Safar they forbade it with Muharram they are forbidden, this is a strange description of the postponement and there is consideration in it because in one year they only forbid three months for this and in the year that follows they forbid five months so where is this from the saying of God the Almighty: They make it lawful one year and forbid it another year to match the number of months that God has forbidden. Another strange description was also narrated from Mujahid. Abd al-Razzaq said: Muammar told us on the authority of Abu Nujayh on the authority of Mujahid regarding the words of God the Almighty: The postponement is only an increase in disbelief 10:13, he said: God the Almighty made Hajj obligatory in Dhul-Hijjah. He said: The polytheists used to call Dhul-Hijjah Muharram, Safar, Rabi’ and Rabi’, Jumada and Jumada, Rajab and Sha’ban, Ramadan, Shawwal, Dhul-Qa’dah and Dhul-Hijjah. They would perform Hajj in it once, then they would remain silent about Muharram and not mention it, then they would go back and call it Safar, then they would call Rajab Jumada al-Akhira, then they would call Sha’ban Ramadan, then they would call Shawwal Ramadan, then they would call Dhul-Qa’dah Shawwal, then they would call Dhul-Hijjah Dhul-Qa’dah, then they would call Muharram Dhul-Hijjah and they would perform Hajj in it, and its name among them was Dhul-Hijjah. Then they returned in the same manner, so they would perform Hajj every year for two months, until the Hajj of Abu Bakr, the last of the two years, coincided with Dhul-Qi’dah. Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, performed his Hajj, which coincided with Dhul-Hijjah. That is when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would say in his sermon: Time has turned back to its state on the day God created the heavens and the earth. What Mujahid said is also questionable, and how can Abu Bakr’s Hajj be valid when it occurred in Dhul-Qi’dah? And how is this? God the Almighty said: And an announcement from God and His Messenger to the people on the day of the greater pilgrimage that God is free from the polytheists and so is His Messenger verse. It was only announced during the pilgrimage of Abu Bakr. If it had not been in Dhu al-Hijjah, God the Almighty would not have said: the day of the greater pilgrimage. This postponement that He mentioned about the rotation of the year for them and their pilgrimage in every month for two years is not required from their action. The postponement is not possible without this. For when they made the month of Muharram permissible one year, they made Safar its substitute forbidden, and after it Rabi’ and Rabi’ until the end of the year as it is according to its system, number, and names of its months. Then in the second year they made Muharram permissible and left it as it was forbidden, and after it Safar and Rabi’ and Rabi’ until the end of it. They made it permissible one year and forbade it another year to match the number of what God has forbidden, so they make permissible what God has forbidden meaning in the prohibition of four months of the year, except that sometimes they bring forward the prohibition of the third month of the three consecutive months, which is Muharram, and sometimes they postpone it to Safar, meaning they delay it. We have already discussed the statement of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Time has come round hadith, meaning that the matter is in the number of months and the prohibition of what is It is forbidden from it according to what was mentioned in the Book of God regarding the number and the sequence, not as the ignorant Arabs depend on them, separating the prohibition of some of them by intercalation from others, and God knows best. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Salih bin Bishr bin Salamah al-Tabarani told us, Makki bin Ibrahim told us, Musa bin Ubaidah told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Dinar, on the authority of Ibn Umar, that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stopped at al-Aqabah and whoever God willed of the Muslims gathered around him, so he praised God and extolled Him as He deserves, then he said: The intercalation is only from Satan, an increase in disbelief by which those who disbelieve are led astray, permitting it one year and forbidding it another year. So they would forbid the sacred month one year and permit Safar, and permit the sacred month, which is the intercalation. Imam Muhammad bin Ishaq spoke about this in his book, Al-Seerah, in a good, beneficial and beautiful way. He said: The first person to postpone the months for the Arabs, and to make permissible what God had forbidden and to make permissible what God had made permissible, was Al-Qalams, who was Hudhayfah bin Abd Faqim bin Adi bin Amir bin Tha’laba bin Al-Harith bin Malik bin Kinanah bin Khuzaymah bin Mudrikah bin Ilyas bin Mudar bin Nizar bin Ma’ad bin Adnan. Then after him, his son Ibad took over this, then after Ibad, his son Qala’ bin Ibad, then his son Umayyah bin Qala’, then his son Awf bin Umayyah, then his son Abu Thamama Junadah bin Awf, and he was the last of them. Islam was established upon him. When the Arabs finished their Hajj, they would gather around him, and he would stand among them as a preacher, and he would make Rajab, Dhul-Qa’dah, and Dhul-Hijjah forbidden. He would make Muharram permissible one year and replace it with Safar, and he would make it forbidden to match the number of months that God had forbidden, so he made permissible what God had forbidden, meaning he made permissible what God had forbidden and forbade what God had made permissible. And God knows best.
9:38: This is the beginning of a rebuke to those who stayed behind from the Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) in the Battle of Tabuk when the fruits and shade were good in the intense heat and scorching summer. God the Almighty said: O you who have believed, what is [the matter] with you that when you are told to go forth in the cause of God meaning when you are called to jihad in the cause of God you cling heavily to the earth meaning you become lazy and inclined to remain in ease, comfort and good fruits. Are you satisfied with the life of this world rather than the Hereafter? meaning why did God the Blessed and Exalted act like this, more satisfied with the world than the Hereafter? Then God the Blessed and Exalted showed indifference to the world and desired the Hereafter, saying: The enjoyment of the life of this world is but little compared to the Hereafter as Imam Ahmad said: We were told by Wakee' and Yahya bin Saeed, they said: Ismail bin Abi Khalid told us on the authority of Qais on the authority of Al-Mustawrid, the brother of Banu Fihr, he said: The Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) said: "The world in comparison to the Hereafter is nothing but like one of you dipping his finger into the sea. Let him see what it brings back?" And he pointed with his index finger. Muslim alone narrated it. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated: Bishr bin Muslim bin Abdul Hamid Al-Himsi told us in Homs. Al-Rabi bin Ruh told us. Muhammad bin Khalid Al-Wahbi told us. Ziyad, meaning Al-Jassas, told us on the authority of Abu Uthman who said: I said: O Abu Hurairah, I heard from my brothers in Basra that you say: I heard the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: God rewards for a good deed with a million good deeds. Abu Hurairah said: Rather, I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: God rewards for a good deed with two million good deeds. Then he recited this verse: But the enjoyment of the life of this world is but little compared to the Hereafter. The worldly life is what has passed of it and what remains of it with God is little. Ath-Thawri said on the authority of Al-A’mash regarding the verse: But the enjoyment of the life of this world is but little compared to the Hereafter. He said: Like the provisions of a traveler. Abdul Aziz bin Abi Hazim said on the authority of his father: When the death of Abdul Aziz bin Marwan was approaching, he said: Bring me my shroud in which I will be shrouded so that I may look at it. When it was placed in front of him, he looked at it and said: Do I not have anything great left behind in this world except this? Then he turned his back and wept, saying: Shame on you, O home! Indeed, your much is little, and indeed, your little is short, and indeed, we are in delusion because of you. Then the Almighty threatened those who abandon jihad, saying: If you do not go forth, He will punish you with a painful punishment. Ibn Abbas said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called forth a tribe of Arabs, but they were reluctant to go forth, so God withheld rain from them, and their punishment was and will replace you with another people, meaning to support His Prophet and establish His religion, as God Almighty said: And if you turn away, He will replace you with another people; then they will not be the likes of you. “And you will not harm Him at all,” meaning you will not harm God at all by turning away from jihad, your refusal, and your reluctance to go forth. And God is over all things competent, meaning He is able to triumph over the enemies without you. It has been said that this verse and His statement: Go forth, whether light or heavy, and His statement: It was not for the people of Medina and those around them of the bedouins to stay behind from the Messenger of God, were abrogated by God Almighty’s statement: “And it is not for the believers to go forth all at once. So why should not a party from every division of them go forth?” This was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, Al-Hasan, and Zaid. Ibn Aslam responded to Ibn Jarir and said: This is only for those whom the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called to jihad, and it became obligatory for them. If they had abandoned it, they would have been punished for it. This has a direction, and God Almighty knows best what is correct.
9:39: This is the beginning of a rebuke to those who stayed behind from the Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) in the Battle of Tabuk when the fruits and shade were good in the intense heat and scorching summer. God the Almighty said: O you who have believed, what is [the matter] with you that when you are told to go forth in the cause of God meaning when you are called to jihad in the cause of God you cling heavily to the earth meaning you become lazy and inclined to remain in ease, comfort and good fruits. Are you satisfied with the life of this world rather than the Hereafter? meaning why did God the Blessed and Exalted act like this, more satisfied with the world than the Hereafter? Then God the Blessed and Exalted showed indifference to the world and desired the Hereafter, saying: The enjoyment of the life of this world is but little compared to the Hereafter as Imam Ahmad said: We were told by Wakee' and Yahya bin Saeed, they said: Ismail bin Abi Khalid told us on the authority of Qais on the authority of Al-Mustawrid, the brother of Banu Fihr, he said: The Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) said: "The world in comparison to the Hereafter is nothing but like one of you dipping his finger into the sea. Let him see what it brings back?" And he pointed with his index finger. Muslim alone narrated it. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated: Bishr bin Muslim bin Abdul Hamid Al-Himsi told us in Homs. Al-Rabi bin Ruh told us. Muhammad bin Khalid Al-Wahbi told us. Ziyad, meaning Al-Jassas, told us on the authority of Abu Uthman who said: I said: O Abu Hurairah, I heard from my brothers in Basra that you say: I heard the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: God rewards for a good deed with a million good deeds. Abu Hurairah said: Rather, I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: God rewards for a good deed with two million good deeds. Then he recited this verse: But the enjoyment of the life of this world is but little compared to the Hereafter. The worldly life is what has passed of it and what remains of it with God is little. Ath-Thawri said on the authority of Al-A’mash regarding the verse: But the enjoyment of the life of this world is but little compared to the Hereafter. He said: Like the provisions of a traveler. Abdul Aziz bin Abi Hazim said on the authority of his father: When the death of Abdul Aziz bin Marwan was approaching, he said: Bring me my shroud in which I will be shrouded so that I may look at it. When it was placed in front of him, he looked at it and said: Do I not have anything great left behind in this world except this? Then he turned his back and wept, saying: Shame on you, O home! Indeed, your much is little, and indeed, your little is short, and indeed, we are in delusion because of you. Then the Almighty threatened those who abandon jihad, saying: If you do not go forth, He will punish you with a painful punishment. Ibn Abbas said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called forth a tribe of Arabs, but they were reluctant to go forth, so God withheld rain from them, and their punishment was and will replace you with another people, meaning to support His Prophet and establish His religion, as God Almighty said: And if you turn away, He will replace you with another people; then they will not be the likes of you. “And you will not harm Him at all,” meaning you will not harm God at all by turning away from jihad, your refusal, and your reluctance to go forth. And God is over all things competent, meaning He is able to triumph over the enemies without you. It has been said that this verse and His statement: Go forth, whether light or heavy, and His statement: It was not for the people of Medina and those around them of the bedouins to stay behind from the Messenger of God, were abrogated by God Almighty’s statement: “And it is not for the believers to go forth all at once. So why should not a party from every division of them go forth?” This was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, Al-Hasan, and Zaid. Ibn Aslam responded to Ibn Jarir and said: This is only for those whom the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called to jihad, and it became obligatory for them. If they had abandoned it, they would have been punished for it. This has a direction, and God Almighty knows best what is correct.
9:40: God the Almighty says: "If you do not support him meaning support his Messenger, then God will support him, suffice him, and protect him, just as He took charge of supporting him when those who disbelieved expelled him, the second of two" meaning the year of the Hijra, when the polytheists intended to kill him, imprison him, or exile him, so he fled from them with his friend and companion Abu Bakr ibn Abi Quhafah, and took refuge in the Cave of Thawr for three days so that those who had gone out could return to their tracks and then move towards Madinah. Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, was afraid that someone would come upon them and harm the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would calm him down and make him steadfast, saying: "O Abu Bakr, what do you think of two, with God as their third?" as Imam Ahmad said: Affan told us, Hammam told us, Thabit told us, on the authority of Anas, that Abu Bakr told him, he said: I said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while we were in al-Kahf 18:If one of them looked at his feet, he would see us under his feet. He said: So he said: "O Abu Bakr, what do you think?" By two, God is the third of them. They both included it in the two Sahihs. That is why the Almighty said: Then God sent down His tranquility upon him, meaning His support and victory over him, meaning the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, according to the most famous of the two opinions. It was also said that it was upon Abu Bakr. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas and others that they said: Because the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, always had tranquility with him. This does not contradict the renewal of tranquility specific to that situation. That is why He said: And supported him with soldiers you did not see, meaning the angels. And He made the word of those who disbelieved the lowest, while the word of God was the highest. Ibn Abbas said: He meant by the word of those who disbelieved polytheism, and the word of God is there is no god but God. In the two Sahihs, on the authority of Abu Musa al-Ash’ari, may God be pleased with him, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about a man who fights bravely, fights out of pride, and fights for show, which of them is in the way of God? He said: Whoever fights so that the word of God is supreme is in the way of God. And his saying: And God is Exalted in Might means in His vengeance and victory, impregnable in His side, and no one who seeks refuge at His door and takes protection by adhering to His address will be wronged. Wise in His words and actions.
9:41: Sufyan al-Thawri said on the authority of his father on the authority of Abu al-Dhaha Muslim bin Subaih: This verse, Go forth, whether light or heavy, was the first to be revealed in Surat Bara'ah. Mu'tamir bin Sulayman said on the authority of his father: A Hadrami claimed that it was mentioned to him that some people were thinking that one of them might be sick or old and he would say: I will not sin, so God revealed, Go forth, whether light or heavy, the verse. God Almighty commanded the general mobilization with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the year of the Battle of Tabuk to fight the enemies of God from the infidel Romans from the People of the Book, and He made it obligatory for the believers to go out with him in every situation, in ease and hardship, in difficulty and ease, so He said, Go forth, whether light or heavy. Ali bin Zaid said on the authority of Anas on the authority of Abu Talha: “Old men and young men, God did not hear the excuse of anyone. Then he went out to the Levant and fought until he was killed.” In another narration, Abu Talha recited Surah Bara’ah and came to this verse: Go forth, whether light or heavy, and strive with your wealth and your lives in the cause of God. He said: “I see that our Lord has called us to battle, old and young. Prepare me, my son.” His sons said: “May God have mercy on you. You fought with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, until he died, and with Abu Bakr until he died, and with Umar until he died, so we will fight on your behalf.” But he refused and boarded the sea and died. They did not find an island to bury him on except after nine days, and he did not change, so they buried him on it. And thus it was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, Abu Salih, Al-Hasan Al-Basri, Suhayl bin Atiyah, Muqatil bin Hayyan, Al-Sha’bi, and Zaid bin Aslam that they said in the interpretation of this verse: Go forth, whether light or heavy, old men and young men. And so said Ikrimah, Ad-Dahhak, Muqatil bin Hayyan, and more than one. Mujahid said: young men.” And the elderly, the rich, and the poor. Abu Saleh and others said the same. Al-Hakam bin Utaybah said: busy and not busy. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the words of God Almighty: March forth, whether light or heavy, meaning, march forth with energy and without energy. Qatada said the same. Ibn Abi Nujayh said on the authority of Mujahid: March forth, whether light or heavy, they said: For among us are the heavy, the needy, the poor, the busy, and the one who has his affairs made easy. So God revealed and refused to excuse them unless they march forth, light or heavy, meaning whatever they were. Al-Hasan bin Abi Al-Hasan Al-Basri also said: regarding hardship and ease. All of this is from the requirements of the generality in the verse. This is the choice of Ibn Jarir. Imam Abu Amr Al-Awza’i said: If the mobilization was to the paths of the Romans, people would mobilize to them lightly and on horseback, and if the mobilization was to these coasts, they would mobilize to them lightly and heavily, on horseback and on foot. This is a detailed explanation of the issue. It has been narrated from Ibn Abbas, Muhammad bin Ka’b, Ata’ Al-Khurasani and others that this verse was abrogated by the words of God Almighty: Why should not a party from every division of them go forth? We will discuss that later, God willing. Al-Suddi said: His words: Go forth, whether light or heavy mean rich or poor, strong or weak. A man came to him that day, they claimed that he was Al-Miqdad, and he was a great and fat man. He complained to him and asked him to give him permission, but he refused. So the verse was revealed that day: Go forth, whether light or heavy. When this verse was revealed, people were distressed, so God abrogated it and said: There is no blame upon the weak or upon the ill or upon those who do not find what they can spend if they are sincere to God and His Messenger. Ibn Jarir said: Yaqub told me, Ibn Ulayyah told us, Ayoub told us, on the authority of Muhammad, who said: Abu Ayoub witnessed Badr with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and then he did not stay away from any Muslim expedition except for one year. He said: Abu Ayoub used to say: God Almighty said: Go forth, whether light or heavy, and I do not find myself except light or heavy. Ibn Jarir said: Saeed bin Amr Al-Sakuni told me, Baqiyah told us, Jarir told us, Abd Al-Rahman bin Maysarah told us, Abu Rashid Al-Habrani told me: I came across Al-Miqdad bin Al-Aswad, the knight of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sitting on a coffin of the money changers in Homs, and some of its bones had been removed from it, intending to go on a raid. I said to him: God has excused you. He said: Surat Al-Ba’uth came to us: Go forth, whether light or heavy. Ibn Jarir said: Hayyan bin Zaid Al-Sharabi told me: We went forth with Safwan bin Amr, who was the governor of Homs before Al-Afsus, to Al-Jarajima. I saw an old man, worried, with his eyebrows drooping over his eyes, from the people of Damascus, on his mount among those who had raided. I approached him and said: O uncle, God has excused you. He raised his eyebrows and said: O son of my brother, God has called us forth, whether light or heavy. Beware, whoever God loves, He tests him, then He returns him and keeps him. God only tests from among His servants those who are grateful, patient, and remember Him. None is worshipped except God, the Almighty. Then God, the Almighty, encouraged spending in His cause and sacrificing one’s life to please Him and His Messenger, saying: “And strive with your wealth and your lives in the cause of God. That is best for you, if you only knew.” That is, this is better for you in this world and the Hereafter, because you will spend little in spending, but God will give you the wealth of your enemy in this world, along with what He has saved for you of honor in the Hereafter, as the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God has guaranteed to the one who strives in His cause, if He takes him, that He will admit him to Paradise, or return him to his home with what he has earned of reward or spoils. For this reason God, the Almighty, said: “Fighting has been prescribed for you, though you dislike it. But perhaps you dislike a thing and it is good for you; and perhaps you like a thing and it is bad for you. God knows, while you do not know.” And of this type is what Imam Ahmad narrated: Muhammad ibn Abi Uday narrated to us, on the authority of Humayd, on the authority of Anas, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to a man: Become Muslim. He said: I find myself reluctant. He said: Become Muslim, even if I am reluctant.
9:42: God Almighty says, rebuking those who stayed behind from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the Battle of Tabuk and stayed behind after asking his permission to do so, pretending that they had excuses, but they did not. He said: If it had been a near gain, Ibn Abbas said: a near booty, and a short journey, meaning also near, they would have followed you, meaning they would have come with you for that purpose, but the distance was too far for them, meaning the distance to Syria, and they will swear by God, meaning to you when you return to them, if we were able, we would have gone out with you, meaning if we had no excuses, we would have gone out with you. God Almighty said: They destroy themselves, and God knows that they are liars.
9:43: Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abu Hasin bin Sulayman al-Razi told us, Sufyan bin Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Misa'ar, on the authority of Awn, who said: Have you heard of a better reproach than this? A call for forgiveness before the reproach, so he said: May God forgive you, why did you give them permission? And Muwarriq al-'Ajli and others said the same. Qatada said: He reproached him as you hear, then He revealed what is in Surat An-Nur, giving him permission to give them permission if he wishes, so He said: So when they ask your permission for some of their affairs, give permission to whomever you wish of them (al-An'am 2:10). And this was also narrated on the authority of Ata’ al-Khurasani. Mujahid said: This verse was revealed about some people who said: Ask permission from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and if he gives you permission, then stay, and if he does not give you permission, then stay. For this reason, God Almighty said: Until it becomes clear to you who are truthful meaning in presenting excuses, and you know who are lying. God Almighty says: Why did you not leave them when they asked your permission and not give permission to any of them to stay, so that you could know who among them was truthful in showing your obedience from the liar? For they were determined to stay away from the war even if you did not give them permission to do so. That is why God Almighty informed us that no one who believes in God and His Messenger asks His permission to sit back from fighting, so He said: Those who believe in God and the Last Day do not ask your permission that is, to sit back from fighting, to strive with their wealth and their lives because they see jihad as an act of devotion, and when He called them to it, they hastened and complied. “And God is Knowing of the righteous. Only those who have no excuse ask your permission” that is, to sit back, those who do not believe in God and the Last Day that is, do not hope for God’s reward in the Hereafter for their deeds, and whose hearts doubt that is, doubt the truth of what you have brought them, so in their doubt they waver that is, they are confused, they put one foot forward and the other back, and they have no firm footing in anything, so they are a confused and doomed people, neither to these nor to those. And he whom God sends astray, you will never find for him a way.

9:46: God Almighty says: "And if they had intended to go out meaning with you to the conquest they would have made preparations for it meaning they would have been ready for it but God disliked their going out meaning He disliked that they go out with you to some extent so He held them back meaning He delayed them and it was said, 'Stay with those who stay behind'" meaning to some extent. Then God Almighty explained the reason for His dislike for their going out with the believers and said: "If they had gone out with you, they would not have increased you except in confusion meaning because they are cowards and defeated and they would have slid among you, seeking to cause you discord meaning they would hasten to walk and travel among you with gossip, hatred and discord and among you are those who listen to them" meaning they obey them and approve of their speech and words and seek their advice even if they do not know their condition, which leads to the occurrence of evil among the believers and great corruption. Mujahid, Zaid bin Aslam and Ibn Jarir said: And among you are those who listen to them meaning spies who hear the report for them and convey it to them. This does not remain specific to their going out with them, rather it is general in all situations, and the first meaning is more apparent in the appropriateness of the context, and Qatada and other commentators agreed with it. Muhammad bin Ishaq said: Those who asked permission, as I have heard, were of noble people, including Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul and Al-Jadd bin Qais, and they were nobles among their people. But God, knowing them, discouraged them from going out with him and corrupting his army. There were people among his army who loved them and obeyed them in what they called them to because of their nobility among them. He said: And among you are those who listen to them. Then God Almighty informed about His complete knowledge, saying: And God is Knowing of the wrongdoers. So He informed that He knows what was and what will be and what would not have been if it had been, how it would have been. For this reason God Almighty said: If they had gone out with you, they would not have increased you except in ruin. So He informed about their condition, how it would have been if they had gone out, and despite this they did not go out, as God Almighty said: “And if they had been returned, they would have returned to what they were forbidden. And indeed, they are liars.” God Almighty also said: “And if God had known any good in them, He would have made them hear. And if He had made them hear, they would have turned away while they were averse.” God Almighty also said: “And if We had prescribed for them, ‘Kill yourselves’ or ‘Leave your homes,’ only a few of them would have done it. And if they had done what they were told, they would not have done it.” If they had been admonished by it, it would have been better for them and a firmer confirmation. And then We would have given them from Ourselves a great reward. And We would have guided them to a straight path. And there are many verses on this.

9:48: The Almighty says, inciting His Prophet, peace be upon him, against al-Munafiqun 63:They had sought discord before and had turned matters upside down for you. That is, they had put their minds to work and their opinions to plot against you and your companions and to abandon your religion and extinguish it for a long time. That was when the Prophet, peace be upon him, first came to Medina, the Arabs shot him with one bow, and the Jews of Medina and its hypocrites fought him. Then, when God granted him victory on the day of Badr and made his word supreme, Abdullah bin Ubayy and his companions said: This is a matter that has been decided, so they entered Islam outwardly. Then, whenever God strengthened Islam and its people, that angered them and made them upset. That is why the Almighty said: Until the truth came and the command of God appeared, while they were averse.
9:49: God the Almighty says: And among the hypocrites are those who say to you: O Muhammad, Give me permission to stay and do not tempt me by going out with you because of the female slaves from the Romans. God the Almighty says: Indeed, they have fallen into temptation meaning they have fallen into temptation by saying this as Muhammad ibn Ishaq said on the authority of Al-Zuhri, Yazid ibn Ruman, Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr, Asim ibn Qatadah and others said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said one day while he was preparing for Al-Jadd ibn Qays, the brother of Banu Salamah: Would you like, O Jadd, to fight the yellow people? He said: O Messenger of God, give me permission and do not tempt me, for by God my people know that there is no man more amazed by women than I am, and I fear that if I see the women of Banu Al-Yasr I will not be able to be patient without them. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) turned away from him and said: I have given you permission. This verse was revealed about Al-Jadd bin Qays: And among them is he who says, ‘Give me permission and do not put me to trial’ 1:17. That is, if he only feared the women of Banu Al-Yasr, but that was not the case, then the trial that fell upon him by his staying behind the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and his desire for himself was greater than his own. And thus it was narrated from Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and others that it was revealed about Al-Jadd bin Qays, and this Al-Jadd bin Qays was one of the nobles of Banu Salamah. In the Sahih it is narrated that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to them: Who is your master, O Banu Salamah? They said: Al-Jadd bin Qays, although we consider him stingy. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: What disease is worse than stinginess? But your master is the white, curly-haired young man, Bishr bin Al-Bara’ bin Ma’rur. And the Almighty’s statement: And Hell will surely encompass the disbelievers means that they have no escape from it, no way out, and no way out.
9:50: The Blessed and Most High knows His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, of the enmity of these people towards him, because no matter how much good he receives, that is, victory and triumph over the enemies, which pleases him and his companions, it displeases them. And if disaster befalls you, they say, ‘We took our precaution beforehand,’ meaning, we were cautious about following him before this. And they turn away, rejoicing. So God Almighty guided the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to answer them in this complete enmity, so He said: Say, meaning to them, Nothing will ever happen to us except what God has decreed for us, meaning, we are under His will and destiny. He is our Protector, meaning, our Master and our refuge. And in God let the believers put their trust, meaning, we put our trust in Him, and He is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs.
