9:52: God Almighty says: Say to them, O Muhammad, Do you await for us that is, do you await for us anything but one of the two best things martyrdom or victory over you, as Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah and others said. And we await for you that is, await for you that God may afflict you with a punishment from Himself or by our hands that is, we await for you this or that, either that God may afflict you with a punishment from Himself or by our hands by captivity or killing. Then await, for we are with you, awaiting. And God Almighty says: "Say: Spend willingly or unwillingly" that is, whatever you spend, willingly or unwillingly, "it will not be accepted from you. Indeed, you were a people of evildoers." Then God Almighty informed about the reason for that, which is that it will not be accepted from them except that they disbelieved in God and His Messenger that is, deeds are only valid through faith. And they do not come to prayer except while they are lazy that is, they do not have a correct intention or desire for the work. And they do not spend any spending except while they are reluctant. The Truthful and Trustworthy, may God bless him and grant him peace, said that God does not get tired until you get tired, and that God is good and accepts only that which is good. For this reason, God does not accept any spending or work from these people, because He only accepts from the righteous.

9:55: God the Almighty says to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, So let not their wealth or their children impress you, as He the Almighty said, "And do not strain your eyes toward that by which We have given enjoyment to [some] categories of them - the splendor of the life of this world - by which We test them. But the provision of your Lord is better and more lasting." And He said, Do they think that what We provide them with of wealth and children * We hasten for them in good things? Rather, they do not perceive. And His statement, God only desires to punish them with it in the life of this world, Al-Hasan Al-Basri said about its zakat and spending from it in the way of God. Qatada said: This is from the advanced and deferred, its meaning is: So let not their wealth or their children impress you in the life of this world. God only desires to punish them with it in the Hereafter. Ibn Jarir chose the statement of Al-Hasan, which is the strong and good statement. And His statement, And their souls will depart while they are disbelievers, means that He desires to cause them to die when He causes them to die in disbelief, so that this will be more painful for them and more severe for their punishment. We seek refuge in God from that. This is a way of luring them into what they are in.
9:56: God the Almighty informs His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about their anxiety, fear, division and panic that they swear by God that they are of you a firm oath but they are not of you that is, in reality but they are a people who are afraid that is, He is the One who made them swear if they could find a refuge that is, a fortress in which to fortify themselves and a place of protection in which to guard themselves or caves which are in the mountains or an entrance which is a passage in the ground and a tunnel. This was said in the three by Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and Qatadah they would turn back to it while they were rushing that is, they would hasten to leave you because they are only mixing with you out of hatred, not love, and they wish that they did not mix with you. However, necessity has its rulings, and for this reason they remain in worry, sadness and grief because Islam and its people are still in glory, victory and elevation. For this reason, whenever the Muslims are happy, it makes them sad, so they wish that they did not mix with the believers. For this reason, He said if they could find a refuge or caves or an entrance, they would turn back to it while they were rushing They run wild.

9:58: God the Almighty says: And among them meaning among the hypocrites is he who criticizes you meaning he finds fault with you regarding the division of the alms if you distribute them and accuses you of that, and they are the accused and the dissolute, and with this they do not deny for the sake of religion, but they deny for the sake of their own interests, and for this reason if they are given from it, they are pleased, but if they are not given from it, then at once they become angry meaning they become angry for the sake of themselves. Ibn Jurayj said: Dawud bin Abi Asim told me that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was brought some alms and he distributed it here and there until it was gone. He said, and behind him was a man from the Ansar, so he said: This is not justice, so this verse was revealed. Qatada said about His statement: And among them is he who criticizes you concerning the alms meaning: And among them is he who criticizes you concerning the alms, and it was mentioned to us that a man from the desert who had recently met a Bedouin woman came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was distributing gold and silver, and he said, O Muhammad, by God, if God has commanded you to be just, you have not been just. Then the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Woe to you! Who will be just towards you after me? Then the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Beware of this man and his likes, for among my nation are those like him who recite the Qur’an, but it does not go beyond their collarbones. So if they go out, kill them. Then if they go out, kill them. Then if they go out, kill them.” And it was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: “By the One in Whose hand is my soul, I will not give you anything, nor will I withhold it from you. I am only a treasurer.” What Qatada mentioned is similar to what the two sheikhs narrated from the hadith of Az-Zuhri on the authority of Abu Salamah on the authority of Abu Saeed in the story of Dhu Al-Khuwaysira, whose name was Harqoos, when he objected to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he divided the spoils of Hunayn, so he said to him: Be just, for you have not been just. He said: You have failed and lost if I am not just. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said when he saw him standing behind his back: “From the offspring of this man will emerge a people whom one of you will consider insignificant in comparison to his prayer and his fasting in comparison to their fasting. They will depart from the religion as an arrow departs from its target. So wherever you encounter them, kill them, for they are the worst of those killed under the sky.” He mentioned the rest of the hadith, then God Almighty said, alerting them to what is better for them than that, saying: “And if they had been satisfied with what God and His Messenger have given them and had said, ‘Sufficient for us is God. God will give us of His bounty, and [so will] His Messenger. Indeed, we are desirous toward God.” This noble verse contains great etiquette and a noble secret, as it made contentment with what God and His Messenger have given one and trust in God alone, and He is His saying: And they said, ‘God is sufficient for us,’ and also the desire to turn to God alone for success in obeying the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and complying with his commands, abandoning his prohibitions, believing his report, and following his footsteps.

9:60: When God the Almighty mentioned the objection of the ignorant hypocrites to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and their slander of him regarding the division of the charity, God the Almighty explained that He is the One who divided it and ruled over it and took charge of its matter Himself and did not entrust its division to anyone other than Him, so He divided it for these mentioned people as narrated by Imam Abu Dawud in his Sunan from the hadith of Abd al-Rahman ibn Ziyad ibn An'am, and in it there is weakness, on the authority of Ziyad ibn Na'im, on the authority of Ziyad ibn al-Harith al-Sada'i, may God be pleased with him, who said: I came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and pledged allegiance to him, then a man came and said: Give me some of the charity, so he said to him: "God was not pleased with the ruling of a prophet or anyone else regarding charity until He ruled over it, so He divided it into eight categories. If you are one of those categories, I will give you." The scholars differed regarding these eight categories: Is it necessary to pay all of them or to what is possible from them? There are two opinions one of them that it is necessary, and this is the opinion of al-Shafi'i and a group. The second is that it is not necessary to cover all of them, but it is permissible to pay them to one of them and give all of the charity if the rest are present. This is the opinion of Malik and a group of the early and later generations, including Omar, Hudhayfah, Ibn Abbas, Abu Al-Aaliyah, Saeed bin Jubair, and Maymun bin Mihran. Ibn Jarir said: This is the opinion of a general group of scholars. Based on this, the categories were mentioned here to clarify the recipient, not to make it necessary to cover all of the giving. There are reasons for argument and objection, and God knows best. The poor were mentioned here before the rest because they are more in need than others, according to the well-known opinion, and because of their extreme poverty and need. According to Abu Hanifa, the needy are in a worse state than the pauper, and this is as Ahmad said. Ibn Jarir said: Yaqub told me, Ibn Ulayyah told us, Ibn Awn told us, on the authority of Muhammad, who said: Umar, may God be pleased with him, said: The poor is not the one who has no money, but the poor is the one who is not good at earning. Ibn Ulayyah said: The one who is not good at earning, according to us, and the majority are against him. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Al-Hasan Al-Basri, and Ibn Zayd. Ibn Jarir and others chose that the poor person is the one who is self-sufficient and does not ask people for anything, and the needy person is the one who asks, wanders around, and follows people. Qatada said: The poor person is the one who has a disease, and the needy person is the one who is healthy. Al-Thawri said on the authority of Mansur on the authority of Ibrahim: They are the poor immigrants. Sufyan al-Thawri said: It means that the Bedouins are not given anything from it. And this was narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair and Saeed bin Abd al-Rahman bin Abza. Ikrimah said: Do not call the poor Muslims poor. The poor are the People of the Book. Let us mention hadiths related to each of the eight categories. As for the poor, it was narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Charity is not permissible for the rich or for the one who has a strong means of livelihood. Narrated by Ahmad, Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi. Ahmad, al-Nasa’i and Ibn Majah also narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah something similar. On the authority of Ubaydullah ibn ‘Adi ibn al-Khayyar that two men told him that they came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, asking him for charity. He looked at them and saw that they were strong. He said: “If you wish, I will give you something. But consider whether it is for the rich or for the strong, able-bodied person.” Narrated by Ahmad, Abu Dawud and al-Nasa’i with a strong chain of transmission. Ibn Abi Hatim said in the Book of al-Jarh wa’l-Ta’dil: Abu Bakr al-‘Absi said: ‘Umar, may God be pleased with him, recited: Zakat is only for the poor. He said: They are the People of the Book. ‘Umar ibn Nafi’ narrated on his authority: I heard my father say that. I said: This is a very strange statement, assuming the chain of transmission is sound. Even if Abu Hatim did not state that this Abu Bakr was unknown, he is considered unknown. As for the needy, it was narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The needy is not like this. The one who goes around to the people and is turned away with a morsel or two, or a date or two. They said: Who is the poor, O Messenger of God? He said: The one who does not find enough wealth to make him independent, and no one notices him so that he can give him charity and does not ask people for anything. Narrated by Al-Bukhari and Muslim. As for those who work on it, they are the tax collectors and messengers who deserve a share from him for that, and it is not permissible for them to be from the relatives of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to whom charity is forbidden, as is proven in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Abdul Muttalib bin Rabi’ah bin Al-Harith, that he and Al-Fadl bin Al-Abbas went out to ask the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to employ them in collecting charity, so he said: Charity is not permissible for Muhammad or the family of Muhammad, rather it is the filth of the people. As for those whose hearts are to be reconciled, some of them are given something to convert to Islam, as the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave Safwan ibn Umayya some of the spoils of Hunayn, even though he had been a polytheist. He said: He kept giving me something until he became the most beloved of people to me after he had been the most hated of people to me, as Imam Ahmad said: Zakariya ibn Adi told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Sa`id ibn al-Musayyab, on the authority of Safwan ibn Umayya, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave me something on the day of Hunayn, even though he was the most hated of people to me. He kept giving me something until he became the most beloved of people to me.” Muslim and al-Tirmidhi narrated it from the hadith of Yunus, on the authority of al-Zuhri, with it. Some of them are given something to improve their Islam and strengthen their hearts, as he also gave a group of the most prominent and prominent freed slaves a hundred camels on the day of Hunayn, and he said: I give to a man, and others are more beloved to me than him, for fear that God will throw him on his face into the fire of Hell. In the two Sahihs, on the authority of Abu Sa`id, that `Ali sent to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, a gold coin in its soil from Yemen, and he divided it among four men: Al-Aqra` ibn Habis, `Uyaynah ibn Badr, `Alqamah ibn `Ulatha, and Zayd al-Khair, and he said, I will win them over. Some of them will be given what is hoped will be the conversion of their peers to Islam, and some of them will be given to collect alms from those closest to them, or to protect the Muslims from harm from the outskirts of the country. The place for the details of this is in the books of branches, and God knows best. Are those who were reconciled to Islam given a gift after the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him)? There is a difference of opinion on this. It was narrated from ‘Umar, ‘Amir, al-Sha’bi and a group that they are not given a gift after him because God has honored Islam and its people and empowered them in the lands and humbled the necks of the servants for them. Others said that they are given a gift because he (peace and blessings of God be upon him) gave it to them after the conquest of Mecca and the defeat of Hawazin, and this is something that may be needed and given to them. As for the slaves, it was narrated from al-Hasan al-Basri, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, ‘Umar ibn ‘Abd al-‘Aziz, Sa’id ibn Jubayr, al-Nakha’i, al-Zuhri and Ibn Zayd that they are those who were freed from slavery. Something similar was narrated from Abu Musa al-Ash’ari, and it is the opinion of al-Shafi’i and al-Layth may God be pleased with them both. Ibn Abbas and Al-Hasan said: There is nothing wrong with freeing a slave from zakat, and this is the doctrine of Ahmad, Malik and Ishaq, meaning that slaves are more general than giving or buying a slave and freeing it independently. Many hadiths have been narrated about the reward for freeing and freeing a slave, and that God frees for each limb of a slave a limb of its freedman, even the vagina for the vagina. This is only because the reward is of the same kind as the deed: And you are not recompensed except for what you used to do. And on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There are three who have a right to God’s help: the one who fights in the cause of God, the one who is freed from slavery who wants to pay it off, and the one who marries who wants to remain chaste.” Narrated by Imam Ahmad and the people of Sunan except Abu Dawud. In Al-Musnad, on the authority of Al-Bara’ bin Azib, he said: A man came and said: O Messenger of God, guide me to a deed that will bring me closer to Paradise and distance me from Hellfire? He said: Freeing a soul and freeing a slave. He said: O Messenger of God, are they not the same? He said: No, freeing a soul means that you free it alone, and freeing a slave means that you help with its price. As for those in debt, they are divided into categories. Among them: the one who took on a burden or guaranteed a debt and it became binding on him, so he was deprived of his money or was in debt in paying his debt or in a sin, then he repented. These are the ones to whom it is paid. The basis for this matter is the hadith of Qubaysah ibn Mukhariq al-Hilali, who said: I took on a burden, so I came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to ask him about it. He said: Stay until the charity comes to us, so we can order it for you. He said: Then he said: “O Qubaysah, begging is not permissible except for one of three: a man who took on a burden, so begging is permissible for him until he obtains it and then stops; a man who was afflicted with a calamity that swept away his wealth, so begging is permissible for him until he obtains a livelihood – or he said, a repayment of a livelihood – and a man who was afflicted with poverty until three wise men from his people’s relatives stood up and said, ‘So-and-so has been afflicted with poverty, so begging is permissible for him until he obtains a livelihood – or he said, a repayment of a livelihood –’ so what? Other than that, it is ill-gotten gain that its owner consumes as ill-gotten gain.” Narrated by Muslim. On the authority of Abu Sa`id, he said: A man was afflicted during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with fruits that he had bought, and his debts increased. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Give him charity. The people gave him charity, but that did not cover his debt. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to his creditors: Take what you find, and you have nothing but that. Narrated by Muslim. Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Samad told us, Sadaqah ibn Musa told us, on the authority of Abu Imran al-Jawni, on the authority of Qais ibn Yazid, on the authority of the judge of Egypt, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God will call upon the one who has a debt on the Day of Resurrection until he is made to stand before Him and say: O son of Adam, why did you take this debt and why did you waste the rights of the people? He will say: O Lord, You know that I took it and did not eat or drink or waste it, but either burning or stealing or wasting came at my hands. God will say: My servant has spoken the truth, I am more deserving of paying it off on your behalf today. So he calls upon God for something and He places it on the scale of his balance, so his good deeds outweigh his bad deeds, and he enters Paradise by the grace and mercy of God.” As for those who are in the way of God, among them are the warriors who have no right to the register, and according to Imam Ahmad, al-Hasan, and Ishaq, Hajj is from the way of God, and so is the wayfarer, who is the traveler who passes through a country and does not have anything to help him on his journey, so he is given from the charity what is sufficient for him to reach his country even if he has money, and this is the ruling for those who want to… He sets out on a journey from his country and does not have anything with him. He is given enough zakat money to cover his expenses for his outing and return. The evidence for this is the verse and what Imam Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah narrated from the hadith of Muammar on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam on the authority of Ata bin Yasar on the authority of Abu Saeed, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Charity is not permissible for a rich person except for five: the one who collects it, or a man who bought it with his own money, or a debtor, or a fighter in the cause of God, or a poor person who receives charity from it and gives it to a rich person.” Al-Sufyan and Al-Sufyan narrated it on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam on the authority of Ata’ as a mursal, and Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Atiyyah Al-Awfi on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Charity is not permissible for a rich person except in the cause of God, or a wayfarer, or a poor neighbor who gives you a gift or invites you. His statement: An obligation from God means a ruling determined by God’s determination, imposition, and division. And God is Knowing and Wise means He knows the outward and inward aspects of things and the interests of His servants. Wise in what He says, does, legislates, and rules. There is no god but Him and no Lord but Him.
9:61: God the Almighty says: Among the hypocrites are people who harm the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) by speaking ill of him, and they say, He is an ear, meaning whoever says something to him, he believes it, and whoever talks to him, he believes it, so if we go to him and swear to him, we believe him. Its meaning was narrated from Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and Qatadah. God the Almighty says: Say, 'He is an ear of goodness for you,' meaning he is an ear of goodness, he knows the truthful from the liar, He believes in God and believes the believers, meaning he believes the believers, and a mercy to those who believe among you, meaning he is an argument against the disbelievers, and for this reason He said, And those who harm the Messenger of God will have a painful punishment.
9:62: Qatada said about the words of God Almighty: They swear to you by God to please you the verse. He said: It was mentioned to us that a man from the hypocrites said: By God, these are the best and most noble of us, even if what Muhammad says is true, they are worse than donkeys. He said: A man from the Muslims heard him and said: By God, what Muhammad says is true, and you are worse than a donkey. He said: The man went to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and told him. He sent for the man and called him and said: What made you say what you said? He began to curse and swear by God that he did not say that, and the Muslim man began to say: O God, make the truthful one true and the liar a liar. So God revealed the verse. And the Almighty’s saying: Do they not know that whoever opposes God and His Messenger the verse, meaning, have they not realized and known that whoever opposes God Almighty, meaning, opposes Him, fights Him, and contradicts Him, and is within the limits of God and His Messenger, then for him is the fire of Hell, wherein he will abide eternally meaning, humiliated and tormented, that is the great disgrace meaning, and this is the great humiliation and great misery.
9:63: Qatada said about the words of God Almighty: They swear to you by God to please you the verse. He said: It was mentioned to us that a man from the hypocrites said: By God, these are the best and most noble of us, even if what Muhammad says is true, they are worse than donkeys. He said: A man from the Muslims heard him and said: By God, what Muhammad says is true, and you are worse than a donkey. He said: The man went to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and told him. He sent for the man and called him and said: What made you say what you said? He began to curse and swear by God that he did not say that, and the Muslim man began to say: O God, make the truthful one true and the liar a liar. So God revealed the verse. And the Almighty’s saying: Do they not know that whoever opposes God and His Messenger the verse, meaning, have they not realized and known that whoever opposes God Almighty, meaning, opposes Him, fights Him, and contradicts Him, and is within the limits of God and His Messenger, then for him is the fire of Hell, wherein he will abide eternally meaning, humiliated and tormented, that is the great disgrace meaning, and this is the great humiliation and great misery.
9:64: Mujahid said: They say the saying among themselves and then they say: Perhaps God will not reveal this secret of ours to us. This verse is similar to the Almighty’s saying: “And when they come to you, they greet you with that with which God has not greeted you and they say to themselves: Why does God not punish us for what we say? Hell is sufficient for them, which they will burn, and wretched is the destination.” And he said about this verse: “Say: Scoff! Indeed, God will bring forth that which you fear.” That is, God will send down to His Messenger that which will disgrace you and make clear to him your situation, like the Almighty’s saying: “Or do those in whose hearts is disease think that God will not bring forth their hatred? And if We willed, We could show them to you, and you would know them by their mark, and you would know them by the tone of their speech.” The verse. For this reason, Qatada said: This exposing surah was called the Exposing the Hypocrites.
9:65: Abu Ma'shar Al-Madani said: On the authority of Muhammad bin Ka'b Al-Qurazi and others, they said: A hypocrite man said: I do not see these readers of ours except that we are the most greedy in bellies, the most lying in tongues, and the most cowardly in the encounter. So that was reported to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. So he came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he had departed and mounted his camel, and said: O Messenger of God, we were only joking and playing. So he said: "Was it at God and His verses and His Messenger that you were mocking? Make no excuse; you have disbelieved after your belief. If We pardon one party of you, We will punish another party because they were criminals." And his feet were scorching the stones, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not pay any attention to him, as he was clinging to the rope of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Abdullah bin Wahb said: Hisham bin Saad told me, on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam, on the authority of Abdullah bin Omar, who said: A man said in a gathering during the Battle of Tabuk: I have never seen anyone like our reciters, more greedy in stomachs, more lying in tongues, or more cowardly in combat. A man in the mosque said: You have lied, but you are a hypocrite. I will tell the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). That reached the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and the Qur’an was revealed. Abdullah bin Omar said: I saw him clinging to the saddle of the Messenger of God’s (peace and blessings of God be upon him) camel, and stones were hitting him, and he was saying: O Messenger of God, we were only joking and playing, and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was saying: Was it at God, His verses, and His Messenger that you were mocking? Al-Layth narrated it in a similar manner on the authority of Hisham bin Saeed. Ibn Ishaq said: He was from a group of hypocrites, including Wadi’ah ibn Thabit, the brother of Banu Umayyah ibn Zayd ibn Amr ibn Awf, and a man from Ashja’, an ally of Banu Salamah, called Makhshi ibn Himyar. They were travelling with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as he was heading to Tabuk. Some of them said to one another: Do you think that fighting the yellow people is like fighting the Arabs with one another? By God, tomorrow we will be bound together in ropes, to frighten and intimidate the believers. Makhshi bin Himyar said: By God, I would like to sue so that each man of us is flogged a hundred lashes, and we are unlikely to have the Qur’an revealed about us for what you said. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, as I have heard, to Ammar bin Yasir: “Catch up with the people, for they have been burned. Ask them what they said. If they deny it, say: Yes, you said such and such.” So Ammar went to them and said that to them. They came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to apologize to him. Wadi’ah bin Thabit said, while the Messenger of God was standing on his mount, and he kept saying, holding onto its reins: O Messenger of God, we were only joking and playing. Makhshi bin Himyar said: O Messenger of God, my name and my father’s name were with me. The one who was pardoned in this verse was Makhshi bin Himyar. He called himself Abd al-Rahman and asked God to be killed as a martyr whose whereabouts were not known. He was killed on the day of Yamamah and no trace of him was found. Qatada said: And if you ask them, they will surely say, ‘We were only conversing and joking.’ He said: While the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was on the Tabuk expedition and a group of hypocrites were walking before him, they said: “He thinks that he will conquer the palaces and fortresses of the Romans. Never! Never!” So God informed His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, of what they had said, so Ali said about these people, so he called them and said, You said such and such. They swore that we were only conversing and joking. Ikrimah said in his interpretation of this verse: There was a man whom God, if He wills, He will pardon, saying, “O God, I hear a verse that I mean, which makes the skin shudder and the heart tremble. O God, make my death a killing in Your cause, so that no one will say, ‘I was washed, I was shrouded, I was buried.’” He said: Then he was killed on the day of Yamamah, and there was not one of the Muslims who did not find someone else. And His saying: “Do not make excuses. You have disbelieved after your belief,” meaning this statement that you mocked. If We pardon one group of you, We will punish another group, meaning that not all of you will be pardoned, and some of you must be punished. Because they were criminals, meaning criminals with this wicked, wrong statement.

9:67: God Almighty says, denouncing the hypocrites who are contrary to the characteristics of the believers, and since the believers enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, these people enjoin what is wrong and forbid what is right and withhold their hands i.e. from spending in the way of God, they forgot God i.e. they forgot to mention God so He forgot them i.e. He treated them as someone who forgot them, as God Almighty says: And it will be said, ‘Today We will forget you as you forgot the meeting of this Day of yours’ “Indeed, the hypocrites are the wicked” i.e. those who have deviated from the path of truth and entered the path of misguidance, and His statement: God has promised the hypocrites, men and women, and the disbelievers the fire of Hell i.e. for this action that was mentioned about them to abide therein i.e. they will remain therein forever, they and the disbelievers it is sufficient for them i.e. it is sufficient for them in the punishment and God has cursed them i.e. He has expelled them and kept them away and for them is a lasting punishment.
9:68: God Almighty says, denouncing the hypocrites who are contrary to the characteristics of the believers, and since the believers enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, these people enjoin what is wrong and forbid what is right and withhold their hands i.e. from spending in the way of God, they forgot God i.e. they forgot to mention God so He forgot them i.e. He treated them as someone who forgot them, as God Almighty says: And it will be said, ‘Today We will forget you as you forgot the meeting of this Day of yours’ “Indeed, the hypocrites are the wicked” i.e. those who have deviated from the path of truth and entered the path of misguidance, and His statement: God has promised the hypocrites, men and women, and the disbelievers the fire of Hell i.e. for this action that was mentioned about them to abide therein i.e. they will remain therein forever, they and the disbelievers it is sufficient for them i.e. it is sufficient for them in the punishment and God has cursed them i.e. He has expelled them and kept them away and for them is a lasting punishment.
9:69: God Almighty says that these people have been afflicted with the punishment of God in this world and the Hereafter, just as He afflicted those before them. His statement, because of their character, Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: because of their religion. His statement, and you plunged like those who plunged, meaning in lies and falsehood. Those, their deeds have become worthless, meaning their efforts have been invalidated, so they will have no reward for them because they are corrupt. In this world and the Hereafter, and those are the losers, because they will not receive any reward for them. Ibn Jurayj said on the authority of Amr ibn Ata’ on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, Like those before you, the verse, Ibn Abbas said: How similar tonight is to last night, Like those before you, these are the Children of Israel. We likened them to them. I do not know except that he said: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, you will follow them until if a man of them entered the hole of a lizard, you would enter it. Ibn Jurayj said: And Ziyad ibn Sa’d informed me on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ziyad ibn Muhajir on the authority of Sa’id ibn Abi Sa’id al-Maqburi on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, you will follow the ways of those before you, inch by inch, cubit by cubit, and span by span, until if they entered the hole of a lizard, you would enter it. They said: Who are they, O Messenger of God? The People of the Book? He said: Then who? And thus Abu Ma`shar narrated it on the authority of Abu Sa`id al-Maqburi on the authority of Abu Hurayrah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: He mentioned it, and added that Abu Hurayrah said: Recite, if you wish, the Qur’an: Like those before you the verse. Abu Hurayrah said: The creative religion. And you plunged like those who plunged They said: O Messenger of God, as the Persians and Romans did? He said: Are there any people except them? This hadith has a corroborating evidence in Sahih.
9:70: The Almighty says, admonishing these hypocrites who denied the Messengers: Has there not come to you the report of those before you? That is, have you not heard the report of the nations who denied the Messengers before you? The people of Noah and what happened to them of the general drowning of all the people of the earth except for those who believed in His servant and Messenger Noah, peace be upon him, And Aad how they were destroyed by the barren wind when they denied Hud, peace be upon him, And Thamud how the blast took them when they denied Salih, peace be upon him, and hamstrung the she-camel, And the people of Abraham how God granted him victory over them and supported him with the miracles that appeared to them and destroyed their king, Nimrod bin Canaan bin Kush the Canaanite, may God curse him, And the people of Midian who are the people of Shuaib, peace be upon him, and how the earthquake and the torment of the Day of Shadow struck them, And the overturned ones the people of Lot who lived in cities, and He said in another verse: And the overturned ones are more inclined meaning the nation that is in seclusion, and it was said that it is the Their villages, which is Sodom, and the point is that God Almighty destroyed them all because they denied the Prophet of God, Lot, peace be upon him, and committed an immorality that no one in the world had ever committed before them. Their messengers came to them with clear proofs, meaning with decisive arguments and evidence. So God would not have wronged them, meaning by destroying them because He established proof against them by sending messengers and removing the causes. But they were wronging themselves, meaning by denying the messengers and opposing the truth, so they ended up in the torment and destruction that they ended up in.
9:71: When God the Almighty mentioned the reprehensible qualities of the hypocrites, He followed it up by mentioning the praiseworthy qualities of the believers, saying: And the believing men and believing women are allies of one another, meaning they support and assist one another as stated in the Sahih, The believer to the believer is like a building, some parts of which support others, and he interlaced his fingers. Also stated in the Sahih, “The example of the believers in their love and mercy for one another is like that of a single body: if one part of it is ill, the rest of the body responds to it with fever and sleeplessness.” And His statement, They enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, is like His statement, the Almighty, And let there arise out of you a community inviting to good, enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong, and His statement, And establish prayer and give zakah, meaning they obey God and are good to His creation. And obey God and His Messenger, meaning in what He commanded and refrained from what He forbade. Those - God will have mercy on them, meaning God will have mercy on whoever has these qualities. Indeed, God is Exalted in Might, meaning He exalts whoever obeys Him, for Glory be to God, to His Messenger, and to the believers. He is wise in allocating these attributes to them and singling out the hypocrites with their aforementioned attributes. He has wisdom in everything He does, blessed and exalted be He.
9:72: God Almighty tells us what He has prepared for the believers, men and women, of good things and eternal bliss in gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide eternally meaning they will remain there forever and good dwellings meaning well-built and well-established, as stated in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Abu Imran al-Jawni on the authority of Abu Bakr ibn Abi Musa Abdullah ibn Qays al-Ash’ari on the authority of his father who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Two gardens of gold, their vessels and everything in them, and two gardens of silver, their vessels and everything in them, and nothing will stand between the people and them looking at their Lord except the cloak of majesty on His face in the Garden of Eden.” And he said the same, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Indeed, for the believer in Paradise there is a tent made of a single hollow pearl, sixty miles long in the sky! The believer will have wives in it who will go around among them and they will not see each other.” They reported it in the two Sahihs, and in them also on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever believes in God and His Messenger, establishes prayer, and fasts Ramadan, then truly God will admit him into Paradise, whether he migrates in the cause of God or is detained in the land in which he was born.” They said: O Messenger of God, should we not inform the people? He said: “Indeed, in Paradise there are one hundred levels that God has prepared for those who strive in His cause. Between each two levels is the distance between the heavens and the earth. So if you ask God for something, ask Him for Al-Firdaws, for it is the highest level of Paradise and the middle of Paradise, and from it the rivers of Paradise flow, and above it is the Throne of the Most Merciful.” At-Tabarani, at-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah, on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam, on the authority of Ata’ ibn Yasar, on the authority of Mu’adh ibn Jabal, may God be pleased with him, I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say, and he mentioned something similar. Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Ubadah ibn al-Samit something similar. On the authority of Abu Hazim on the authority of Sahl ibn Sa`d who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The people of Paradise will see the rooms in Paradise just as you see a star in the sky. Both of them narrated it in their Sahihs. Then it should be known that the highest station in Paradise is a place called al-Wasilah because of its proximity to the Throne, and it is the dwelling place of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Paradise, as Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Ka`b, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When you send blessings upon me, then ask God to grant me al-Wasilah. It was said: O Messenger of God, what is al-Wasilah? He said: The highest station in Paradise, which none will attain except one man, and I hope that I am he. In Sahih Muslim, from the hadith of Ka’b ibn Alqamah: on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-Aas, that he heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “When you hear the muezzin, say what he says, then pray for me, for whoever prays for me once, God will pray for him ten times. Then ask God for intercession for me, for it is a position in Paradise that is not appropriate for anyone but one of God’s servants. And I hope that I will be that one, for whoever asks God for intercession for me, intercession will be granted to him on the Day of Resurrection.” Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Ahmad ibn Ali al-Abbar told us, al-Walid ibn Abd al-Malik al-Harrani told us, Musa ibn A’yan told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Dhi’b, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Ask God for intercession for me, for no servant asks for it for me in this world except that I will be a witness or intercessor for him on the Day of Resurrection. Narrated by al-Tabarani. In Musnad of Imam Ahmad, from the hadith of Sa`d ibn Mujahid al-Ta`i, from Abu al-Mudlah, from Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, he said: We said, O Messenger of God, tell us about Paradise, what is its structure? He said: “Bricks of gold and bricks of silver, its mortar is musk, its pebbles are pearls and rubies, and its soil is saffron. Whoever enters it will be blessed and will never be miserable, and will live forever and will never die, his clothes will never wear out and his youth will never fade.” It was narrated from Ibn `Umar, with a similar chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, and in al-Tirmidhi from the hadith of `Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq, from al-Nu`man ibn Sa`d, from `Ali, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: In Paradise there are rooms whose outside can be seen from their inside and whose inside can be seen from their outside. Then a Bedouin stood up and said: O Messenger of God, for whom are they? He said: For the one who speaks kindly, feeds the poor, fasts regularly, and prays at night while people are asleep. Then he said: A strange hadith. It was narrated by al-Tabarani from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Amr and Abu Malik al-Ash’ari, each of them from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a similar manner. Both chains of transmission are good and hasan. He believes that the questioner is Abu Malik al-Ash’ari, and God knows best. On the authority of Usamah ibn Zayd, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Is there anyone who is eager to go to Paradise? Paradise is not dangerous. By the Lord of the Kaaba, it is a shining light, a swaying fragrant plant, a lofty palace, a flowing river, ripe fruit, a beautiful wife, many garments, an eternal abode in a sound home, fruits, greenery, joy, and comfort in a high and splendid place.” They said: Yes, O Messenger of God, we are eager to go to it. He said: Say, ‘God willing.’ The people said: God willing. Narrated by Ibn Majah. And the Almighty’s saying: And the pleasure of God is greater means that God’s pleasure with them is greater, more sublime and more magnificent than what they are in of bliss, as Imam Malik, may God have mercy on him, said on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam, on the authority of Ata bin Yasar, on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God, the Almighty, says to the people of Paradise: O people of Paradise, and they say: At your service, our Lord, and at your pleasure, and goodness is in your hands. He says: Are you satisfied? They say: Why should we not be satisfied, O Lord, when you have given us what you have not given to any of your creation? He says: Shall I not give you something better than that? They say: O Lord, what is better than that? He says: I have bestowed upon you My pleasure, and I will never be angry with you after that.” They narrated it from the hadith of Malik. Abu Abdullah Al-Hussein bin Ismail Al-Muhammadi said: Al-Fadl Al-Raja’i told us, Al-Faryabi told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Muhammad bin Al-Munkadir, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When the people of Paradise enter Paradise, God, the Almighty, says: Do you desire anything so that I may give you more?” They say: O our Lord, what is better than what You have given us? He said: My pleasure is greater. Al-Bazzar narrated it in his Musnad from the hadith of Al-Thawri. Al-Hafiz Al-Dhiya Al-Maqdisi said in his book Sifat Al-Jannah: This, in my opinion, meets the criteria of Sahih, and God knows best.
9:73: God Almighty commanded His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to fight the infidels and hypocrites and to be harsh with them, as He commanded him to lower his wing for those believers who followed him, and He informed him that the destiny of the infidels and hypocrites is Hell in the Hereafter. It was mentioned earlier from the Commander of the Faithful, Ali bin Abi Talib, that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent with four swords: a sword for the polytheists, So when the sacred months have passed, kill the polytheists, a sword for the infidels of the People of the Book, “Fight those who do not believe in God or in the Last Day and do not consider unlawful what God and His Messenger have forbidden and do not adopt the religion of truth from among those who were given the Scripture until they pay the jizyah with willing submission,” a sword for the hypocrites, Fight the infidels and hypocrites, and a sword for the rebels, So fight those who rebel until they return to the command of God, and this requires that they fight with swords if they display hypocrisy, and this is the choice of Ibn Jarir. Ibn Masoud said about the verse: Fight the disbelievers and the hypocrites, he said: with his hand, and if he is unable to do so, then let him scowl at him. Ibn Abbas said: God commanded him to fight the disbelievers with the sword and the hypocrites with the tongue, and to remove gentleness from them. Ad-Dahhak said: Fight the disbelievers with the sword and be harsh with the hypocrites with words, which is fighting them. Muqatil and Ar-Rabi’ said something similar. Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: Fighting them means implementing the prescribed punishments on them. It may be said that there is no contradiction between these statements, because sometimes He holds them accountable for this and sometimes for that, according to the circumstances, and God knows best. And His statement: They swear by God that they did not say it, but they did say the word of disbelief and disbelieved after their Islam, Qatadah said: It was revealed about Abdullah bin Ubayy, and that was because two men, a Juhani and an Ansari, fought, and the Juhani attacked the Ansari, so Abdullah said to the Ansari: Will you not support your brother? By God, our example and that of Muhammad are only as the one who said: Fatten your dog and it will eat you, and he said: If we return to Medina, the more honorable will expel therefrom the more humble. A man from the Muslims went to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he sent for him and asked him, and he began to swear by God that he did not say anything, so God revealed this verse about him. Ismail bin Ibrahim bin Uqbah narrated on the authority of his uncle Musa bin Uqbah, who said: Abdullah bin Al-Fadl told me that he heard Anas bin Malik, may God be pleased with him, say: I was saddened by those of my people who were afflicted in Al-Harrah, so Zaid bin Arqam wrote to me and was informed of the severity of my sadness, mentioning that he heard the Messenger of God say: O God, forgive the Ansar and the sons of the Ansar. Ibn Al-Fadl was doubtful about the sons of the sons of the Ansar. Ibn Al-Fadl said: Anas asked some of those who were with him about Zaid bin Arqam, and he said: He is the one to whom the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God has fulfilled his permission for him. He said: That was when he heard a man from the hypocrites say while the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was delivering a sermon: If he is truthful, then we are worse than donkeys. Zaid bin Arqam said: So he is By God, you are truthful, and you are worse than a donkey. Then this was reported to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, but the speaker denied it, so God revealed this verse confirming what Zaid said, meaning his statement: They swear by God that they did not say the verse. Al-Bukhari narrated it in his Sahih on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Uways on the authority of Ismail bin Ibrahim bin Uqbah - until his statement - this is the one to whom God has fulfilled His permission, and perhaps what comes after it is from the statement of Musa bin Uqbah, and Muhammad bin Falih narrated it on the authority of Musa bin Uqbah with his chain of transmission: Then he said Ibn Shihab said, and he mentioned what comes after it on the authority of Musa on the authority of Ibn Shihab. What is well-known about this story is that it took place during the Battle of Banu Mustaliq, so perhaps the narrator made a mistake in mentioning the verse and wanted to mention something else, so he mentioned it. And God knows best. Al-Umawi said in his Maghazi: Muhammad bin Ishaq told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Abdullah bin Kaab bin Malik, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, who said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, arrived, my people seized me and said: You are a poet, so if you want, apologize to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, for some of the ailments, then it will be a sin for which you seek forgiveness from God. And he mentioned the hadith in full until he said: Among those who stayed behind from the hypocrites and the Qur’an was revealed about them, among them who were with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was Al-Jalas bin Suwaid bin Al-Samit, and he was married to Umm Umair bin Saad, and Umair was in his lap. So when the Qur’an was revealed and God reminded them of what He mentioned of what was revealed about the hypocrites, Al-Jalas said: By God, if this man is truthful in what he says, then we are worse than donkeys? Then Umair bin Saad heard him and said: By God, O Jalas, you are the most beloved of people to me, the best of those who are tested by me, and the most difficult for me to have something that I dislike reach you. You said something that if I mentioned it, it would disgrace you, and if I concealed it, it would destroy me, and one of them is easier for me than the other. So he walked to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and told him what Jalas had said. When Jalas heard about that, he went out until he came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and swore by God that he had not said what Umair bin Saad had said, and he had lied about me. So God Almighty revealed about him: They swear by God that they did not say it, but they did say the word of disbelief and disbelieved after their Islam to the end of the verse. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stopped him on it, and they claimed that Jalas had repented, and his repentance was good, and he had given up, and he gave... This is how it came in the hadith, connected to it, as if, God knows best, it was from the words of Ibn Ishaq himself, not from the words of Ka`b ibn Malik. Urwah ibn al-Zubayr said: This verse was revealed about al-Jalas ibn Suwaid ibn al-Samit. He and his wife’s son Mus`ab came from Quba’. Al-Jalas said: If what Muhammad brought is true, then we are worse than our donkeys that we are on. Mus`ab said: By God, O enemy of God, I will tell the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, what you said. So I came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I feared that it would be revealed in the Qur’an, or that a calamity would befall me, or that I would be confused by his sin. So I said: O Messenger of God, al-Jalas and I came from Quba’ and he said such and such. Had it not been for the fear that I would be confused by a sin or that a calamity would befall me, I would not have told you. He said: So he called al-Jalas and said: O Jalas, did you say what Mus`ab said? So he swore, and God revealed, They swear by God that they did not say it, the verse. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: The one who said that statement, as I have heard, was Al-Jalas ibn Suwaid ibn Al-Samit, and a man who was in his lap, called Umair ibn Saad, brought it up against him, and he denied it, so he swore by God that he did not say it. When the Quran was revealed about him, he repented and stopped, and his repentance was good, as I have heard. Imam Abu Ja`far ibn Jarir said: Ayyub ibn Ishaq ibn Ibrahim told me, `Abdullah ibn Raja` told us, Isra`il told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sitting in the shade of a tree and said, A man will come to you and look at you with the eyes of Satan, so when he comes, do not speak to him. They did not wait long before a blue-eyed man appeared, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called him and said, Why do you and your companions curse me? The man set out and brought his companions to him, and they swore by God that they had not said anything until he forgave them. Then God Almighty revealed, They swear by God that they had not said anything, the verse. And His saying, And they intended what they did not attain, it was said that it was revealed about Al-Jalas bin Suwaid, and that he intended to kill his wife’s son when he said, “I will inform the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.” And it was said about Abdullah bin Ubayy, that he intended to kill the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Suddi said: It was revealed about people who wanted to crown Abdullah bin Ubayy even though the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was not pleased. It was reported that a group of hypocrites intended to kill the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was in the Battle of Tabuk, on one of those nights while on the road, and they were about a dozen men. Ad-Dahhak said: This verse was revealed about them, and that is clear in what Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bayhaqi narrated in the book, Evidence of Prophethood, from the hadith of Muhammad bin Ishaq, from Al-A’mash, from Amr bin Murrah, from Abu Al-Bukhtari, from Hudhayfah bin Al-Yaman, may God be pleased with him, who said: I was holding the reins of The she-camel of the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) was led by me and Ammar was leading the she-camel, or I was leading him and Ammar was leading him, until we were at the pass, and there were twelve riders who had intercepted him on it. He said: So I alerted the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) about them, and he shouted at them, but they turned and fled. The Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) said to us: Do you recognize the people? We said: No, O Messenger of God, they were veiled, but we recognized the riders. He said: “These are the hypocrites until the Day of Resurrection. Do you know what they wanted?” We said: No. He said: “They wanted to jostle the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) on the pass and throw him from it.” We said: O Messenger of God, will you not send to their clans so that each tribe sends to you the head of their leader? He said: No, I hate for the Arabs to say among themselves that Muhammad fought with a people, and when God made him victorious through them, he turned to them and killed them. Then he said: O God, shoot them with the Dabilah.” We said: O Messenger of God, what is the Dabilah? He said: A meteor of fire that falls on the heart of one of them and he is destroyed. Imam Ahmad, may God have mercy on him, said: Yazid told us, Al-Walid bin Abdullah bin Jami’ told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Tufayl, who said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned from the Battle of Tabuk, he ordered a crier to call out: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, has taken Al-Aqaba, so no one else should take it. While the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was being led by Hudhayfah and Ammar was driving him, a group of veiled men approached on camels and deceived Ammar while he was driving the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ammar, may God be pleased with him, approached and struck the faces of the camels, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Hudhayfah, Here he is, until the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, dismounted. When he dismounted, he dismounted and Ammar returned. He said, O Ammar, do you recognize the people? He said: I recognized most of the camels, and the people were veiled.” He said: Do you know what they wanted? He said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: “They wanted to scare away the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from his mount and throw him down.” He said: So Ammar asked a man from the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: I ask you by God, how many do you know were the companions of Al-Aqaba? He said: Fourteen men. He said: If you are one of them, then there were fifteen. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, counted three of them. They said: By God, we did not hear the call of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and we did not know what the people wanted. So Ammar said: I bear witness that the remaining twelve are at war with God and His Messenger in this worldly life and on the Day when the witnesses will stand. And thus Ibn Lahi’ah narrated on the authority of Abu al-Aswad on the authority of Urwah ibn al-Zubayr something similar to this, and that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered the people to walk in the valley, and he, Hudhayfah, and Ammar ascended the pass. These vile men followed them while they were veiled, and they wanted to take the pass. So God informed the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, of their intention, so he ordered Hudhayfah to return to them and strike the faces of their mounts, so they were frightened and returned ugly. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, informed Hudhayfah and Ammar of their names and what they intended to do to kill him, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he ordered them to keep it a secret from them. And thus Yunus ibn Bakir narrated on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, except that he named a group of them, and God knows best. And this is what was narrated in the Mu'jam of At-Tabarani, as Al-Bayhaqi said. And what testifies to the authenticity of this story is what Muslim narrated: Zuhair bin Harb narrated to us, Abu Ahmad Al-Kufi narrated to us, Al-Walid bin Jami' narrated to us, Abu At-Tayyib narrated to us, he said: There was something between a man from the people of Al-'Aqabah and Hudhayfah, as happens between people, so he said: I ask you by God, how many were the people of Al-'Aqabah? He said: The people said to him: Tell him when he asked you? He said: We used to say that they were fourteen, so if you are one of them, then the people were fifteen, and I bear witness by God that twelve of them are at war with God and His Messenger in this worldly life and on the Day when the witnesses will stand, and three were excused, they said: We did not hear the caller of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, nor did we know what the people wanted. And he was walking in a lava field and said: The water is scarce, so no one should get there before me. So he found some people who had gotten there before him, so he cursed them that day. And what Muslim also narrated from the hadith of Qatadah from Abu Nadrah from Qays ibn Abbad from Ammar ibn Yasir, he said: Hudhayfah told me from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “Among my companions are twelve hypocrites who will not enter Paradise or smell its fragrance until a camel passes through the eye of a needle. Eight of them will be sufficient for you to be pierced by a lamp of fire that will appear between their shoulders until it bursts into their chests.” That is why Hudhayfah was called the one who had the secret that no one else knew, that is, the identification of a group of hypocrites, and they were these, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had informed him of them and no one else, and God knows best. And al-Tabarani translated in Musnad Hudhayfah the naming of the companions of al-Aqaba, then it was narrated from Ali ibn Abd al-Aziz from al-Zubayr ibn Bakkar that he said: They are Mu’tab ibn Qushirah, Wadi’ah ibn Thabit, Jad ibn Abdullah ibn Nabtal ibn al-Harith from Banu Amr ibn Awf, and al-Harith ibn Yazid al-Ta’i. Aws bin Qayzi, Al-Harith bin Suwaid, Saad bin Zarara, Qais bin Fahd, Suwaid bin Da’is from Bani Al-Habli, Qais bin Amr bin Sahl, Zaid bin Al-Lasit, and Salalah bin Al-Hamam, who are from Bani Qaynuqa’, declared Islam. God the Almighty says: And they did not resent them except because God and His Messenger enriched them from His bounty. That is, the Messenger had no sin in their view except that God enriched them with His blessing and bestowed happiness. If happiness had been completed for him, God would have guided them to what he brought, as the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to the Ansar: Did I not find you astray and God guided you through me? And you were divided and God united you through me? And you were poor and God enriched you through me. Whenever he said something, they said God and His Messenger believed. This formula is said when there is no sin, like His statement: And they resented them only because they believed in God. And his saying, peace be upon him, Ibn Jameel would not be blamed unless he was poor and God enriched him. Then God, the Blessed and Exalted, called them to repentance, saying, “If they repent, it will be better for them. But if they turn away, God will punish them with a painful punishment in this world and the Hereafter.” That is, if they continue on their path, God will punish them with a painful punishment in this world, that is, with killing, worry, and grief, and in the Hereafter, that is, with torment, humiliation, disgrace, and degradation. And they will have no protector or helper on earth. That is, they will have no one to make them happy or rescue them, who will bring them good or ward off evil from them.
9:74: God Almighty commanded His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to fight the infidels and hypocrites and to be harsh with them, as He commanded him to lower his wing for those believers who followed him, and He informed him that the destiny of the infidels and hypocrites is Hell in the Hereafter. It was mentioned earlier from the Commander of the Faithful, Ali bin Abi Talib, that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent with four swords: a sword for the polytheists, So when the sacred months have passed, kill the polytheists, a sword for the infidels of the People of the Book, “Fight those who do not believe in God or in the Last Day and do not consider unlawful what God and His Messenger have forbidden and do not adopt the religion of truth from among those who were given the Scripture until they pay the jizyah with willing submission,” a sword for the hypocrites, Fight the infidels and hypocrites, and a sword for the rebels, So fight those who rebel until they return to the command of God, and this requires that they fight with swords if they display hypocrisy, and this is the choice of Ibn Jarir. Ibn Masoud said about the verse: Fight the disbelievers and the hypocrites, he said: with his hand, and if he is unable to do so, then let him scowl at him. Ibn Abbas said: God commanded him to fight the disbelievers with the sword and the hypocrites with the tongue, and to remove gentleness from them. Ad-Dahhak said: Fight the disbelievers with the sword and be harsh with the hypocrites with words, which is fighting them. Muqatil and Ar-Rabi’ said something similar. He said: The people said to him: Tell him when he asked you? And he was walking in a lava field and said: The water is scarce, so no one should get there before me. So he found some people who had gotten there before him, so he cursed them that day. And what Muslim also narrated from the hadith of Qatadah from Abu Nadrah from Qays ibn Abbad from Ammar ibn Yasir, he said: Hudhayfah told me from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “Among my companions are twelve hypocrites who will not enter Paradise or smell its fragrance until a camel passes through the eye of a needle. Eight of them will be sufficient for you to be pierced by a lamp of fire that will appear between their shoulders until it bursts into their chests.” That is why Hudhayfah was called the one who had the secret that no one else knew, that is, the identification of a group of hypocrites, and they were these, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had informed him of them and no one else, and God knows best. And al-Tabarani translated in Musnad Hudhayfah the naming of the companions of al-Aqaba, then it was narrated from Ali ibn Abd al-Aziz from al-Zubayr ibn Bakkar that he said: They are Mu’tab ibn Qushirah, Wadi’ah ibn Thabit, Jad ibn Abdullah ibn Nabtal ibn al-Harith from Banu Amr ibn Awf, and al-Harith ibn Yazid al-Ta’i. Aws bin Qayzi, Al-Harith bin Suwaid, Saad bin Zarara, Qais bin Fahd, Suwaid bin Da’is from Bani Al-Habli, Qais bin Amr bin Sahl, Zaid bin Al-Lasit, and Salalah bin Al-Hamam, who are from Bani Qaynuqa’, declared Islam. God the Almighty says: And they did not resent them except because God and His Messenger enriched them from His bounty. That is, the Messenger had no sin in their view except that God enriched them with His blessing and bestowed happiness. If happiness had been completed for him, God would have guided them to what he brought, as the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to the Ansar: Did I not find you astray and God guided you through me? And you were divided and God united you through me? And you were poor and God enriched you through me. Whenever he said something, they said God and His Messenger believed. This formula is said when there is no sin, like His statement: And they resented them only because they believed in God. And his saying, peace be upon him, Ibn Jameel would not be blamed unless he was poor and God enriched him. Then God, the Blessed and Exalted, called them to repentance, saying, “If they repent, it will be better for them. But if they turn away, God will punish them with a painful punishment in this world and the Hereafter.” That is, if they continue on their path, God will punish them with a painful punishment in this world, that is, with killing, worry, and grief, and in the Hereafter, that is, with torment, humiliation, disgrace, and degradation. And they will have no protector or helper on earth. That is, they will have no one to make them happy or rescue them, who will bring them good or ward off evil from them.
9:75: God the Almighty says: And among the hypocrites are those who gave God their covenant and pledge, If He enriches him from His bounty, he will surely give in charity from his wealth and be among the righteous. But he did not fulfill what he said, nor was he truthful in what he claimed. So this action was followed by hypocrisy that resided in their hearts until the day they meet God the Almighty on the Day of Resurrection. We seek refuge in God from that. Many of the commentators, including Ibn Abbas and Al-Hasan Al-Basri, mentioned that the reason for the revelation of this noble verse was Tha'laba bin Hatib Al-Ansari. A hadith was narrated about him by Ibn Jarir here, and Ibn Abi Hatim from the hadith of Ma'an bin Rafa'ah from Ali bin Yazid from Abu Abd Al-Rahman Al-Qasim bin Abd Al-Rahman, the client of Abd Al-Rahman bin Yazid bin Mu'awiyah from Abu Umamah Al-Bahili from Tha'laba bin Hatib Al-Ansari, that he said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: Ask God to grant me wealth. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Woe to you, Tha'laba! A little that you give thanks for is better than a lot. He said: Then he said it again and said: Are you not satisfied to be like the Prophet of God? By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, if I wanted the mountains to move with me in gold and silver, they would move. He said: By the One Who sent you with the truth, if I call upon God and He provides me with wealth, I will give every person with a right his right. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O God, provide Tha`laba with wealth. He said: So he took sheep, and they grew like worms grow, and the city became too small for him, so he moved away from it and went down to one of its valleys until he began to pray the noon and afternoon prayers in congregation and leave everything else. Then they grew and multiplied, so he moved away until he stopped praying except the Friday prayers, and they grew like worms grow until he stopped the Friday prayers. He began to meet the riders on Friday to ask them about the report, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: What has Tha`laba done? They said: O Messenger of God, he took sheep, and the city became too small for him. So they informed him of his situation, and he said: Woe to Tha`laba, woe to Tha`laba, woe to Tha`laba. And God, the Most High, revealed the verse, Take from their wealth a charity, and the obligatory charity was revealed. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent two men to collect the charity from among the Muslims, a man from Juhayna and a man from Sulaym. He wrote to them how to collect the charity from the Muslims, and he said to them, Pass by Tha’laba and so-and-so - a man from Banu Sulaym - and take their charity. So they went out until they came to Tha’laba and asked him for the charity, and he read him the letter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said, “This is nothing but a tribute. This is nothing but a sister of the tribute. I do not know what this is.” They set out until they were done, then they returned to me. They set out and As-Salami heard about them, so he looked at the best teeth of his camels and set them aside for charity. Then he met them with them. When they saw them, they said, This is not obligatory upon you, and we do not want to take this from you. He said, Yes, take it, for my soul is content with that, and it is for God. So they took it from him and passed by the people and took the charity. Then they returned to Tha’laba. He said, Show me your letter. So he read it and said, “This is nothing but a tribute. This is nothing but a sister of the tribute. Go until I see my opinion.” So they set out until they came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. When he saw them, he said, Woe to Tha’laba, before he spoke to them, and he prayed for blessings for As-Salami. They told him what Tha’laba had done and what As-Salami had done. Then God, the Almighty, revealed, “And among them are those who made a covenant with God, ‘If He gives us from His bounty, we will surely give in charity. ’” The verse was with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and a man from among Tha’laba’s relatives heard that, so he went out until he came to him and said, Woe to you, Tha’laba! God has revealed concerning you. So and so, Tha`laba went out until he came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and asked him to accept his charity. He said: Woe to you, God has prevented me from accepting your charity. So he began to throw dirt on his head, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: This is your work, I ordered you but you did not obey me. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, refused to accept his charity, he returned to his home. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, died and did not accept anything from him. Then he came to Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, when he was appointed caliph and said: “You know my status with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and my position among the Ansar, so accept my charity.” Abu Bakr said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not accept it from you and refused to accept it.” So Abu Bakr died and did not accept it. When Umar may God be pleased with him took office, he came to him and said: O Commander of the Faithful, accept my charity. He said: Neither the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) nor Abu Bakr accepted it, and how can I accept it from you? So he died without accepting it. When Uthman may God be pleased with him took office, he came to him and said: Accept my charity. He said: Neither the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) nor Abu Bakr nor Umar accepted it, and how can I accept it from you? So he did not accept it from him. So Tha`laba died during the caliphate of Uthman. And the Almighty said: Because they broke their promise to God 2:10, meaning that hypocrisy became a consequence of their breaking their promise and lying, as in the two Sahihs on the authority of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) that he said: “The signs of a hypocrite are three: when he speaks, he lies; when he promises, he breaks his promise; and when he is entrusted, he betrays.” And there are many corroborating evidences for this, and God knows best. And His statement: Do they not know that God knows their secrets and their private conversations? The verse, the Most High informs us that He knows the secret and what is hidden, and that He knows their innermost thoughts even if they reveal that if they have money and give charity from it and are grateful for it, then God knows them better than they know themselves, because the Most High is the Knower of the unseen, meaning He knows everything that is hidden and witnessed, and every secret and private conversation, and He knows what is apparent and what is hidden.
