And the Almighty said: Because they broke their promise to God 2:10, meaning that hypocrisy became a consequence of their breaking their promise and lying, as in the two Sahihs on the authority of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) that he said: “The signs of a hypocrite are three: when he speaks, he lies; when he promises, he breaks his promise; and when he is entrusted, he betrays.” And there are many corroborating evidences for this, and God knows best. And His statement: Do they not know that God knows their secrets and their private conversations? The verse, the Most High informs us that He knows the secret and what is hidden, and that He knows their innermost thoughts even if they reveal that if they have money and give charity from it and are grateful for it, then God knows them better than they know themselves, because the Most High is the Knower of the unseen, meaning He knows everything that is hidden and witnessed, and every secret and private conversation, and He knows what is apparent and what is hidden.
9:79: This is also one of the characteristics of the hypocrites. No one is safe from their faultfinding and backbiting in all circumstances, not even those who give charity are safe from them. If one of them comes with a large sum of money, they say, "This is hypocrisy. But if he comes with something small, they say, God is independent of this man's charity." As narrated by Al-Bukhari, Ubaydullah bin Saeed told us, Abu Al-Nu'man Al-Basri told us, Shu'bah told us, on the authority of Sulayman, on the authority of Abu Wa'il, on the authority of Abu Mas'ud, may God be pleased with him, who said: When the verse of charity was revealed, we would carry loads on our backs. Then a man came and gave a large amount of charity, so they said, "He is a show-off. Then a man came and gave a Sa' of charity, so they said, God is independent of this man's charity. Then the verse was revealed, Those who backbite the voluntary ones." Muslim also narrated it in his Sahih from the hadith of Shu’bah, and Imam Ahmad said: Yazid told us, Al-Jariri told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Sulayl, who said: A man stopped us in our gathering in Al-Baqi’ and said: My father or my uncle told me that he saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Al-Baqi’ and he was saying: Whoever gives charity, I will bear witness for him on the Day of Resurrection. He said: So I took off one or two of my turban and I wanted to give them in charity, but that which overtakes the son of Adam overtook me, so I tied my turban, and a man came, the one I had never seen in Al-Baqi’ blacker than him, nor younger than him, nor darker than him, with a camel whose legs I had never seen in Al-Baqi’ more beautiful than any she-camel. He said: O Messenger of God, do you give charity? He said: Yes. He said: Here is this she-camel. A man nudged him and he said: This man gives this in charity, and by God, it is better than him. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, heard him and said: You have lied, rather he is better than you and it three times. Then he said: Woe to those who have hundreds of camels three times. They said: Except for whom, O Messenger of God? He said: Except for the one who says about wealth like this and like this. Then he put his hands together on his right and left, then he said: The ascetic who strives has succeeded three times. The ascetic in life, the one who strives in worship. Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding this verse: Abd al-Rahman bin Awf came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with forty ounces of gold, and a man from the Ansar came to him with a sa’ of food. Some of the hypocrites said: By God, Abd al-Rahman did not bring what he brought except to show off. They said: God and His Messenger do not need this sa’. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The Messenger of God went out to the people one day and called out to them to collect their charity. So the people collected their charity, then a man came from the last of them with a saa of dates and said: O Messenger of God, this is a saa of dates. I spent the whole night dragging water from a jug until I got two saa of dates. I kept one of them and brought you the other. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered him to scatter it among the charity. Some men mocked him and said: God and His Messenger are independent of this and they will not do anything with your saa. Then Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: Is there anyone left from the people of charity? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is no one left except you. Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf said to him: I have one hundred ounces of gold in charity. So Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, said to him: Are you mad? He said: I am not mad. He said: Did you do what you did? He said: Yes, I have eight thousand, as for the four thousand I lend to my Lord, and as for the four thousand, I have them, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: May God bless you for what you have withheld and what you have given. The hypocrites slandered him and said: By God, Abd al-Rahman did not give his gift except to show off, and they were lying. He was only doing it voluntarily. So God, the Almighty, revealed his excuse and the excuse of his poor friend who brought the saa’ of dates, so God, the Most High, said in His Book: Those who criticize the believers who give voluntarily in charity (al-Baqarah 2:17). This is how it was narrated from Mujahid and others. Ibn Ishaq said: Among the believers who gave voluntarily in charity were Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, who gave four thousand dirhams in charity, and Asim ibn Adi, the brother of Banu al-Ajlan. This is because the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, encouraged charity and urged it, so Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf stood up and gave four thousand in charity, and Asim ibn Adi stood up and gave one hundred wasqs of dates in charity. They slandered them and said: This is nothing but showing off. The one who gave charity with his effort was Abu Uqayl, the brother of Banu Anif al-Arashy, an ally of Banu Amr ibn Awf. He came. A sa` of dates, so he poured it into charity. They laughed at it and said: God is not in need of Abu Aqil’s sa`. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Talut ibn Abbad told us, Abu Awana told us, on the authority of Umar ibn Abi Salamah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Give charity, for I want to send an expedition. Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf came and said: O Messenger of God, I have four thousand, two thousand of which I will lend to my Lord and two thousand for my family. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: May God bless you in what you have given and bless you in what you have withheld. A man from the Ansar spent the night and acquired two sa’s of dates, so he said: O Messenger of God, I acquired two sa’s of dates, one sa’ of which I will lend to my Lord and one sa’ for my family. The hypocrites mocked him and said: He did not give what Ibn Awf gave except to show off. They said: Were not God and His Messenger independent of this sa’? Then God revealed, Those who criticize the believers who give voluntary charity and those who find only their effort, so they ridicule them, the verse. Then he narrated it on the authority of Abu Kamil on the authority of Abu Awana on the authority of Umar ibn Abi Salamah on the authority of his father, without a chain of transmission. He said, No one supported it except Talut. Imam Abu Ja`far ibn Jarir said: Ibn Wakee` told us, Zayd ibn al-Habbab told us on the authority of Musa ibn Ubaydah, Khalid ibn Yasar told me on the authority of Ibn Abi `Aqil on the authority of his father, who said: I spent the night carrying the Jarir on my back for two sa`s of dates. I went back with one of them to my family so that they could provide for them, and I came with the other to draw closer to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. I went to him and informed him, and he said, Sprinkle it in charity. He said, The people mocked and said, ‘God is independent of the charity of this poor man.’ Then God revealed, “Those who criticize the believers who give voluntary charity, the two verses. And thus al-Tabarani narrated it on the authority of Zayd ibn Habbab, and he said: Abu `Aqil’s name is Habbab, and it is said, ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn `Abdullah ibn Tha`labah. His saying: So they mock them, God mocks them. This is a way of responding to their bad deeds and mocking the believers, because the punishment is of the same kind as the deed, so He treated them as those who mocked them, in victory for the believers in this world, and He prepared for the hypocrites in the Hereafter a painful punishment, because the punishment is of the same kind as the deed.
9:80: God the Almighty informs His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that these hypocrites are not worthy of seeking forgiveness, and that even if he seeks forgiveness for them seventy times, God will not forgive them. It has been said that the seventy was mentioned to eliminate the need to seek forgiveness for them, because the Arabs in their speech styles mention seventy in an exaggerated manner, and do not intend to specify it or for what is more than that to be contrary to it. It has been said that it has an implication, as Al-Awfi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When this verse was revealed, ‘I hear my Lord has given me permission regarding them, so by God I will seek forgiveness for them more than seventy times, perhaps God will forgive them.’ So God, out of His intense anger with them, said: It is the same to them whether you seek forgiveness for them or do not seek forgiveness for them. Al-Sha’bi said that when Abdullah bin Ubayy became seriously ill, his son went to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: My father is dying, so I would like you to be present and pray over him. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: What is your name? He said: Al-Hubab bin Abdullah. He said: “Rather, you are Abdullah bin Abdullah. Al-Hubab is the name of a devil.” So he went with him until he witnessed him and put his shirt on him, which was covered in sweat, and prayed over him. It was said to him: Do you pray over him while he is a hypocrite? He said: “God said: ‘If you ask forgiveness for them seventy times,’ I will ask forgiveness for them seventy and seventy and seventy.” This was also narrated on the authority of Urwah bin Az-Zubayr, Mujahid bin Jubayr, Qatadah bin Di’amah, and Ibn Jarir narrated it with his chains of transmission.
9:81: God Almighty says, blaming the hypocrites who stayed behind from the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the Battle of Tabuk, and were happy to stay behind after his departure, and they hated to strive with him with their wealth and their lives in the cause of God, and they said that is, some of them to each other, Do not go forth in the heat, because the departure for the Battle of Tabuk was in intense heat when the shade and fruits were pleasant, so this is why they said, Do not go forth in the heat. God Almighty said to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say to them, The fire of Hell, which you will go to because of your disobedience, is more intense in heat than the heat from which you fled, in fact, more intense in heat than the fire, as Imam Malik said on the authority of Abu al-Zinad on the authority of al-A’raj on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The fire of the children of Adam that you kindle is one part of seventy parts of the fire of Hell. They said: O Messenger of God, is that sufficient? He said: It is superior to it by sixty-nine parts. They included it in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Malik with it. Imam Ahmad said: Sufyan told us on the authority of Abu al-Zinad on the authority of al-A’raj on the authority of Abu Hurayrah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: This fire of yours is one part of seventy parts of the fire of Hell, and it has been struck in the sea twice, and were it not for that, God would not have made any benefit in it for anyone. This is also an authentic chain of transmission. Imam Abu ‘Isa al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah narrated on the authority of Abbas al-Duri, and on the authority of Yahya ibn Abi Bakr on the authority of Sharik on the authority of ‘Asim on the authority of Abu Salih on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God kindled the fire for a thousand years until it turned red, then He kindled it for a thousand years until it turned white, then He kindled it for a thousand years until it turned black, so it is black like a dark night.” Then al-Tirmidhi said: I do not know of anyone who attributed it to the Prophet except Yahya, that is what he said. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh narrated it on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Muhammad on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Mukram on the authority of ‘Ubaydullah ibn Sa’d on the authority of his uncle on the authority of Sharik. He is the son of Abdullah Al-Nakha’i. Ibn Mardawayh also narrated, on the authority of Mubarak bin Fadala, on the authority of Thabit bin Anas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: A Fire whose fuel is men and stones. He said: “It was kindled for a thousand years until it turned white, a thousand years until it turned red, and a thousand years until it turned black. It is black like the night, and its flame does not shine.” Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani narrated on the authority of Tamam bin Nujayj, and there is disagreement about it, on the authority of al-Hasan, on the authority of Anas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: If a spark were in the east - meaning from the fire of Hell - its heat would be felt by those in the west. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la narrated, on the authority of Ishaq bin Abi Isra’il, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah al-Haddad, on the authority of Hisham bin Hassan, on the authority of Muhammad bin Shabib, on the authority of Ja’far bin Abi Wahshiyyah, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If there were in this mosque a hundred thousand or more, and among them was a man from the people of Hell, and he breathed and his breath struck them, the mosque and those in it would burn. Strange. Al-A’mash said on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of al-Nu’man bin Bashir, who said: He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The least punished of the people of Hell on the Day of Resurrection will be the one who has two sandals and two straps of Hellfire from which his brain will boil as a cauldron boils. He will not think that any of the people of Hell will be more severely punished than him, and he will be the least punished of them.” Both of them included it in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Al-A’mash. Muslim also said: Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah told us, Yahya bin Abi Katheer told us, Zuhair bin Muhammad told us, on the authority of Suhayl bin Abi Salih, on the authority of Al-Nu’man bin Abi Ayyash, on the authority of Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The least punished of the people of Hell on the Day of Resurrection will be the one who wears two sandals of fire from which his brain will boil from the heat of his sandals. Imam Ahmad said: Yahya told us, on the authority of Ibn ‘Ajlan, I heard my father, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The least punished of the people of Hell will be the man who has two sandals from which his brain will boil. This is a good, strong chain of transmission, its men meet the criteria of Muslim, and God knows best. The hadiths and prophetic narrations on this subject are many, and God, the Most High, said: In His Noble Book: No indeed! It is a blazing Fire, tearing away the skin. And the Almighty said: “Boiling water will be poured over their heads, melting thereby what is in their bellies and their skins. And for them are maces of iron. Whenever they wish to get out of it out of distress, they will be returned to it and [they will be] declared, ‘Taste the punishment of the Burning Fire.’” And the Almighty said: “Indeed, those who disbelieve in Our verses - We will drive them into a Fire. Every time their skins are roasted through, We will replace them with other skins so they may taste the punishment.” And the Almighty said in this noble verse: Say, ‘The fire of Hell is more intense in heat, if they only understood.’ That is, if they understood and comprehended, they would have set out with the Messenger in the way of God in the heat to protect themselves from the heat of Hell, which is many times more intense than this. But as the other said: Like someone who seeks refuge from the heat of the sun into the fire The other said: You spent your life on a diet, fearing the cold and the hot. It would have been better for you to avoid sins as you fear Hellfire. Then the Almighty, the Majestic, said, threatening these hypocrites for their actions: So let them laugh a little verse. Ibn Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The world is little, so let them laugh in it as much as they want. Then when the world ends and they turn to God, the Almighty, the Majestic, they will resume weeping that will never stop. This is what Abu Razin, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Al-Rabi’ bin Khathim, Awn Al-Uqayli, and Zayd bin Aslam said. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la Al-Mawsili said: Abdullah bin Abdul Samad bin Abi Khidash told us, Muhammad bin Jubayr told us, on the authority of Ibn Al-Mubarak, on the authority of Imran bin Zayd, Yazid Al-Raqashi told us, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “O people, weep, and if you do not weep, then pretend to weep, for the people of Hell will weep until their tears run down their faces like streams, until the tears stop and blood flows and the eyes become sore. If ships were to be thrown into it, they would sail.” It was narrated by Ibn Majah from the hadith of Al-A’mash on the authority of Yazid Al-Raqashi on his authority. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr bin Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Abi Al-Dunya: Muhammad bin Abbas told us, Hammad Al-Jazari told us, on the authority of Zaid bin Rafi’, who said: When the people of Hell enter Hell, they will cry tears for a time, then they will cry pus for a time. He said: The keepers will say to them, “O group of wretched ones, you stopped crying in the home whose people were shown mercy in this world. Do you find anyone today to call upon for help?” He said: They will raise their voices, “O group of fathers, mothers and children, we came out of the graves thirsty, and we were thirsty the entire time we were standing, and we are thirsty today, so pour on us some water or some of what God has provided for you.” They will call out for forty years, but He will not answer them, then He will answer them, You will remain, and they will despair of all good.

9:83: The Almighty says, commanding His Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, If God returns you meaning God returns you from this expedition to a group of them Qatada said: He mentioned to us that they were twelve men and they ask your permission to go out meaning with you to another expedition then say, ‘You will never go out with me, nor will you fight with me an enemy’ meaning as a punishment and a reprimand for them. Then He explained that by saying: You were satisfied to sit back the first time. This is like the Almighty’s saying: And We will turn their hearts and their eyes away just as they did not believe in it the first time (al-An’am 2:10). The recompense for a bad deed is the bad deed after it, just as the reward for a good deed is the good deed after it, like His saying in the Umrah of al-Hudaybiyyah Those who stayed behind will say, when you set out to take the spoils (al-An’am 2:10). And the Almighty’s saying: So sit with those who stayed behind. Ibn Abbas said: meaning the men who stayed behind from the battles. Qatada said: So sit with those who stayed behind meaning with the women. Ibn Jarir said: This is not correct because the plural of women is not with the letter ya and the letter nun. If women were meant, he would have said: So sit with those who stayed behind or those who stayed behind. And the statement of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, is preferred.
9:84: God the Almighty commanded His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to disavow the hypocrites and not to pray for any of them when they die, and not to stand at their graves to seek forgiveness for them or pray for them because they disbelieved in God and His Messenger and died upon that. This is a general ruling for everyone who is known to be a hypocrite, even though the reason for the revelation of the verse was about Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul, the leader of the hypocrites, as Al-Bukhari said: Ubayd bin Ismail told us on the authority of Abu Usamah on the authority of Ubayd God on the authority of Nafi’ on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: When Abdullah bin Ubayy died, his son Abdullah bin Abdullah came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and asked him to give him his shirt to shroud his father in it, so he gave it to him. Then he asked him to pray for him, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up to pray for him, so Umar stood up and took hold of the Messenger of God’s garment, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, will you pray for him when your Lord has forbidden you to pray for him? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God has given me a choice and said: ‘Whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them, if you ask forgiveness for them…’” Seventy times, God will not forgive them. And I will add to the seventy. He said, He is a hypocrite. He said, “So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed over him, and God, the Almighty, revealed the verse, “And never pray over any of them who dies, nor stand at his grave.” Muslim narrated it in the same way on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah on the authority of Abu Usamah Hammad bin Usamah on his authority. Then Al-Bukhari narrated it on the authority of Ibrahim bin Al-Mundhir on the authority of Anas bin Ayyad on the authority of Ubaidullah, who is Ibn Umar Al-Umari on his authority. He said, So he prayed over him, and we prayed with him, and God revealed the verse, “And never pray over any of them who dies, on his authority. Imam Ahmad narrated it in the same way on the authority of Yahya bin Saeed Al-Qattan on the authority of Ubaidullah on his authority. It was also narrated from the same hadith of Omar bin Al-Khattab in a similar manner. Imam Ahmad said: Yaqub told us, my father told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, Al-Zuhri told me, on the authority of Ubaidullah bin Abdullah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: I heard Omar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, say: When Abdullah bin Ubayy died, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was called to pray over him. He stood over him, and when he stood over him intending to pray, I moved until I stood in front of him and said: O Messenger of God, is it the enemy of God, Abdullah bin Ubayy, who said on such and such a day, and he counted his days? He said: And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was smiling, until I said a lot to him, then he said: “Stay away from me, Omar, for I was given a choice and I chose. It was said to me, ‘Seek forgiveness for them’” verse. If I knew that if I increased the number of seventy, he would be forgiven, I would have increased it.” He said: Then he prayed over him and walked with him and stood at his grave until he finished. He said: I was amazed at my audacity towards the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and God and His Messenger know best. He said: By God, it was only a short time before these two verses were revealed: And never pray over any of them who dies Surat al-Bara’ah. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not pray over a hypocrite after that, nor did he stand at his grave until God, the Almighty, took him. And thus it was narrated by al-Tirmidhi in his Tafsir from the hadith of Muhammad ibn Ishaq from al-Zuhri with it, and he said: It is good and authentic. Al-Bukhari narrated it from Yahya ibn Bakir from al-Layth from Uqayl from al-Zuhri with it, and he mentioned something similar. He said: Stay away from me, O Umar. So when I continued with him, he said: I was given a choice and I chose, and if I knew that if I increased the number of seventy, he would be forgiven, I would have increased it. He said: So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed over him and left. It was only a short time before the two verses of Bara’ah were revealed: And never pray over any of them who dies, nor stand at his grave. His grave "the verse, then I was amazed after that at my audacity towards the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, knows best. Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad bin Abi Ubaid told us, Abdul Malik told us on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr on the authority of Jabir, who said: When Abdullah bin Ubay died, his son came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, if you do not come to him, we will not continue to be taunted by this. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to him and found him put in his grave, so he said: "Why did you not put him in?" So he was taken out of his grave and spat on him from his saliva from his head to his feet and put his shirt on him. Al-Nasa'i narrated it on the authority of Abu Dawud al-Harrani on the authority of Ya'la bin Ubaid on the authority of Abdul Malik, who is the son of Abu Sulayman, on his authority. Al-Bukhari said: Abdullah bin Uthman told us, Ibn Uyaynah told us on the authority of Amr, he heard Jabir bin Abdullah say: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to Abdullah bin Ubay after he was put in his grave, so he ordered him to be taken out and placed on his knees and breathed on him from his saliva and put his shirt on him, and God knows best. It was also narrated in more than one place by Muslim and Al-Nasa’i from more than one source, on the authority of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah. Imam Abu Bakr Ahmad bin Amr bin Abdul Khaliq Al-Bazzar said in his Musnad: Amr bin Ali told us, Yahya told us, Mujalid told us, Amer told us, Jabir H told us, and Yusuf bin Musa told us, Abdul Rahman bin Mughra Al-Dawsi told us, Mujalid told us on the authority of Al-Sha’bi on the authority of Jabir who said: When the leader of the hypocrites, Yahya bin Saeed, died in Medina, he recommended that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, pray over him. His son came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: My father recommended that he be shrouded in your shirt. These words are in the hadith of Abdul Rahman bin Mughra. Yahya said in his hadith: So he prayed over him and dressed him in his shirt, and God Almighty revealed: And never pray over any of them who dies, nor stand at his grave. Abdul Rahman added: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, took off his shirt and gave it to him and walked, prayed over him and stood at his grave. Gabriel, peace be upon him, came to him when he turned away and said: And never pray over any of them who dies, nor stand at his grave. Its chain of transmission is sound, and what precedes it supports it. Imam Abu Ja`far al-Tabari said: Ahmad ibn Ishaq told us, Ahmad told us, Hammad ibn Salamah told us, on the authority of Yazid al-Raqashi, on the authority of Anas, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wanted to pray over Abdullah ibn Ubayy, so Gabriel took hold of his garment and said, And never pray over any of them who dies, nor stand at his grave. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya`la narrated it in his Musnad from the hadith of Yazid al-Raqashi, and it is weak. Qatada said: Abdullah bin Ubayy was sent to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was sick. When he entered upon him, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: Love for the Jews has destroyed you. He said: O Messenger of God, I only sent to you to ask forgiveness for me, and I did not send to you to rebuke me. Then Abdullah asked him to give him his shirt to shroud his father in, so he gave it to him and prayed over him and stood at his grave. Then God Almighty revealed: And never pray over any of them who dies 1:13. Some of the early Muslims mentioned that he gave him his shirt because when Abdullah bin Ubayy came to Al-Abbas, he asked for a shirt for himself, but he could not find anything similar to it except the garment of Abdullah bin Ubayy, because he was large and tall. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did that to him as a reward for him. And God knows best. That is why the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, after this noble verse was revealed to him, did not pray over any of the hypocrites nor did he stand at their graves, as Imam Ahmad said: Yaqub told us, my father told us on the authority of his father, Abdullah bin Abi Qatada told me on the authority of his father who said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was called to a funeral, he would ask about it. If it was praised well, he would stand and pray over it. If it was otherwise, he would say to its people, Do what you want with it, and he would not pray over it. Umar bin Al-Khattab would not pray over the funeral of someone whose situation he did not know until Hudhayfah bin Al-Yaman prayed over it, because he knew the most prominent hypocrites, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had informed him of them. That is why he was called the one who kept the secret that no one else knew, that is, any of the Companions. Abu Ubaid said in the book Al-Gharib in the hadith of Omar that he wanted to pray over a man’s funeral, but Hudhayfah stopped him as if he wanted to prevent him from praying over it. Then he narrated from some of them that Marz in the language of the people of Yamamah means pinching with the tips of the fingers, and when God the Almighty forbade praying over the hypocrites and standing at their graves to ask forgiveness for them, this action was one of the greatest acts of worship for the believers, so it was legislated, and in doing it there is a great reward as proven in the Sahihs and other books from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever attends a funeral until he prays over it will have one qirat, and whoever attends it until it is buried will have two qirats. It was said: What are the two qirats? He said, The smaller of them is like Uhud. As for standing at the grave of a believer when he dies, Abu Dawud narrated: Ibrahim bin Musa al-Razi told us, Hisham told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Buhair, on the authority of Hani’, who is Abu Sa’id al-Barbari, the client of Uthman bin Affan, on the authority of Uthman, may God be pleased with him, who said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, finished burying the dead, he would stand over him and say, Seek forgiveness for your brother and ask for him to be steadfast, for he is being questioned now. Abu Dawud, may God have mercy on him, was the only one to narrate it.
9:85: This verse has been interpreted in a similar way, praise be to God.
9:86: The Almighty says, denouncing and condemning those who stayed behind from jihad and refused it despite being able to do so and having the means and time. They asked the Messenger for permission to stay behind and said, Leave us to be with those who stay behind. They accepted for themselves the shame and staying in the country with the women, who were the ones who stayed behind after the army had left. When war broke out, they were the most cowardly of people, and when it was safe, they were the most talkative of people, as the Almighty said about them in another verse: "But when fear comes, you will see them looking at you, their eyes rolling like one who is fainting from death. But when the fear departs, they lash you with sharp tongues." That is, their tongues rose with sharp, strong words in safety, and in war they are the most cowardly of things, as the poet said: In peace there are harsh and rough men, and in war there are those who are like women and are effeminate? And God Almighty said in another verse: “And those who believe say, ‘Why was a surah not sent down?’ But when a clear surah is sent down and fighting is mentioned therein, you see those in whose hearts is disease looking at you with the look of one fainting from death. So it is more appropriate for them * Obedience and honorable speech. But when the matter is decided, if they had been true to God, it would have been better for them.” And His statement, And their hearts are sealed, means because of their refusal to fight and go out with the Messenger in the way of God, so they do not understand, meaning they do not understand what is good for them so they do it, nor what is harmful to them so they avoid it.

9:88: When God Almighty mentioned the sin of the hypocrites and explained His praise of the believers and their fate in the afterlife, He said, But the Messenger and those who believed with him strove to the end of the two verses explaining their condition and their fate, and His saying, And those will have good things meaning in the afterlife in the gardens of Paradise and the highest ranks.
9:89: When God Almighty mentioned the sin of the hypocrites and explained His praise of the believers and their fate in the afterlife, He said, But the Messenger and those who believed with him strove to the end of the two verses explaining their condition and their fate, and His saying, And those will have good things meaning in the afterlife in the gardens of Paradise and the highest ranks.
9:90: Then the Almighty explained the situation of those who had excuses for not participating in Jihad, who came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, apologizing to him and explaining to him their weakness and inability to go out, and they were from the Arab tribes around Medina. Ad-Dahhak said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he used to read and the excused ones came with a light pronunciation and say: they are the people with excuses. And Ibn Uyaynah narrated on the authority of Humayd on the authority of Mujahid, Ibn Ishaq said: It has reached me that they were a group of Banu Ghaffar, Khafaf bin Ima’ bin Rukhsah. This statement is the most apparent in the meaning of the verse, because after this he said: And those who denied God and His Messenger sat down, meaning they did not come to apologize. And Ibn Jurayj said on the authority of Mujahid: And the excuse-makers from among the bedouins came, meaning a group of Banu Ghaffar came and apologized, but God did not excuse them. And this is what Al-Hasan, Qatadah, and Muhammad bin Ishaq said, and the first statement is more apparent, and God knows best, because of what we have mentioned of his statement after it: And those who denied God and His Messenger sat down, meaning others from among the bedouins sat down from coming to apologize, then He threatened them with a painful punishment, saying: A painful punishment will befall those among them who disbelieved.
9:91: Then the Almighty mentioned the excuses for which there is no blame on the one who sits back from fighting, so He mentioned from them what is necessary for the person and cannot be separated from him, which is the weakness in the constitution that prevents the fighter from fighting in jihad, and from it blindness and lameness and the like, and for this reason He began with it, and from it what is incidental due to an illness that has befallen him in his body that has kept him from going out in the way of God or due to his poverty that prevents him from preparing for war, so there is no blame on these people if they sit back and advise while they are sitting and do not stir up trouble among the people or discourage them while they are doing good in this state, and for this reason He said: "There is no blame upon the doers of good, and God is Forgiving and Merciful." Sufyan al-Thawri said on the authority of Abdul Aziz bin Rafi' on the authority of Abu Thamamah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The disciples said, O Spirit of God, tell us about the one who advises God? He said, The one who gives preference to the right of God over the right of people, and if two matters happen to him or the matter of this world and the matter of the Hereafter appear to him, he begins with that which is for the Hereafter and then devotes himself to that which is for this world. Al-Awza’i said: The people went out to pray for rain, and Bilal bin Sa’d stood up among them, praised and thanked God, then said: O people present, do you not admit to wrongdoing? They said: Yes, O God. He said: O God, we hear you say: There is no blame upon the doers of good. O God, we have admitted to wrongdoing, so forgive us, have mercy upon us, and give us rain. He raised his hands, and they raised their hands and gave rain. Qatada said: This verse was revealed about A’idh bin Amr Al-Muzani. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Hisham bin Ubaidullah Al-Razi told us, Ibn Jabir told us, on the authority of Ibn Farwah, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Abi Laila, on the authority of Zaid bin Thabit, who said: I was writing for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I was writing Bara’ah, and I was putting the pen to my ear when we were commanded to fight. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was looking at what was being revealed to him, when a blind man came and said: How can I be, O Messenger of God, when I am blind? Then the verse There is nothing upon the weak was revealed. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding this verse, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered the people to go out to fight with him, so a group of his companions came to him, among them Abdullah bin Mughaffal bin Muqrin Al-Muzni, and they said: O Messenger of God, give us some mounts. He said to them: By God, I cannot find anything to mount you on. So they turned away crying, and it was difficult for them to sit out the jihad while they could not find any money or a mount. When God saw their eagerness to love Him and His Messenger, He revealed their excuse in His Book, saying, There is no blame upon the weak until His saying, for they do not know. Mujahid said in His saying, nor upon those who, when they come to you that you may carry them, that it was revealed about Banu Muqrin of Muzaynah. Muhammad ibn Ka’b said: There were seven men from Banu Amr ibn Awf: Salim ibn Umair, from Banu Waqif: Harmi ibn Amr, from Banu Mazin ibn al-Najjar: Abd al-Rahman ibn Ka’b, who was called Abu Layla, from Banu al-Mu’alla: Salman ibn Sakhr, from Banu Salamah: Amr ibn Ghanmah and Abdullah ibn Amr al-Muzani. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said in the context of the Battle of Tabuk: Then some men from the Muslims came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they were the crying ones, and they were seven men from the Ansar and others, from Banu Amr ibn Awf: Salim ibn Umair, Aliyah ibn Zayd, the brother of Banu Haritha, Abu Layla: Abd al-Rahman ibn Ka’b, the brother of Banu Mazin ibn al-Najjar, Amr ibn al-Hamam ibn al-Jamuh, the brother of Banu Salamah, and Abdullah ibn al-Mughaffal al-Muzani. Some people say: Rather, he is Abdullah bin Amr Al-Muzani, and Harami bin Abdullah, the brother of Banu Waqif, and Ayyad bin Sariyah Al-Fazari, so they carried the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they were in need, so he said, I do not find anything to carry you on. They turned away, their eyes overflowing with tears, grieving that they did not find anything to spend. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Omar bin Al-Awdi told us, Wakee’ told us, on the authority of Al-Rabi’, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: You have left behind in Medina people who did not spend anything, nor cross a valley, nor attain anything from the enemy, except that they shared with you in the reward. Then he recited: And there is no blame upon those who, when they came to you for mounts, you said, ‘I find nothing on which to mount you,’ the verse. The origin of the hadith is in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Anas, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: In Medina there are people who did not cross a valley or travel a journey except that they were with you. They said, And they are in Medina? He said: Yes, they were held back by an excuse. Imam Ahmad said: Waki’ told us, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Abu Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “You left behind in Madinah men who did not cross a valley or take a road without sharing in the reward with you. They were held back by illness.” Muslim and Ibn Majah narrated it through various chains of transmission on the authority of Al-A’mash. Then God, the Most High, responded to the blame of those who asked permission to stay behind even though they were rich, and rebuked them for their contentment with being with the women who stayed behind in the tents. And God has sealed their hearts so they do not know.

Al-Awza’i said: The people went out to pray for rain, and Bilal bin Sa’d stood up among them, praised and thanked God, then said: O people present, do you not admit to wrongdoing? They said: Yes, O God. He said: O God, we hear you say: There is no blame upon the doers of good. O God, we have admitted to wrongdoing, so forgive us, have mercy upon us, and give us rain. He raised his hands, and they raised their hands and gave rain. Qatada said: This verse was revealed about A’idh bin Amr Al-Muzani. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Hisham bin Ubaidullah Al-Razi told us, Ibn Jabir told us, on the authority of Ibn Farwah, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Abi Laila, on the authority of Zaid bin Thabit, who said: I was writing for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I was writing Bara’ah, and I was putting the pen to my ear when we were commanded to fight. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was looking at what was being revealed to him, when a blind man came and said: How can I be, O Messenger of God, when I am blind? Then the verse There is nothing upon the weak was revealed. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding this verse, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered the people to go out to fight with him, so a group of his companions came to him, among them Abdullah bin Mughaffal bin Muqrin Al-Muzni, and they said: O Messenger of God, give us some mounts. He said to them: By God, I cannot find anything to mount you on. So they turned away crying, and it was difficult for them to sit out the jihad while they could not find any money or a mount. When God saw their eagerness to love Him and His Messenger, He revealed their excuse in His Book, saying, There is no blame upon the weak until His saying, for they do not know. Mujahid said in His saying, nor upon those who, when they come to you that you may carry them, that it was revealed about Banu Muqrin of Muzaynah. Muhammad ibn Ka’b said: There were seven men from Banu Amr ibn Awf: Salim ibn Umair, from Banu Waqif: Harmi ibn Amr, from Banu Mazin ibn al-Najjar: Abd al-Rahman ibn Ka’b, who was called Abu Layla, from Banu al-Mu’alla: Salman ibn Sakhr, from Banu Salamah: Amr ibn Ghanmah and Abdullah ibn Amr al-Muzani. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said in the context of the Battle of Tabuk: Then some men from the Muslims came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they were the crying ones, and they were seven men from the Ansar and others, from Banu Amr ibn Awf: Salim ibn Umair, Aliyah ibn Zayd, the brother of Banu Haritha, Abu Layla: Abd al-Rahman ibn Ka’b, the brother of Banu Mazin ibn al-Najjar, Amr ibn al-Hamam ibn al-Jamuh, the brother of Banu Salamah, and Abdullah ibn al-Mughaffal al-Muzani. Some people say: Rather, he is Abdullah bin Amr Al-Muzani, and Harami bin Abdullah, the brother of Banu Waqif, and Ayyad bin Sariyah Al-Fazari, so they carried the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they were in need, so he said, I do not find anything to carry you on. They turned away, their eyes overflowing with tears, grieving that they did not find anything to spend. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Omar bin Al-Awdi told us, Wakee’ told us, on the authority of Al-Rabi’, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: You have left behind in Medina people who did not spend anything, nor cross a valley, nor attain anything from the enemy, except that they shared with you in the reward. Then he recited: And there is no blame upon those who, when they came to you for mounts, you said, ‘I find nothing on which to mount you,’ the verse. The origin of the hadith is in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Anas, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: In Medina there are people who did not cross a valley or travel a journey except that they were with you. They said, And they are in Medina? He said: Yes, they were held back by an excuse. Imam Ahmad said: Waki’ told us, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Abu Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “You left behind in Madinah men who did not cross a valley or take a road without sharing in the reward with you. They were held back by illness.” Muslim and Ibn Majah narrated it through various chains of transmission on the authority of Al-A’mash. Then God, the Most High, responded to the blame of those who asked permission to stay behind even though they were rich, and rebuked them for their contentment with being with the women who stayed behind in the tents. And God has sealed their hearts so they do not know.
9:94: God Almighty informed about the hypocrites that if they return to the city, they will apologize to them. Say, ‘Do not apologize, we will never believe you.’ That is, we will not believe you. God has already informed us of your report. That is, God has informed us of your conditions. And God will see your deeds and His Messenger. That is, He will reveal your deeds to the people in this world. Then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and He will inform you of what you used to do. That is, He will inform you of your deeds, both good and bad, and He will reward you for them. Then He informed about them that they will swear to you, apologizing so that you will turn away from them, so do not rebuke them. So turn away from them, looking down on them, for they are unclean, that is, filthy and impure in their inner selves and beliefs. Their abode in the Hereafter is Hell, as a reward for what they used to earn, that is, of sins and transgressions. He informed that if they are pleased with them because of their oath to them, then God is not pleased with the wicked people. That is, those who go outside of the obedience of God and the obedience of His Messenger, for wickedness is going outside, and from it The mouse is called a foysqa because it comes out of its hole to cause corruption. It is said that the date is foysqat if it comes out of its sleeve.

9:97: God the Almighty informed us that among the Bedouins there are disbelievers, hypocrites and believers, and that their disbelief and hypocrisy are greater than others, more severe and more deserving, that is, more deserving of their not knowing the limits of what God has revealed to His Messenger, as Al-A'mash said on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: A Bedouin sat with Zaid bin Suhan while he was talking to his companions, and his hand had been injured on the day of Nahavand. The Bedouin said: By God, your talk pleases me, but your hand makes me doubt. Zaid said: What makes you doubt my hand, is it the left? The Bedouin said: By God, I do not know whether they cut off the right or the left? Zaid bin Suhan said: God has spoken the truth: The Bedouins are more severe in disbelief and hypocrisy and more likely not to know the limits of what God has revealed to His Messenger. Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Rahman bin Mahdi told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Musa, on the authority of Wahb bin Munabbih, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Whoever lives in the desert is rude, whoever follows game is heedless, and whoever comes to the ruler is tempted. Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa’i narrated it through various chains of transmission on the authority of Sufyan al-Thawri, and al-Tirmidhi said: It is hasan ghareeb, and we do not know it except from the hadith of al-Thawri. Since roughness and rudeness were among the people of the desert, God did not send a Messenger from them, but rather the mission was from the people of the villages, as God the Almighty said: And We did not send before you, [O Muhammad], except men to whom We revealed, from the people of the towns. When that Bedouin presented that gift to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he returned it to him in multiples until he was satisfied, he said: I was thinking of not accepting a gift except from a Qurayshi, a Thaqafi, an Ansari or a Dawsi, because these people used to live in the cities of Mecca. And Taif, Medina and Yemen, they are more gentle in character than the Bedouins because of the harshness in the Bedouins’ nature. The Hadith of the Bedouin about kissing the child Muslim said: Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah and Abu Kurayb told us: Abu Usamah and Ibn Numayr told us on the authority of Hisham on the authority of his father on the authority of Aisha who said: Some Bedouins came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: Do you kiss your children? They said: Yes. They said: But by God, we do not kiss. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: And what do you have control over if God has taken mercy away from you? And Ibn Numayr said: Mercy from your heart. And His saying, And God is All-Knowing, All-Wise, meaning, He is All-Knowing of who deserves to be taught faith and knowledge. He is All-Wise in what He has divided among His servants of knowledge and ignorance, faith and disbelief and hypocrisy. He is not questioned about what He does because of His knowledge and wisdom. And the Most High informed us that among them are some who take what they spend meaning in the way of God as a loss meaning a fine and a loss and he waits for you to have bad consequences meaning, he awaits accidents and calamities for you upon them is a bad consequence meaning, it is reflected back to them and evil is circling them and God is All-Hearing, All-Knowing meaning, He hears the supplications of His servants and He is All-Knowing of who deserves victory and who deserves to be let down. And His saying, And among the desert Arabs are those who believe in God and the Last Day and take what they spend as means of drawing near to God and prayers of the Messenger this is the praised section of the desert Arabs, and they are those who take what they spend in the way of God as means of drawing near to God and seek thereby the supplication of the Messenger for them Indeed, it is a means of drawing near to God meaning, indeed, that will happen to them “God will admit them into His mercy. Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful.”

9:100: God the Almighty informs us of His pleasure with the first of the Muhajireen and Ansar and those who followed them in righteousness, and their pleasure with Him for what He has prepared for them of gardens of bliss and eternal bliss. Al-Sha'bi said: The first of the Muhajireen and Ansar are those who witnessed the Pledge of Ridwan in the year of Al-Hudaybiyyah. Abu Musa Al-Ash'ari, Sa'id bin Al-Musayyab, Muhammad bin Sirin, Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: They are those who prayed towards the two Qiblahs with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Muhammad bin Ka'b Al-Qurazi said: Umar bin Al-Khattab passed by a man reciting this verse, "And the first of the Muhajireen and the Ansar," so Umar took him by the hand and said: Who taught you this? He said: Ubayy bin Ka'b. He said: Do not leave me until I take you to him. When he came to him, Umar said: Did you teach this verse like this? He said: Yes. He said: And did you hear it from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace? He said: Yes. He said: I used to think that we were raised to a height that no one after us would reach. My father said: This verse is confirmed in the beginning of Surat al-Jumuah 62:And others of them have not yet joined them, and He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise. And in Surat al-Hashr 59:And those who came after them the verse, and in al-Anfal 8:And those who believed after them and emigrated and fought with you the verse. Ibn Jarir narrated it. He said: It was mentioned on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Basri that he used to recite it with the Ansar raised in apposition to and the first forerunners. God Almighty has informed us that He is pleased with the first forerunners from the Muhajireen and the Ansar and those who followed them in righteousness. So woe to whoever hates them or curses them or hates or curses some of them, especially the master of the companions after the Messenger and the best of them and the most excellent of them, I mean the greatest friend and greatest caliph Abu Bakr bin Abi Quhafah, may God be pleased with him. For the betrayed group of the Rafidah are hostile to the best of the companions and hate them and curse them. God forbid from that. This indicates that their minds are upside down and their hearts are inverted. So where are these people from the faith in the Qur’an when they insult those with whom God is pleased? As for the Sunnis, they are pleased with those with whom God is pleased and insult those whom God and His Messenger insulted. They are loyal to those who are loyal to God and hostile to those who are hostile to God. They are followers, not innovators, and they follow examples, not innovators. For this reason, they are the successful party of God and His believing servants.
9:101: The Almighty informs His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, that among the Arab tribes around Medina there are hypocrites, and among the people of Medina there are also hypocrites who are recalcitrant to hypocrisy, meaning they have become accustomed to it and persist in it. From this it is said that a rebellious devil or a rebellious person is said to have rebelled against God, meaning he has become arrogant and haughty. His statement, You do not know them, We know them, does not contradict the statement of the Almighty, And if We willed, We could show them to you, and you would know them by their mark, and you will surely know them by the tone of their speech, because this is a matter of identifying them by characteristics by which they are known, not that he knows all of the hypocrites and doubters with him specifically. He knew that there were hypocrites among some of the people of Medina whom he mixed with, even though he saw them morning and evening. Evidence of this is the soundness of what Imam Ahmad narrated in his Musnad where he said: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, Shu`bah told us on the authority of al-Nu`man ibn Salim on the authority of a man on the authority of Jubayr ibn Mut`im, may God be pleased with him, who said: I said: O Messenger of God, they claim that we have no reward in Mecca. He said: Your rewards will come to you, even if you were in a fox’s hole. He leaned his head towards the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said, There are hypocrites among my companions. This means that some hypocrites and slanderers may say things that are not true, and this is the speech that Jubayr ibn Mut’im heard. It was mentioned in the interpretation of his statement, and they intended what they did not attain, that he, may God bless him and grant him peace, informed Hudhayfah of the names of fourteen or fifteen hypocrites. This is a specification that does not require that he knew their names and identities, all of them. And God knows best. Al-Hafiz Ibn Asakir narrated in the biography of Abu Omar Al-Bayrouti on the authority of Hisham bin Ammar: Sadaqah bin Khalid told us, Ibn Jaber told us, an old man in Beirut whose nickname was Abu Omar told me, I think he told me on the authority of Abu Al-Darda’ that a man called Harmalah came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: Faith is here, and he pointed with his hand to his tongue, and hypocrisy is here, and he pointed with his hand to his heart, and he did not remember God except a little, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O God, make for him a tongue that remembers, and a heart that is grateful, and provide him with my love and the love of those who love me, and turn his affair to goodness. He said: O Messenger of God, I had companions from among the hypocrites and I was a leader among them, so should I not bring them to you? He said: Whoever comes to us, we will ask forgiveness for him, and whoever persists, God is more deserving of it, and do not tear anyone’s curtain. He said: And Abu Ahmad al-Hakim narrated it likewise on the authority of Abu Bakr al-Baghdadi on the authority of Hisham ibn Ammar on his authority. And Abd al-Razzaq said: Muammar informed us on the authority of Qatadah regarding this verse that he said: What is the matter with people who are forced to teach people? So-and-so is in Paradise and so-and-so is in Hell. So if you ask one of them about himself, he says, I do not know. By my life, you know yourself better than you about the conditions of the people. And you have taken on something that the prophets before you did not take on. The Prophet of God, Noah, peace be upon him, said: And I do not know what they used to do. And the Prophet of God, Shu`ayb, peace be upon him, said: “What remains of God is better for you, if you are believers. And I am not a guardian over you.” And God, the Most High, said to His Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him: Do not teach them, We know them. Al-Suddi said on the authority of Abu Malik on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding this verse, he said: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, stood up as a preacher on Friday and said: “Go out, so-and-so, for you are a hypocrite. Go out, so-and-so, for you are a hypocrite.” So he was taken out of the mosque. Some of them were disgraced, so Umar came while they were leaving the mosque, so he hid from them out of shame that he did not attend the Friday prayer and he thought that the people had left, and they hid from Umar thinking that he had known about their affair, so Umar came and entered the mosque and found that the people had not prayed, so a man from the Muslims said to him: Be happy, Umar, God has disgraced the hypocrites today. Ibn Abbas said: This is the first punishment when he expelled them from the mosque, and the second punishment is the punishment of the grave, and Al-Thawri said something similar on the authority of Al-Suddi on the authority of Abu Malik. Mujahid said in his statement, We will punish them twice, meaning killing and captivity. He said in a narration, With hunger and the torment of the grave, then they will be returned to a great torment. Ibn Jurayj said, The torment of this world and the torment of the grave, then they will be returned to a great torment in the Fire. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said, A torment in this world and a torment in the grave. Abd Al-Rahman bin Zaid said, As for the torment in this world, it is wealth and children. He recited the statement of God Almighty, “So let not their wealth or their children impress you. God only intends to punish them with them in the life of this world.” These calamities are a torment for them, and for the believers they are a reward. And a torment in the Hereafter in the Fire. Then they will be returned to a great torment, he said, The Fire. Muhammad bin Ishaq said, We will punish them twice, he said, “It is what I have heard of what they are in regarding the matter of Islam and what enters them of wrath from that without reckoning, then their torment in the graves when they reach them, then the great torment to which they will be returned is the torment of the Hereafter and eternity in it.” Saeed said, on the authority of Qatada, in his statement, We will punish them twice, “The torment of this world and the torment of the grave,” Then they will be returned to a great torment, and he mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, confided to Hudhayfah twelve hypocrites. He said, Six of them will be sufficed by the plague, a lamp from the fire of Hell that will take hold of one of their shoulders until it reaches his chest, and six will die a natural death. It was mentioned to us that when a man died whom he thought was one of them, Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, would look at Hudhayfah and if he prayed over him, well and good, otherwise he would leave him. It was mentioned to us that Umar said to Hudhayfah, I ask you by God, am I one of them? He said, No, and I will not believe anyone of them after you.
9:102: When the Almighty explained the state of the hypocrites who stayed behind from the battles out of aversion, denial and doubt, He began to explain the state of the sinners who stayed behind from the battles out of laziness and inclination towards comfort, while believing and confirming the truth. He said, And others have acknowledged their sins, meaning they acknowledged them and confessed them between themselves and their Lord, and they have other good deeds that mixed these with those. These are under the pardon and forgiveness of God. Although this verse was revealed about specific people, it is general for all sinners, erring, mixed and polluted. Mujahid said that it was revealed about Abu Lubabah when he said to Banu Qurayzah: It is the slaughter and he pointed with his hand to his throat. Ibn Abbas said, And others was revealed about Abu Lubabah and a group of his companions who stayed behind from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the Battle of Tabuk. Some of them said: Abu Lubabah and five with him, and it was said seven with him, and it was said nine with him. So when he returned The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, during his expedition, tied themselves to the pillars of the mosque and swore that none but the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would release them. When God revealed this verse, And others have acknowledged their sins, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, released them and forgave them. Al-Bukhari said: Mu’ammil bin Hisham told us, Ismail bin Ibrahim told us, Awf told us, Abu Raja’ told us, Samurah bin Jundub told us: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to us, “Two men came to me tonight and sent me away. They took me to a city built of bricks of gold and bricks of silver. We were met by men, half of whose appearance was as beautiful as you have ever seen, and half of whose appearance was as ugly as you have ever seen. They said to them, ‘Go and fall into that river.’ So they fell into it and then returned to us with that evil gone from them and they became in the best appearance. They said to me, ‘This is the Garden of Eden and this is your home.’ They said, ‘As for the people who were half handsome and half ugly, they mixed good deeds with bad deeds. God forgave them.’” This is how Al-Bukhari narrated it. Briefly explaining this verse.
9:103: God Almighty commanded His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to take from their wealth a charity to purify and sanctify them with it. This is general, even though some of them attributed the pronoun in their wealth to those who confessed their sins and mixed good deeds with bad ones. For this reason, some of the Arab tribes who withheld zakat believed that paying zakat to the imam was not permissible, but rather this was specific to the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace. For this reason, they used to cite God Almighty’s saying: Take from their wealth a charity verse. This interpretation and corrupt understanding were refuted by Abu Bakr al-Siddiq and the rest of the Companions, who fought them until they paid zakat to the Caliph as they used to pay it to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Abu Bakr al-Siddiq said: By God, if they withheld from me a she-goat - and in another narration a hobble - which they used to pay to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, I would fight them for withholding it. His saying, And pray for them, means pray for them and seek forgiveness for them, as Muslim narrated in his Sahih on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Awfa, who said: When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was visited, With the charity of a people, he prayed for them, so my father brought him his charity and said: O God, pray for the family of Abu Awfa. In another hadith, a woman said: O Messenger of God, pray for me and my husband, so he said: May God bless you and your husband. And his saying: Indeed, your prayers are a comfort to them. Some of them read your prayers in the plural and others read indeed, your prayers in the singular. A comfort to them. Ibn Abbas said: Mercy for them. Qatada said: Dignity. And his saying: And God is All-Hearing, meaning of your supplication. Knowing, meaning who deserves that from you and who is worthy of it. Imam Ahmad said: We were told by Wakee’, we were told by Abu Al-Umais on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Amr bin Utbah on the authority of Ibn Hudhayfah on the authority of his father that when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed for a man, it would befall him and his son and his son’s son. Then he narrated it on the authority of Abu Na’im on the authority of Mis’ar on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Amr bin Utbah on the authority of Ibn Hudhayfah. Mis’ar said: And he mentioned it once on the authority of Hudhayfah that the prayer of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would reach a man, his son, and his son’s son. And His statement, Do they not know that it is God who accepts repentance from His servants and takes the charities? This is an incitement to repentance and charity, each of which erases sins, purifies them, and obliterates them. And God the Almighty informed us that whoever repents to Him, He will accept his repentance. And whoever gives charity from lawful earnings, God the Almighty accepts it with His right hand and increases it for its owner until a date becomes like Mount Uhud, as came in the hadith from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as Al-Thawri and Waki’ both said on the authority of Ibad bin Mansour on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Muhammad, that he heard Abu Hurairah say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God accepts charity and takes it with His right hand and increases it for one of you as one of you increases his foal, until a morsel becomes like Mount Uhud. And the confirmation of that is in the Book of God the Almighty: Do they not know that it is God who accepts repentance from His servants and takes the charities? And His statement, God obliterates interest and increases charities. Al-Thawri and Al-A’mash said, both on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Sa’ib on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Qatadah. He said: Abdullah bin Masoud, may God be pleased with him, said that charity falls into the hand of God Almighty before it falls into the hand of the beggar. Then he recited this verse: Do they not know that it is God who accepts repentance from His servants and takes the charities? Ibn Asakir narrated in his history in the biography of Abdullah bin Al-Shaer Al-Sakaski Al-Dimashqi, who was originally from Homs, and was one of the jurists. He narrated from Muawiyah and others. Hawshab bin Saif Al-Sakaski Al-Himsi narrated from him that he said: The people went on a raid in the time of Muawiyah, may God be pleased with him, and Abd Al-Rahman bin Khalid bin Al-Walid was in charge of them. A Muslim man took away one hundred Roman dinars. When the army returned, he regretted it and went to the emir, but he refused to accept it from him and said: The people have dispersed and I will not accept it from you until you bring it to God on the Day of Resurrection. The man began to ask the companions to say the same thing to him. When he arrived in Damascus, he went to Muawiyah to accept it from him, but he refused. He left him crying and urging God to restore it. He passed by Abdullah bin Al-Shaer Al-Sakaski and said to him: What makes you cry? So he mentioned his matter to him, and he said to him: Are you my obedient one? He said: Yes. So he said: Go to Muawiyah and tell him to accept from me your fifth, and give him twenty dinars, and look at the remaining eighty and give them in charity on behalf of that army, for God accepts the repentance of His servants, and He knows their names and their places. So the man did, and Muawiyah, may God be pleased with him, said: For me to have given him this fatwa is dearer to me than everything I own. Good man.
