So the man did, and Muawiyah, may God be pleased with him, said: For me to have given him this fatwa is dearer to me than everything I own. Good man.
9:105: Mujahid said: This is a threat from God Almighty to those who disobey His commands, that their deeds will be presented to Him, the Blessed and Exalted, and to the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to the believers. This will inevitably happen on the Day of Resurrection, as He said: On that Day you will be exposed, nothing of yours will be hidden. And He, the Most High, said: On the Day when secrets will be exposed. And He, the Most High, said: And what is in the breasts will be revealed. And God, the Most High, may reveal this to people in this world, as Imam Ahmad said: Hasan ibn Musa told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, Diraj told us, on the authority of Abu al-Haytham, on the authority of Abu Sa’id, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: If one of you were to work in a solid rock that had no door or window, God would bring forth his work for the people, whatever it was. It has been reported that the deeds of the living are shown to the dead from among their relatives and clans in the intermediate realm, as Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: As-Salt ibn Dinar told us, on the authority of al-Hasan, on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Your deeds are shown to your relatives and clans in their graves. If they are good, they will rejoice in them, and if they are not, they will say: O God, inspire them to work in obedience to You.” And Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of someone who heard Anas. He said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Your deeds are shown to your relatives and your dead clans. If they are good, they rejoice in them, but if they are not, they say: O God, do not cause them to die until You guide them as You have guided us.” Al-Bukhari said: Aisha may God be pleased with her said: If you are impressed by the good deeds of a Muslim, then say: Work, and God will see your deeds, and so will His Messenger and the believers. A similar hadith was narrated. Imam Ahmad said: Yazid narrated to us, Humayd narrated to us, on the authority of Anas, that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “There is no harm in being impressed by someone until you see how he ends up, for a worker works for a period of his life or a part of his life doing good deeds, and if he died while doing that he would enter Paradise, then he turns and does bad deeds. And a servant may work for a part of his life doing bad deeds, and if he died while doing that he would enter Hell, then he turns and does good deeds. And if God wants good for a servant, He uses him before his death.” They said: O Messenger of God, how does He use him? He said: He guides him to do good deeds, then He takes him while doing them. Imam Ahmad is the only one to narrate this from this source.
9:106: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ikrimah, Ad-Dahhak and others said: They are the three who stayed behind, that is, did not repent, and they are Murarah bin Ar-Rabi’, Ka’b bin Malik and Hilal bin Umayyah. They stayed behind from the Battle of Tabuk among a group of those who stayed behind out of laziness and inclination towards ease, preservation, good fruits and shade, not out of doubt and hypocrisy. A group of them tied themselves to the pillars as Abu Lubabah and his companions did, and a group did not do that, and they are the three mentioned. So the repentance of those was revealed before those, and those were delayed from repentance, until the following verse was revealed, which is His saying: God has already forgiven the Prophet, the Muhajireen and the Ansar 17:20, And the three who stayed behind until the earth became too narrow for them with all its vastness 17:20, as will be explained in the hadith of Ka’b bin Malik. His saying: Either He will punish them or He will forgive them 17:20, that is, they are under God’s forgiveness. If He wills, He will do this to them, and if He wills, He will do that to them, but His mercy prevails over His wrath. And God is Knowing. “Wise” means He knows who deserves punishment and who deserves forgiveness. He is wise in His actions and words. There is no god but Him and no lord but Him.
9:107: The reason for the revelation of these noble verses is that before the arrival of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, there was in Medina a man from the Khazraj called Abu Amir the monk. He had become a Christian in the pre-Islamic era and studied the knowledge of the People of the Book. He was a worshipper in the pre-Islamic era and had great honor among the Khazraj. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, arrived as an immigrant to Medina and the Muslims gathered around him and Islam became a high word and God made them victorious on the day of Badr, the accursed Abu Amir shone his light and showed hostility and declared it, and fled to the infidels of Mecca from the polytheists of Quraysh, siding with them in fighting the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. They gathered with those who agreed with them from the tribes of the Arabs and arrived in the year of Uhud. What happened to the Muslims happened and God Almighty tested them, and the outcome was for the righteous. This immoral man had dug holes between the two lines, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, fell into one of them and was injured that day, wounding his face, breaking his lower right front tooth, and splitting his head, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him. And peace be upon him, and Abu Amir advanced at the beginning of the duel to his people from the Ansar and addressed them and won them over to his support and agreement, and when they knew his words they said: May God not bless you, you wicked person, you enemy of God, and they attacked him and cursed him, so he returned saying: By God, evil has befallen my people after me, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had called him to God before his flight and read to him from the Qur’an, but he refused to convert to Islam and rebelled, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed against him that he would die far away, an outcast, and this prayer reached him, and that is because when the people finished with Uhud, and he saw the matter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, rising and appearing, he went to Heraclius, the king of the Romans, to seek his support against the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he promised him and hoped for him and stayed with him, and wrote to a group of his people from the Ansar from the people of hypocrisy and doubt, promising them and hoping that he would come with an army with which he would fight the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and defeat him and turn him back from what he was in, and he ordered them to build a fortress for him to come to them from him to deliver his letters and be As an ambush for him if he came to them after that, so they began to build a mosque adjacent to the Quba Mosque, so they built it and made it perfect and finished it before the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, left for Tabuk. They came and asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to come to them and pray in their mosque so that they could use his prayer in it as evidence of his approval and confirmation. They mentioned that they had only built it for the weak and the sick among them on a winter night, so God protected him from praying in it, so he said: We are on a journey, but when we return, God willing. So when he, peace be upon him, returned to Medina from Tabuk, and there was only a day or part of a day between him and it, Gabriel came down to him with the report of the Mosque of Harm and what its builders had relied on of disbelief and division among the group of believers in their mosque, the Quba Mosque, which had been founded from the first day on piety. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent to that mosque someone to demolish it before his arrival in Medina, as Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse, they are people from the Ansar who built a mosque, so Abu Amir said to them: Build a mosque and prepare with whatever strength and weapons you can, for I am going to Caesar, the king of the Romans, and I will bring Roman soldiers and expel Muhammad and his companions. When they finished their mosque, they came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said to him: We have finished building our mosque, so we would like you to pray in it and supplicate for blessings for us. So God Almighty revealed: Do not stand in it ever until His saying: the wrongdoers. And this was also narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, Mujahid, Urwah bin Az-Zubayr, Qatadah, and more than one of the scholars. Muhammad bin Ishaq bin Yasar said, on the authority of Az-Zuhri, Yazid bin Ruman, Abdullah bin Abi Bakr, Asim bin Umar bin Qatadah, and others, they said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came, meaning from Tabuk, until he stopped at Dhi Awan, a town between it and Medina, an hour of the day, and the people of the Mosque of Harm were there. They came to him while he was preparing for Tabuk and said: O Messenger of God, we have built a mosque for those who are sick and in need, and for rainy nights and winter nights, and we would like you to come and pray for us in it. He said: I am on the verge of a journey and busy, or as the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If we were to arrive, God willing, we would come to you and pray for you in it. When he arrived at Dhi Awan, report of the mosque reached him, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called Malik ibn al-Dakhshum, the brother of Banu Salim ibn Awf, and Ma’n ibn Adi, or his brother Amir ibn Adi, the brother of Balajlan, and said: Go to this mosque whose people are oppressing it, and demolish it and burn it. So they left quickly until they reached Banu Salim ibn Awf, who were the people of Malik ibn al-Dakhshum. Malik said to Ma'n: Give me time until I bring you fire from my family. So his family entered and he took a palm frond and set it on fire. Then they went out running until they entered the mosque and its people were in it. They burned it and demolished it and dispersed from it. And what was revealed about them in the Qur'an was revealed: And those who took a mosque for the purpose of causing harm and disbelief until the end of the story. It was built by twelve men: Khadham bin Khalid from Banu Ubayd bin Zayd, one of Banu Amr bin Awf, from whose house the mosque of Al-Shaqaq was removed, Tha’laba bin Hattab from Banu Ubayd and a client of Banu Umayyah bin Zayd, Mu’tab bin Qushair from Banu Dhubay’ah bin Zayd, Abu Habeeba bin Al-Az’ar from Banu Dhubay’ah bin Zayd, Ibad bin Hanif, the brother of Sahl bin Hanif from Banu Amr bin Awf, Haritha bin Aamer and his sons Mujammi’ bin Haritha and Zayd bin Haritha and Nabtal Al-Harith, who are from Banu Dhubay’ah, and Mukhraj, who are from Banu Dhubay’ah, Bajad bin Othman, who is from Banu Dhubay’ah, Wadi’ah bin Thabit, and the clients of Banu Umayyah, the people of Abu Lubabah bin Abdul Mundhir. And His statement, And they will swear, meaning those who built it, We intended nothing but good, meaning we intended nothing by building it but good and kindness to the people. God Almighty said, And God bears witness that they are liars, meaning in what they intended and what they intended. They only built it to harm the Quba Mosque, and to disbelieve in God, and to divide the believers, and to lie in wait for those who had fought God and His Messenger before, namely Abu Amir the wicked one who was called the monk, may God curse him. And His statement, Never stand in it, is a prohibition to him, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the nation that follows him in that, from standing in it, meaning praying in it, ever. Then he urged him to pray in the Quba Mosque, which was founded from the first day of its construction on piety, which is obedience to God and obedience to His Messenger, and a gathering of the believers and a stronghold and refuge for Islam and its people. For this reason, God Almighty said: A mosque founded on piety from the first day is more worthy for you to stand in it. The context is in reference to the Quba Mosque. For this reason, it was stated in the authentic hadith that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Prayer in the Quba Mosque is like an Umrah. In the authentic hadith, it is stated that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to visit the Quba Mosque riding and walking. In the hadith, it is stated that when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, built and founded it upon his first arrival and descent upon Banu Amr ibn Awf, it was Gabriel who appointed the direction of the qiblah for him. And God knows best. Abu Dawud said: Muhammad ibn al-Ala’ told us, Mu’awiyah ibn Hisham told us, on the authority of Yunus ibn al-Harith, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Abi Maymunah, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “This verse was revealed about the people of Quba’: ‘In it are men who love to purify themselves’ - he said: They used to clean themselves with water, so this verse was revealed about them.” At-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah narrated it on the authority of Yunus ibn al-Harith, and it is weak. At-Tirmidhi said: It is strange from this source. At-Tabarani said: Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Ma’mari told us, Muhammad ibn Hamid al-Razi told us, Salamah ibn al-Fadl told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: When this verse was revealed: ‘In it are men who love to purify themselves’ - the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent for ‘Uwaim ibn Sa’idah and said: ‘What is this purification for which God has praised you?’ He said: O Messenger of God, no man or woman among us has ever left the toilet without washing his private parts or, he said, his anus. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: This is it. Imam Ahmad said: Hussein bin Muhammad told us, Abu Uwais told us, Shurahbil told us on the authority of Uwaim bin Sa’idah al-Ansari, that he told him that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to them in the Quba Mosque and said: God Almighty has praised you well for purification in the story of your mosque, so what is this purification with which you purify yourself? They said: By God, O Messenger of God, we do not know anything, except that we had Jewish neighbors who used to wash their backsides after defecating, so we washed as they did. Ibn Khuzaymah narrated it in his Sahih. Hisham said on the authority of Abdul Hamid Al-Madani on the authority of Ibrahim bin Ismail Al-Ansari: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Uwaim bin Sa’idah: “What is this that God praised you for? ‘Therein are men who love to purify themselves’ verse. They said: O Messenger of God, we wash our backsides with water.” Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad bin ‘Amara Al-Asadi told me, Muhammad bin Sa’d told us on the authority of Ibrahim bin Muhammad on the authority of Shurahbil bin Sa’d, who said: I heard Khuzaymah bin Thabit say: This verse was revealed: ‘Therein are men who love to purify themselves, and God loves those who purify themselves’. He said: They used to wash their backsides after defecating. Another hadith Imam Ahmad bin Hanbal said: Yahya bin Adam told us, Malik, meaning Ibn Mughul, told us, I heard Sayyar Abu Al-Hakam, on the authority of Shahr bin Hawshab, on the authority of Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Salam, who said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, arrived, meaning Quba, he said, “God Almighty has praised you for purification. Will you not tell me?” He meant his statement, In it are men who love to purify themselves. They said, O Messenger of God, we find it written for us in the Torah to clean ourselves with water. A group of the Salaf have stated that it is the Quba Mosque. It was narrated by Ali bin Abi Talha on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and it was narrated by Abdul Razzaq on the authority of Muammar Al-Zuhri on the authority of Urwah bin Al-Zubayr. Atiyah Al-Awfi, Abdul Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam, Al-Sha’bi, and Al-Hasan Al-Basri said, and Al-Baghawi narrated it on the authority of Saeed bin Jubayr and Qatadah. It was mentioned in the authentic hadith that the mosque of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, which is in the heart of Madinah is the mosque that was founded on piety, and this is correct. There is no contradiction between the verse and this, because if the mosque of Quba was founded on piety from the first day, then it is more appropriate and more appropriate for it to be the mosque of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. For this reason, Imam Ahmad bin Hanbal said in his Musnad: Abu Na’im told us, Abdullah bin Amir Al-Aslami told us on the authority of Imran bin Abi Anas, on the authority of Sahl bin Sa’d, on the authority of Ubay bin Ka’b that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The mosque that was founded on piety is this mosque of mine. Ahmad is the only one to narrate it. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: We were told by Wakee’, we were told by Rabia bin Othman Al-Taymi, on the authority of Imran bin Abi Anas, on the authority of Sahl bin Sa’d Al-Sa’idi, who said: Two men differed during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding the mosque that was founded on piety. One of them said it was the mosque of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the other said it was the mosque of Quba. So they came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and asked him, and he said: It is this mosque of mine. Ahmad also transmitted it alone. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Musa bin Dawud told us, Laith told us, on the authority of Imran bin Abi Anas, on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Saeed Al-Khudri, may God be pleased with him, who said: Two men disputed about the mosque that was founded on piety from the first day. One of them said it was the Quba Mosque, and the other said it was the mosque of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, It is this mosque of mine. Ahmad alone transmitted it. Another way Imam Ahmad said: Ishaq bin Isa told us, Laith told us, Imran bin Abi Anas told me, on the authority of Ibn Abi Saeed, on the authority of his father, who said: Two men disputed about the mosque that was founded on piety from the first day. One man said, It is the mosque of Quba, and the other said, “It is the mosque of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.” The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, It is my mosque. And this is how it was narrated by al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa’i on the authority of Qutaybah on the authority of al-Laith, and al-Tirmidhi authenticated it, and Muslim narrated it as will come. Another way Imam Ahmad said: Yahya told us on the authority of Anis bin Abi Yahya, my father told me: I heard Abu Saeed Al-Khudri say: Two men, a man from Banu Khudra and a man from Banu Amr bin Awf, disagreed about the mosque that was founded on piety. Al-Khudri said it was the mosque of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Al-Amri said it was the mosque of Quba. So they came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and asked him about that, so he said: It is this mosque of the mosque of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said in that meaning the mosque of Quba. Another way Imam Ahmad said: Abu Ja`far ibn Jarir said: Ibn Bashar told us, Yahya ibn Sa`id told us, Hamid al-Kharrat al-Madani told us: I asked Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Sa`id and said: How did you hear your father say about the mosque that was founded on piety? He said: I came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and entered upon him in the house of one of his wives and said: O Messenger of God, where is the mosque that was founded on piety? He said: So he took a handful of pebbles and threw them on the ground, then he said: This is your mosque. Then he said: I heard your father mention it. Muslim narrated it alone on the authority of Muhammad ibn Hatim on the authority of Yahya ibn Saeed on his authority, and it was narrated on the authority of Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and others on the authority of Hatim ibn Ismail on the authority of Hamid al-Kharrat on his authority. A group of the predecessors and successors said that it was the mosque of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was narrated on the authority of Umar ibn al-Khattab, his son Abdullah, Zaid ibn Thabit, and Saeed ibn al-Musayyab, and Ibn Jarir chose it. His saying: “A mosque founded on piety from the first day is more worthy for you to stand in it. In it are men who love to purify themselves, and God loves those who purify themselves.” This is evidence of the desirability of praying in old mosques founded from the beginning of their construction on the worship of God alone, with no partner for Him, and of the desirability of praying with a group of righteous and working worshippers who maintain the perfection of ablution and avoid contact with filth. Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad bin Ja'far narrated to us from Shu'bah from Abdul Malik bin Umair, I heard Shabib Abu Ruh narrating from a man from the companions of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) that the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) prayed the dawn prayer with them and recited Surah Ar-Rum in it, so he was mistaken. When he finished, he said: "The Qur'an confuses us. Some of you pray with us but do not perform ablution well. Whoever attends the prayer with us should perform ablution well." Then he narrated it through two other chains of narration from Abdul Malik bin Umair from Shabib Abu Ruh from Dhi Al-Kila', that he prayed with the Prophet (peace be upon him) and he mentioned it. This indicates that completing purification makes it easier to perform worship and helps in completing it, perfecting it, and performing its prescribed acts. Abu Al-Aaliyah said regarding the verse: And God loves those who purify themselves that purification with water is good, but they are those who purify themselves from sins. Al-A'mash said: Repentance from sins and purification from polytheism. It was reported in the hadith narrated through chains of narration in Sunan and elsewhere that the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) said to the people of Quba: God has praised you for purification, so what do you do? They said: We clean ourselves with water. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar said: Abdullah bin Shabib told us, Ahmad bin Abdul Aziz told us: I found it in my father’s book on the authority of Al-Zuhri on the authority of Ubaidullah bin Abdullah on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: This verse was revealed about the people of Quba: Among them are men who love to purify themselves, and God loves those who purify themselves. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked them, and they said: We clean ourselves with water after washing ourselves. Al-Bazzar narrated it. Then he said: Muhammad bin Abdul Aziz narrated it on the authority of Al-Zuhri alone, and no one narrated it on his authority except his son. I said: I only mentioned it with this wording because it is well-known among the jurists, and many or all of the later hadith scholars did not know it, and God knows best.
9:108: The reason for the revelation of these noble verses is that before the arrival of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, there was in Medina a man from the Khazraj called Abu Amir the monk. He had become a Christian in the pre-Islamic era and studied the knowledge of the People of the Book. He was a worshipper in the pre-Islamic era and had great honor among the Khazraj. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, arrived as an immigrant to Medina and the Muslims gathered around him and Islam became a high word and God made them victorious on the day of Badr, the accursed Abu Amir shone his light and showed hostility and declared it, and fled to the infidels of Mecca from the polytheists of Quraysh, siding with them in fighting the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. They gathered with those who agreed with them from the tribes of the Arabs and arrived in the year of Uhud. What happened to the Muslims happened and God Almighty tested them, and the outcome was for the righteous. This immoral man had dug holes between the two lines, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, fell into one of them and was injured that day, wounding his face, breaking his lower right front tooth, and splitting his head, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him. And peace be upon him, and Abu Amir advanced at the beginning of the duel to his people from the Ansar and addressed them and won them over to his support and agreement, and when they knew his words they said: May God not bless you, you wicked person, you enemy of God, and they attacked him and cursed him, so he returned saying: By God, evil has befallen my people after me, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had called him to God before his flight and read to him from the Qur’an, but he refused to convert to Islam and rebelled, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed against him that he would die far away, an outcast, and this prayer reached him, and that is because when the people finished with Uhud, and he saw the matter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, rising and appearing, he went to Heraclius, the king of the Romans, to seek his support against the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he promised him and hoped for him and stayed with him, and wrote to a group of his people from the Ansar from the people of hypocrisy and doubt, promising them and hoping that he would come with an army with which he would fight the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and defeat him and turn him back from what he was in, and he ordered them to build a fortress for him to come to them from him to deliver his letters and be As an ambush for him if he came to them after that, so they began to build a mosque adjacent to the Quba Mosque, so they built it and made it perfect and finished it before the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, left for Tabuk. They came and asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to come to them and pray in their mosque so that they could use his prayer in it as evidence of his approval and confirmation. They mentioned that they had only built it for the weak and the sick among them on a winter night, so God protected him from praying in it, so he said: We are on a journey, but when we return, God willing. So when he, peace be upon him, returned to Medina from Tabuk, and there was only a day or part of a day between him and it, Gabriel came down to him with the report of the Mosque of Harm and what its builders had relied on of disbelief and division among the group of believers in their mosque, the Quba Mosque, which had been founded from the first day on piety. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent to that mosque someone to demolish it before his arrival in Medina, as Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse, they are people from the Ansar who built a mosque, so Abu Amir said to them: Build a mosque and prepare with whatever strength and weapons you can, for I am going to Caesar, the king of the Romans, and I will bring Roman soldiers and expel Muhammad and his companions. When they finished their mosque, they came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said to him: We have finished building our mosque, so we would like you to pray in it and supplicate for blessings for us. So God Almighty revealed: Do not stand in it ever until His saying: the wrongdoers. And this was also narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, Mujahid, Urwah bin Az-Zubayr, Qatadah, and more than one of the scholars. Muhammad bin Ishaq bin Yasar said, on the authority of Az-Zuhri, Yazid bin Ruman, Abdullah bin Abi Bakr, Asim bin Umar bin Qatadah, and others, they said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came, meaning from Tabuk, until he stopped at Dhi Awan, a town between it and Medina, an hour of the day, and the people of the Mosque of Harm were there. They came to him while he was preparing for Tabuk and said: O Messenger of God, we have built a mosque for those who are sick and in need, and for rainy nights and winter nights, and we would like you to come and pray for us in it. He said: I am on the verge of a journey and busy, or as the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If we were to arrive, God willing, we would come to you and pray for you in it. When he arrived at Dhi Awan, report of the mosque reached him, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called Malik ibn al-Dakhshum, the brother of Banu Salim ibn Awf, and Ma’n ibn Adi, or his brother Amir ibn Adi, the brother of Balajlan, and said: Go to this mosque whose people are oppressing it, and demolish it and burn it. So they left quickly until they reached Banu Salim ibn Awf, who were the people of Malik ibn al-Dakhshum. Malik said to Ma'n: Give me time until I bring you fire from my family. So his family entered and he took a palm frond and set it on fire. Then they went out running until they entered the mosque and its people were in it. They burned it and demolished it and dispersed from it. And what was revealed about them in the Qur'an was revealed: And those who took a mosque for the purpose of causing harm and disbelief until the end of the story. It was built by twelve men: Khadham bin Khalid from Banu Ubayd bin Zayd, one of Banu Amr bin Awf, from whose house the mosque of Al-Shaqaq was removed, Tha’laba bin Hattab from Banu Ubayd and a client of Banu Umayyah bin Zayd, Mu’tab bin Qushair from Banu Dhubay’ah bin Zayd, Abu Habeeba bin Al-Az’ar from Banu Dhubay’ah bin Zayd, Ibad bin Hanif, the brother of Sahl bin Hanif from Banu Amr bin Awf, Haritha bin Aamer and his sons Mujammi’ bin Haritha and Zayd bin Haritha and Nabtal Al-Harith, who are from Banu Dhubay’ah, and Mukhraj, who are from Banu Dhubay’ah, Bajad bin Othman, who is from Banu Dhubay’ah, Wadi’ah bin Thabit, and the clients of Banu Umayyah, the people of Abu Lubabah bin Abdul Mundhir. And His statement, And they will swear, meaning those who built it, We intended nothing but good, meaning we intended nothing by building it but good and kindness to the people. God Almighty said, And God bears witness that they are liars, meaning in what they intended and what they intended. They only built it to harm the Quba Mosque, and to disbelieve in God, and to divide the believers, and to lie in wait for those who had fought God and His Messenger before, namely Abu Amir the wicked one who was called the monk, may God curse him. And His statement, Never stand in it, is a prohibition to him, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the nation that follows him in that, from standing in it, meaning praying in it, ever. Then he urged him to pray in the Quba Mosque, which was founded from the first day of its construction on piety, which is obedience to God and obedience to His Messenger, and a gathering of the believers and a stronghold and refuge for Islam and its people. For this reason, God Almighty said: A mosque founded on piety from the first day is more worthy for you to stand in it. The context is in reference to the Quba Mosque. For this reason, it was stated in the authentic hadith that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Prayer in the Quba Mosque is like an Umrah. In the authentic hadith, it is stated that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to visit the Quba Mosque riding and walking. In the hadith, it is stated that when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, built and founded it upon his first arrival and descent upon Banu Amr ibn Awf, it was Gabriel who appointed the direction of the qiblah for him. And God knows best. Abu Dawud said: Muhammad ibn al-Ala’ told us, Mu’awiyah ibn Hisham told us, on the authority of Yunus ibn al-Harith, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Abi Maymunah, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “This verse was revealed about the people of Quba’: ‘In it are men who love to purify themselves’ - he said: They used to clean themselves with water, so this verse was revealed about them.” At-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah narrated it on the authority of Yunus ibn al-Harith, and it is weak. At-Tirmidhi said: It is strange from this source. At-Tabarani said: Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Ma’mari told us, Muhammad ibn Hamid al-Razi told us, Salamah ibn al-Fadl told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: When this verse was revealed: ‘In it are men who love to purify themselves’ - the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent for ‘Uwaim ibn Sa’idah and said: ‘What is this purification for which God has praised you?’ He said: O Messenger of God, no man or woman among us has ever left the toilet without washing his private parts or, he said, his anus. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: This is it. Imam Ahmad said: Hussein bin Muhammad told us, Abu Uwais told us, Shurahbil told us on the authority of Uwaim bin Sa’idah al-Ansari, that he told him that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to them in the Quba Mosque and said: God Almighty has praised you well for purification in the story of your mosque, so what is this purification with which you purify yourself? They said: By God, O Messenger of God, we do not know anything, except that we had Jewish neighbors who used to wash their backsides after defecating, so we washed as they did. Ibn Khuzaymah narrated it in his Sahih. Hisham said on the authority of Abdul Hamid Al-Madani on the authority of Ibrahim bin Ismail Al-Ansari: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Uwaim bin Sa’idah: “What is this that God praised you for? ‘Therein are men who love to purify themselves’ verse. They said: O Messenger of God, we wash our backsides with water.” Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad bin ‘Amara Al-Asadi told me, Muhammad bin Sa’d told us on the authority of Ibrahim bin Muhammad on the authority of Shurahbil bin Sa’d, who said: I heard Khuzaymah bin Thabit say: This verse was revealed: ‘Therein are men who love to purify themselves, and God loves those who purify themselves’. He said: They used to wash their backsides after defecating. Another hadith Imam Ahmad bin Hanbal said: Yahya bin Adam told us, Malik, meaning Ibn Mughul, told us, I heard Sayyar Abu Al-Hakam, on the authority of Shahr bin Hawshab, on the authority of Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Salam, who said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, arrived, meaning Quba, he said, “God Almighty has praised you for purification. Will you not tell me?” He meant his statement, In it are men who love to purify themselves. They said, O Messenger of God, we find it written for us in the Torah to clean ourselves with water. A group of the Salaf have stated that it is the Quba Mosque. It was narrated by Ali bin Abi Talha on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and it was narrated by Abdul Razzaq on the authority of Muammar Al-Zuhri on the authority of Urwah bin Al-Zubayr. Atiyah Al-Awfi, Abdul Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam, Al-Sha’bi, and Al-Hasan Al-Basri said, and Al-Baghawi narrated it on the authority of Saeed bin Jubayr and Qatadah. It was mentioned in the authentic hadith that the mosque of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, which is in the heart of Madinah is the mosque that was founded on piety, and this is correct. There is no contradiction between the verse and this, because if the mosque of Quba was founded on piety from the first day, then it is more appropriate and more appropriate for it to be the mosque of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. For this reason, Imam Ahmad bin Hanbal said in his Musnad: Abu Na’im told us, Abdullah bin Amir Al-Aslami told us on the authority of Imran bin Abi Anas, on the authority of Sahl bin Sa’d, on the authority of Ubay bin Ka’b that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The mosque that was founded on piety is this mosque of mine. Ahmad is the only one to narrate it. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: We were told by Wakee’, we were told by Rabia bin Othman Al-Taymi, on the authority of Imran bin Abi Anas, on the authority of Sahl bin Sa’d Al-Sa’idi, who said: Two men differed during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding the mosque that was founded on piety. One of them said it was the mosque of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the other said it was the mosque of Quba. So they came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and asked him, and he said: It is this mosque of mine. Ahmad also transmitted it alone. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Musa bin Dawud told us, Laith told us, on the authority of Imran bin Abi Anas, on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Saeed Al-Khudri, may God be pleased with him, who said: Two men disputed about the mosque that was founded on piety from the first day. One of them said it was the Quba Mosque, and the other said it was the mosque of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, It is this mosque of mine. Ahmad alone transmitted it. Another way Imam Ahmad said: Ishaq bin Isa told us, Laith told us, Imran bin Abi Anas told me, on the authority of Ibn Abi Saeed, on the authority of his father, who said: Two men disputed about the mosque that was founded on piety from the first day. One man said, It is the mosque of Quba, and the other said, “It is the mosque of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.” The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, It is my mosque. And this is how it was narrated by al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa’i on the authority of Qutaybah on the authority of al-Laith, and al-Tirmidhi authenticated it, and Muslim narrated it as will come. Another way Imam Ahmad said: Yahya told us on the authority of Anis bin Abi Yahya, my father told me: I heard Abu Saeed Al-Khudri say: Two men, a man from Banu Khudra and a man from Banu Amr bin Awf, disagreed about the mosque that was founded on piety. Al-Khudri said it was the mosque of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Al-Amri said it was the mosque of Quba. So they came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and asked him about that, so he said: It is this mosque of the mosque of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said in that meaning the mosque of Quba. Another way Imam Ahmad said: Abu Ja`far ibn Jarir said: Ibn Bashar told us, Yahya ibn Sa`id told us, Hamid al-Kharrat al-Madani told us: I asked Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Sa`id and said: How did you hear your father say about the mosque that was founded on piety? He said: I came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and entered upon him in the house of one of his wives and said: O Messenger of God, where is the mosque that was founded on piety? He said: So he took a handful of pebbles and threw them on the ground, then he said: This is your mosque. Then he said: I heard your father mention it. Muslim narrated it alone on the authority of Muhammad ibn Hatim on the authority of Yahya ibn Saeed on his authority, and it was narrated on the authority of Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and others on the authority of Hatim ibn Ismail on the authority of Hamid al-Kharrat on his authority. A group of the predecessors and successors said that it was the mosque of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was narrated on the authority of Umar ibn al-Khattab, his son Abdullah, Zaid ibn Thabit, and Saeed ibn al-Musayyab, and Ibn Jarir chose it. His saying: “A mosque founded on piety from the first day is more worthy for you to stand in it. In it are men who love to purify themselves, and God loves those who purify themselves.” This is evidence of the desirability of praying in old mosques founded from the beginning of their construction on the worship of God alone, with no partner for Him, and of the desirability of praying with a group of righteous and working worshippers who maintain the perfection of ablution and avoid contact with filth. When he finished, he said: "The Qur'an confuses us. Some of you pray with us but do not perform ablution well. Whoever attends the prayer with us should perform ablution well." Then he narrated it through two other chains of narration from Abdul Malik bin Umair from Shabib Abu Ruh from Dhi Al-Kila', that he prayed with the Prophet (peace be upon him) and he mentioned it. This indicates that completing purification makes it easier to perform worship and helps in completing it, perfecting it, and performing its prescribed acts.
