Al-A'mash said: Repentance from sins and purification from polytheism. It was reported in the hadith narrated through chains of narration in Sunan and elsewhere that the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) said to the people of Quba: God has praised you for purification, so what do you do? They said: We clean ourselves with water. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar said: Abdullah bin Shabib told us, Ahmad bin Abdul Aziz told us: I found it in my father’s book on the authority of Al-Zuhri on the authority of Ubaidullah bin Abdullah on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: This verse was revealed about the people of Quba: Among them are men who love to purify themselves, and God loves those who purify themselves. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked them, and they said: We clean ourselves with water after washing ourselves. Al-Bazzar narrated it. Then he said: Muhammad bin Abdul Aziz narrated it on the authority of Al-Zuhri alone, and no one narrated it on his authority except his son. I said: I only mentioned it with this wording because it is well-known among the jurists, and many or all of the later hadith scholars did not know it, and God knows best.
9:109: God the Almighty says: Not equal are those who founded their building on piety to God and His pleasure, and those who built a mosque to cause harm and disbelief and to divide the believers, and as an ambush for those who fought God and His Messenger before. These people build their building on the edge of a crumbling precipice, i.e. the edge of a hole. An example of this is "in the fire of Hell. And God does not guide the wrongdoing people" meaning the work of the corruptors will not be right. Jabir ibn Abdullah said: I saw the mosque that was built to cause harm, and smoke was coming out of it during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Jurayj said: It was mentioned to us that men dug a hole and found smoke coming out of it. Qatadah said the same. Khalaf ibn Yasin al-Kufi said: I saw the mosque of the hypocrites that God the Almighty mentioned in the Qur'an, and in it was a hole from which smoke was coming out, and today it is a garbage dump. Narrated by Ibn Jarir, may God have mercy on him. And the Almighty’s saying: Their structure which they have built will continue to be a source of doubt in their hearts meaning doubt and hypocrisy, because of their committing this heinous act, it caused hypocrisy in their hearts just as the worshippers of the calf were made to drink its love. And His saying: Unless their hearts are cut out meaning by their death, as was said by Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah, Zayd ibn Aslam, Al-Suddi, Habib ibn Abi Thabit, Ad-Dahhak, Abd Al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, and more than one of the scholars of the Salaf. And God is Knowing meaning of the deeds of His creation, Wise in punishing them for them, whether good or evil.
9:110: God the Almighty says: Not equal are those who founded their building on piety to God and His pleasure, and those who built a mosque to cause harm and disbelief and to divide the believers, and as an ambush for those who fought God and His Messenger before. These people build their building on the edge of a crumbling precipice, i.e. the edge of a hole. An example of this is "in the fire of Hell. And God does not guide the wrongdoing people" meaning the work of the corruptors will not be right. Jabir ibn Abdullah said: I saw the mosque that was built to cause harm, and smoke was coming out of it during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Jurayj said: It was mentioned to us that men dug a hole and found smoke coming out of it. Qatadah said the same. Khalaf ibn Yasin al-Kufi said: I saw the mosque of the hypocrites that God the Almighty mentioned in the Qur'an, and in it was a hole from which smoke was coming out, and today it is a garbage dump. Narrated by Ibn Jarir, may God have mercy on him. And the Almighty’s saying: Their structure which they have built will continue to be a source of doubt in their hearts meaning doubt and hypocrisy, because of their committing this heinous act, it caused hypocrisy in their hearts just as the worshippers of the calf were made to drink its love. And His saying: Unless their hearts are cut out meaning by their death, as was said by Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah, Zayd ibn Aslam, Al-Suddi, Habib ibn Abi Thabit, Ad-Dahhak, Abd Al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, and more than one of the scholars of the Salaf. And God is Knowing meaning of the deeds of His creation, Wise in punishing them for them, whether good or evil.
9:111: God the Almighty informs us that He has compensated His believing servants for their lives and wealth when they sacrificed them in His cause with Paradise. This is from His grace, generosity and kindness, for He accepted compensation for what He owns with what He has bestowed upon His obedient servants. For this reason, Al-Hasan Al-Basri and Qatadah said: By God, he pledged allegiance to them and made their price high. Shamr bin Atiyah said: There is no Muslim but that God the Almighty has a pledge around his neck, and he fulfilled it or died upon it. Then he recited this verse. For this reason, it is said that whoever carries out a mission in the cause of God pledged allegiance to God, meaning he accepted this contract and fulfilled it. Muhammad bin Kaab Al-Qurazi and others said: Abdullah bin Rawahah may God be pleased with him said to the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him), meaning on the night of Al-Aqaba: Stipulate for your Lord and for yourself whatever you wish. He said: I stipulate for my Lord that you worship Him and do not associate anything with Him. And I stipulate for myself that you protect me from what you protect yourselves and your wealth from. They said: What will happen to us if we do that? He said, Paradise. They said, “The sale is profitable. We do not accept or accept a refusal.” So the verse, Indeed, God has purchased from the believers their lives, was revealed. And His statement, They fight in the cause of God, killing and being killed, means whether they kill or are killed, or both of these things are combined, Paradise is obligatory for them. And for this reason it is stated in the two Sahihs: “God has guaranteed to whoever goes forth in His cause, and he does not go forth except for jihad in My cause and belief in My messengers, that He will take him to Paradise or return him to the home from which he went forth, having attained whatever reward or booty he had attained.” And His statement: A true promise binding upon Him in the Torah, the Gospel, and the Qur’an is an affirmation of this promise and an announcement that He has written it upon Himself and revealed it to His messengers in His great books, which are the Torah revealed to Moses, the Gospel revealed to Jesus, and the Qur’an revealed to Muhammad, may the blessings and peace of God be upon them all. And His statement: And who is more faithful to his covenant than God? means that He does not break His promise. This is like His statement: And who is more truthful than God in speech? “And who is more truthful than God in speech?” And for this reason He said: “So rejoice in your transaction which you have contracted. And that is what is the great attainment.” That is, let the one who fulfills the requirements of this contract and fulfills this covenant rejoice in the great attainment and eternal bliss.
9:112: This is a description of the believers from whom God has purchased their souls and their wealth with these beautiful qualities and sublime characteristics: those who repent from all sins, those who abandon immoralities, those who worship meaning those who worship their Lord and maintain it, which is words and deeds. Among the most specific words is praise, so that is why He said: those who praise. Among the best deeds is fasting, which is abandoning the pleasures of food, drink, and sexual intercourse, and this is what is meant by travel here, so that is why He said: those who travel, just as He described the wives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, with that in His statement, the Most High: those who travel, meaning those who fast. Likewise, bowing and prostrating, which are expressions of prayer, so that is why He said: those who bow and prostrate, and with that they benefit God’s creation and guide them to obey God by commanding what is right and forbidding what is wrong, with knowledge of what should be done and what should be left, which is preserving the limits of God in what is permissible and forbidden, in knowledge and action. So they worshipped the truth and advised creation, and that is why He said: And give good tidings to the believers, because faith includes all of this. Happiness is all happiness for those who have it. Statement that what is meant by travel is fasting Sufyan al-Thawri said: On the authority of Asim, on the authority of Zur, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, he said: The travelers are the fasting ones. And likewise it was narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair and al-Awfi on the authority of Ibn Abbas. And Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Everything that God mentioned in the Qur’an as travel is the fasting ones. And likewise al-Dahhak, may God have mercy on him, said. And Ibn Jarir said: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Ibrahim bin Yazid told us on the authority of al-Walid bin Abdullah on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, she said: The travel of this nation is fasting. And likewise Mujahid, Saeed bin Jubair, Ata’, Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, al-Dahhak bin Muzahim, Sufyan bin Uyaynah, and others said that what is meant by the travelers are the fasting ones. And al-Hasan al-Basri said: The travelers are the fasting ones during the month of Ramadan. And Abu Amr al-Abdi said: The travelers are those believers who fast continuously. And something similar to this was reported in a hadith with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet. And Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Buzay’ told me, Hakim bin Hizam told us, Sulayman told us on the authority of Abu Salih on the authority of Abu Hurairah said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The travelers are those who are fasting. This is the most correct of the statements. He also said: Yunus told me on the authority of Ibn Wahb on the authority of Umar ibn al-Harith on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar on the authority of Ubayd ibn Umair, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about the travelers, and he said: They are those who are fasting. This is a good mursal, and this is the most correct and well-known of the statements. And what indicates that tourism is jihad is what Abu Dawud narrated in his Sunan from the hadith of Abu Umamah that a man said: O Messenger of God, give me permission to travel, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The tourism of my nation is jihad in the way of God. Ibn al-Mubarak said on the authority of Ibn Lahi’ah, ‘Ammarah ibn Ghaziyah informed me that tourism was mentioned to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God has replaced that for us with jihad in the way of God and glorifying God on every high place. And on the authority of ‘Ikrimah, he said: They are the seekers of knowledge. ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: They are the emigrants, both narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. What is meant by tourism is not what some of those who worship by merely traveling on earth and being alone in the high mountains, caves and wildernesses may understand, for this is not permissible except in days of tribulations and earthquakes in religion, as was proven in Sahih al-Bukhari on the authority of Abu Sa’id al-Khudri, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Soon the best wealth of a man will be sheep that he follows along the mountain passes and the places where rain falls, fleeing with his religion from tribulations. Al-‘Awfi said: And Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And those who preserve the limits of God, he said: those who carry out God’s obedience. And this is what Al-Hasan Al-Basri said, and from him is the narration: Those who preserve the limits of God, he said: the obligations of God. And in another narration: those who carry out God’s command.
9:113: Imam Ahmad said: Abdul Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Ibn Al-Musayyab, on the authority of his father, who said: When Abu Talib was about to die, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered upon him and Abu Jahl and Abdullah bin Abi Umayya were with him. He said, O uncle, say, 'There is no god but God,' a word by which I will argue for you before God Almighty. Abu Jahl and Abdullah bin Abi Umayya said, O Abu Talib, are you turning away from the religion of Abdul Muttalib? He said, I am on the religion of Abdul Muttalib. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, I will seek forgiveness for you as long as I am not forbidden from doing so. Then the verse was revealed, It is not for the Prophet and those who have believed to ask forgiveness for the polytheists, even if they were relatives, after it has become clear to them that they are companions of Hellfire. He said, And the verse was revealed about him, 'Indeed, you do not guide whom you like, but God guides whom He wills.' Bukhari and Muslim. Imam Ahmad said: Yahya bin Adam told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Al-Khalil, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, who said: I heard a man asking forgiveness for his parents, even though they were polytheists. I said: Does a man ask forgiveness for his parents, even though they were polytheists? He said: Did not Ibrahim ask forgiveness for his father? I mentioned that to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the verse was revealed: It is not for the Prophet and those who have believed to ask forgiveness for polytheists 1:13. He said: When he died, I do not know whether Sufyan said it, or Israel said it, or it is in the hadith when he died. I said: This is confirmed from Mujahid that he said when he died. Imam Ahmad said: Al-Hasan bin Musa told us, Zuhair told us, Zubayd bin Al-Harith Al-Yami told us, on the authority of Muharib bin Dithar, on the authority of Ibn Buraydah, on the authority of his father, who said: We were with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and we were on a journey. He stopped with us, and we were close to a thousand riders. He prayed two rak’ahs, then turned to us with his face and his eyes were shedding tears. Umar bin Al-Khattab stood up and said: O Messenger of God, what is the matter with you? He said, “I asked my Lord, the Almighty, to seek forgiveness for my mother, but He did not permit me, so my eyes welled up with tears out of mercy for her from the Fire. I had forbidden you from three things: I forbade you from visiting graves, so visit them, for visiting them will remind you of good. I forbade you from eating the meat of sacrifices after three days, so eat and hold back as much as you wish. I forbade you from drinking beverages in vessels, so drink from any vessel you wish, but do not drink intoxicants.” Ibn Jarir narrated from the hadith of Alqamah bin Murthad from Sulayman bin Buraydah from his father that when the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came to Makkah, he came to a grave and sat down next to it and began to address it, then he stood up weeping. We said, O Messenger of God, we have seen what you did. He said, “I asked my Lord for permission to visit my mother’s grave and He gave me permission. I asked Him for permission to seek forgiveness for her, but He did not give me permission.” He was never seen weeping more than that day. Ibn Abi Hatim said in his interpretation of the hadeeth: My father told us, Khalid bin Khidash told us, Abdullah bin Wahb told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ayoub bin Hani’, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah bin Mas’ud, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) went out one day to the graveyards, so we followed him. He came and sat next to one of the graves, and he confided in it for a long time, then he wept, and we wept because of his weeping. Then he stood up and ‘Umar bin Al-Khattab stood up to him and called him, then he called us, and he said, What made you weep? We said, We wept because of your weeping. He said: The grave that I sat at is the grave of Amina, and I asked permission from my Lord to visit her, and He gave me permission. Then he mentioned it from another source, then he mentioned a hadith from Ibn Mas`ud similar to it, in which it says: “And I asked permission from my Lord to pray for her, but He did not give me permission, and He revealed to me, ‘It is not for the Prophet and those who believe,’ the verse, and I was seized by what a son seizes for his father, and I had forbidden you from visiting graves, so visit them, for they remind you of the Hereafter.” Another hadith with the same meaning. Al-Tabarani said: Muhammad bin Ali Al-Marwazi told us, Abu Al-Darda Abdul Aziz bin Munib told us, Ishaq bin Abdullah bin Kaysan told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned from the Battle of Tabuk and performed the minor pilgrimage, and when he descended from Thaniyat Usfan, he ordered his companions to lean on the pass until he returned to them. So he went and descended upon his mother’s grave and communed with his Lord for a long time, then he cried and his crying became intense and these people cried because of his crying, and they said, The Prophet of God did not cry in this place except because God had done something to his nation that they could not bear. So when these people cried, he stood up and returned to them and said, What makes you cry? They said, O Prophet of God, we cried because of your crying, and we said, perhaps something has happened in your nation that you cannot bear. He said, “No, and some of it happened, but I came down to my mother’s grave and asked God to allow me to intercede for her on the Day of Resurrection, but God refused to allow me, so I took pity on her, even though she was my mother, and I cried. Then Gabriel came to me and said, “And Abraham’s asking forgiveness for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him. But when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of God, he disassociated himself from him.” So you disassociate yourself from your mother as Abraham disassociated himself from his father. So I took pity on her, even though she was my mother, and I asked my Lord to lift four things from my nation, and He lifted two from them, but He refused to lift two. I asked my Lord to lift the stoning from the sky and the drowning from the earth, and not to confuse them into sects and not to let some of them taste the violence of others, so God lifted the stoning from the sky and the drowning from the earth, but God refused to lift the killing and chaos from them.” He only went to his mother’s grave because she was buried under Kada’ and it was Usfan. For them, this is a strange hadith and a strange context, and stranger than it and more reprehensible is what Al-Khatib Al-Baghdadi narrated in the book Al-Sabiq wa Al-Lahiq with an unknown chain of transmission on the authority of Aisha in a hadith that contains a story, that God revived his mother so she believed and then returned, and likewise what Al-Suhayli narrated in Al-Rawdh with a chain of transmission that contains a group of unknown al-Nas 114:God revived his father and mother so they believed in him. Al-Hafiz Ibn Dihya said about this evidence, the gist of which is that this is a new life just as the sun returned after its setting, so Ali prayed the afternoon prayer. Al-Tahawi said: It is an authentic hadith, meaning the hadith of the sun. Al-Qurtubi said: Their revival is not impossible rationally or religiously. He said: I heard that God revived his uncle Abu Talib so he believed in him. I said All of this depends on the authenticity of the hadith, so if it is authentic then there is nothing wrong with it, and God knows best. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: It is not for the Prophet and those who have believed to ask forgiveness for the polytheists 3:10, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, wanted to ask forgiveness for his mother, but God Almighty forbade him from doing so. He said: Indeed, Abraham, the friend of God, has asked forgiveness for his father. So God revealed: And Abraham’s asking forgiveness for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him 3:10. Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding this verse: They used to ask forgiveness for them until this verse was revealed. So they refrained from asking forgiveness for their dead, and they were not forbidden from asking forgiveness for the living until they died. Then God revealed: And Abraham’s asking forgiveness for his father 3:10. Qatada said regarding the verse: It was mentioned to us that some men from the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O Prophet of God, some of our fathers were good neighbors, maintained family ties, freed the captives, and fulfilled their obligations. Should we not ask forgiveness for them? He said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Yes, by God, I seek forgiveness for my father as Abraham sought forgiveness for his father. Then God revealed: It is not for the Prophet and those who have believed to ask forgiveness for the polytheists, until he reached the words Hellfire. Then God Almighty excused Abraham, peace be upon him, and said: And it was not for Abraham to ask forgiveness for his father, the verse. He said: And it was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God revealed to me words that entered my ears and settled in my heart: I was commanded not to ask forgiveness for one who died a polytheist, and whoever gives his surplus wealth, it is better for him, and whoever withholds it, it is worse for him, and God does not blame anyone for what is sufficient.” Al-Thawri said, on the authority of Al-Shaibani, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: A Jewish man died and he had a Muslim son, but he did not go out with him. This was mentioned to Ibn Abbas, who said: He should have walked with him, buried him, and prayed for his well-being as long as he was alive. Then when he died, he left him to his own affairs. Then he said: “And Abraham’s seeking of forgiveness for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him. But when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of God, he disassociated himself from him.” He did not pray. And what testifies to its authenticity is what Abu Dawud and others narrated on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, that when Abu Talib died, I said, O Messenger of God, your uncle, the misguided old man, has died. He said, Go and bury him and do not say anything until you come to me. So he mentioned the entire hadith. And it was narrated that when the funeral of his uncle Abu Talib passed by him, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said, May mercy reach you, O uncle. And Ata’ ibn Abi Rabah said, “I would not neglect to pray for any of the people of the Qiblah, even if it were an Ethiopian woman who was pregnant from fornication, because I have not heard God prohibit prayer except for the polytheists. God Almighty says, “It is not for the Prophet and those who have believed to ask forgiveness for the polytheists.” Ibn Jarir narrated, on the authority of Ibn Wakee’, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Asma bin Zamil, on the authority of his father, who said: I heard Abu Hurairah say: May God have mercy on a man who seeks forgiveness for Abu Hurairah and his mother. I said: And for his father? He said: No. He said: My father died as a polytheist, and his statement: And when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of God, he disowned him. Ibn Abbas said: Ibrahim continued to seek forgiveness for his father until he died, and when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of God, he disowned him. In another narration: When he died, it became clear to him that he was an enemy of God. This is what Mujahid, Ad-Dahhak, Qatadah, and others, may God have mercy on them, said. Ubayd ibn Umair and Sa`id ibn Jubayr said: He will disown him on the Day of Resurrection until he meets his father, and on his father’s face is dust and dirt, and he will say: O Ibrahim, I used to disobey you, but today I do not disobey you. He will say: O Lord, did you not promise me that you would not disgrace me on the Day of Resurrection? What disgrace is greater than that of my distant father? It will be said: Look behind you, and there he is a hyena covered in blood, that is, he has been transformed into a hyena, then he will be dragged by his legs and thrown into the Fire. And his saying: Indeed, Abraham was most compassionate and forbearing. Sufyan al-Thawri and others said: On the authority of Asim ibn Bahdalah, on the authority of Zur ibn Hubaish, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Masoud, that he said: Awwa is supplication. And it was narrated in this way from more than one source: On the authority of Ibn Masoud, and Ibn Jarir said: Al-Muthanna told me, Al-Hajjaj ibn Munhal told us, Abdul Hamid ibn Bahram told us, Shahr ibn Hawshab told us, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Shaddad ibn al-Haad, who said: While the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sitting, a man said: O Messenger of God, what is awwa? He said: The one who beseeches. He said: Indeed, Abraham was most compassionate and forbearing. And Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it: From the hadith of Ibn al-Mubarak, on the authority of Abdul Hamid ibn Bahram, with it, and its wording is: He said: The one who beseeches and beseeches and supplicates. And al-Thawri said, on the authority of Salamah ibn Kuhayl, on the authority of Muslim al-Batin, on the authority of Abu al-Ghadir, that he asked Ibn Masoud about awwa and he said: He is the Most Merciful. And Mujahid, Abu Maysarah, Umar ibn Shurahbil, al-Hasan al-Basri, Qatadah, and others said the same, meaning the Most Merciful, meaning to the servants of God. Ibn Al-Mubarak said on the authority of Khalid on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: Al-Awah is the one who is certain in the language of Abyssinia. Al-Awfi said the same on the authority of Ibn Abbas that it is al-Muwakeen. Mujahid and Ad-Dahhak said the same. Ali bin Abi Talhah and Mujahid said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Al-Awah is the believer. Ali bin Abi Talhah added on his authority: He is the repentant believer. Al-Awfi said on his authority that it is the believer in the language of Abyssinia. Ibn Jurayj said the same that it is the believer in the language of Abyssinia. Imam Ahmad said: Musa told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, on the authority of Al-Harith bin Yazid, on the authority of Ali bin Rabah, on the authority of Uqbah bin Amir, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to a man called Dhu Al-Bijadayn, He is the one who glorifies God. That is because he was a man who, when God was mentioned in the Qur’an, would raise his voice in supplication. It was narrated by Ibn Jarir. Saeed bin Jubair and Al-Sha’bi said, The one who glorifies God is the one who praises God. Ibn Wahb said, on the authority of Mu’awiyah bin Salih, on the authority of Abu Al-Zahariyyah, on the authority of Jubayr bin Nufayr, on the authority of Abu Al-Darda’, may God be pleased with him, who said, No one maintains the Duha prayer bead except the one who glorifies God. Shafi bin Mani’ said, on the authority of Abu Ayoub, The one who glorifies God is the one who, when he remembers his sins, seeks forgiveness for them. It was narrated by Mujahid, on the authority of the one who glorifies God, who secretly commits a sin and then secretly repents from it. All of this was mentioned by Ibn Abi Hatim, may God have mercy on him. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Wakee’ told us, Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Hajjaj, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Muslim bin Bayan, that a man used to frequently mention God and glorify God, so he mentioned that to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said, He is the one who glorifies God. He also said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Ibn Hani’ narrated to us, Al-Munhal bin Khalifa narrated to us, on the authority of Hajjaj bin Artah, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, buried a dead person and said: May God have mercy on you, for you were indeed a recitation of the Qur’an. Shu’bah narrated on the authority of Abu Yunus Al-Bahili, who said: I heard a man in Mecca who was originally Roman and was a storyteller, narrating on the authority of Abu Dharr, who said: There was a man who used to circumambulate the Sacred House and say in his supplication: Oh, oh. So he mentioned that to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: He is indeed a recitation of the Qur’an. He said: So I went out one night and saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, burying that man at night with a lamp. This is a strange hadith narrated by Ibn Jarir. It was narrated on the authority of Ka’b Al-Ahbar that he said: I heard Indeed, Ibrahim was indeed a recitation of the Qur’an. He said: Whenever the Fire was mentioned, he would say: Oh, from the Fire. Ibn Jurayj said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Indeed, Ibrahim was indeed a recitation of the Qur’an. He said: A jurist. Imam Abu Jaafar bin Jarir said: The most correct of the sayings is the saying of the one who said that it is a supplication, and it is appropriate for the context, and that is because when God Almighty mentioned that Abraham only asked forgiveness for his father for a promise he had made to him, and Abraham was a frequent supplicant and forbearing towards those who wronged him and caused him harm, and for this reason he asked forgiveness for his father despite his severe harm to him in his saying: Are you averse to my gods, O Abraham? If you do not desist, I will stone you, and leave me for a long time. He said, “Peace be upon you! I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord. Indeed, He is ever Gracious to me.” So he was forbearing towards him despite his harm to him, and he supplicated for him and asked forgiveness, and for this reason God Almighty said: Indeed, Abraham was most kind and forbearing.
9:115: God Almighty says, informing about His noble self and His just judgment: He does not lead a people astray after conveying the message to them, until the proof has been established against them, as God Almighty said: As for Thamud, We guided them verse. And Mujahid said about God Almighty’s statement: And God would not lead a people astray after He had guided them verse, he said that God Almighty’s statement to the believers about not seeking forgiveness for the polytheists in particular, and in His statement to them about His disobedience and obedience in general, so do it or leave it. Ibn Jarir said: God Almighty says: “God would not have decreed that you seek forgiveness for your dead polytheists by going astray after He has provided you with guidance and enabled you to believe in Him and His Messenger, until He has presented to you a prohibition against it and you have abandoned it. But before He made clear to you the undesirability of that by prohibiting it, and you did not waste His prohibition on what He prohibited you from, then He does not judge him to be astray, for obedience and disobedience only occur from the one who is commanded and the one who is prohibited. As for the one who is not commanded and the one who is not prohibited, then he is neither obedient nor disobedient in what he was not commanded and the one who is not prohibited from.” And the Almighty said: “Indeed, to God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He gives life and causes death. And you have not besides God any protector or helper.” Ibn Jarir said, this is an exhortation from God Almighty to His believing servants to fight the polytheists and the kings of disbelief, and to trust in the victory of God, the Owner of the heavens and the earth, and not to be afraid of His enemies, for they have no protector or helper besides God. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali ibn Abi Dulamah al-Baghdadi told us, Abd al-Wahhab ibn Ata’ told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Safwan ibn Mahraz, on the authority of Hakim ibn Hizam, who said: While the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was among his companions, he said to them: Do you hear what I hear? They said, We do not hear anything. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, “I hear the creaking of the sky, and it is not to be blamed for creaking. There is not a place in it the size of a hand’s breadth but that there is an angel prostrating or standing over it.” Ka’b al-Ahbar said, “There is not a place the size of a needle’s eye on the earth but that there is an angel assigned to it who raises knowledge of that to God. The angels of the sky are more numerous than the dust, and the bearers of the Throne, the distance between the heel of one of them and his brain is a journey of one hundred years.”
9:116: God Almighty says, informing about His noble self and His just judgment: He does not lead a people astray after conveying the message to them, until the proof has been established against them, as God Almighty said: As for Thamud, We guided them verse. And Mujahid said about God Almighty’s statement: And God would not lead a people astray after He had guided them verse, he said that God Almighty’s statement to the believers about not seeking forgiveness for the polytheists in particular, and in His statement to them about His disobedience and obedience in general, so do it or leave it. Ibn Jarir said: God Almighty says: “God would not have decreed that you seek forgiveness for your dead polytheists by going astray after He has provided you with guidance and enabled you to believe in Him and His Messenger, until He has presented to you a prohibition against it and you have abandoned it. But before He made clear to you the undesirability of that by prohibiting it, and you did not waste His prohibition on what He prohibited you from, then He does not judge him to be astray, for obedience and disobedience only occur from the one who is commanded and the one who is prohibited. As for the one who is not commanded and the one who is not prohibited, then he is neither obedient nor disobedient in what he was not commanded and the one who is not prohibited from.” And the Almighty said: “Indeed, to God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He gives life and causes death. And you have not besides God any protector or helper.” Ibn Jarir said, this is an exhortation from God Almighty to His believing servants to fight the polytheists and the kings of disbelief, and to trust in the victory of God, the Owner of the heavens and the earth, and not to be afraid of His enemies, for they have no protector or helper besides God. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali ibn Abi Dulamah al-Baghdadi told us, Abd al-Wahhab ibn Ata’ told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Safwan ibn Mahraz, on the authority of Hakim ibn Hizam, who said: While the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was among his companions, he said to them: Do you hear what I hear? They said, We do not hear anything. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, “I hear the creaking of the sky, and it is not to be blamed for creaking. There is not a place in it the size of a hand’s breadth but that there is an angel prostrating or standing over it.” Ka’b al-Ahbar said, “There is not a place the size of a needle’s eye on the earth but that there is an angel assigned to it who raises knowledge of that to God. The angels of the sky are more numerous than the dust, and the bearers of the Throne, the distance between the heel of one of them and his brain is a journey of one hundred years.”
9:117: Mujahid and others said: This verse was revealed about the Battle of Tabuk, and that is because they went out to it in a difficult situation in a year of famine and intense heat and difficulty in food and water. Qatada said: They went out to the Levant in the year of Tabuk in the blazing heat with what God knows of the hardship, and they were afflicted with severe hardship until it was mentioned to us that two men were splitting a date between them, and the group was passing the date around between them, one of them sucking it and then drinking from it, then the other sucking it and then drinking from it, so God accepted their repentance and returned them from their battle. Ibn Jarir said: Yunus bin Abdul A’la told me, Ibn Wahb told us, Amr bin Al-Harith told me on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Hilal on the authority of Utbah bin Abi Utbah on the authority of Nafi’ bin Jubayr bin Mut’im on the authority of Abdullah bin Abbas, that it was said to Umar bin Al-Khattab about the hardship, so Umar bin Al-Khattab said: We went out with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to Tabuk in intense heat, and we stopped at a place where we were afflicted with thirst until we thought our necks were about to fall. It will be cut off, and even if a man goes to seek water, he will not return until he thinks that his neck will be cut off, and even if a man slaughters his camel, squeezes out its dung and drinks it and puts what is left on his liver, Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq said: O Messenger of God, God Almighty has accustomed you to goodness in supplication, so supplicate for us, so he said: Do you like that? He said: Yes, so he raised his hands and did not return them until the sky poured and rained and then calmed down, and they filled what they had with them, then we went to look but did not find it had passed the army, and Ibn Jarir said: In His statement, God has forgiven the Prophet and the Muhajireen and the Ansar who followed him in the hour of hardship meaning of the provision, purification, provisions and water after the hearts of a party of them had almost deviated meaning from the truth, and doubted the religion of the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and doubted the hardship and difficulty that befell them in their travel and their conquest then He forgiven them meaning: then He granted them repentance to their Lord and returning to steadfastness in His religion for He is to them Kind and Merciful.
9:118: Imam Ahmad said: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told us, my nephew Al-Zuhri Muhammad bin Abdullah told us, on the authority of his uncle Muhammad bin Muslim Al-Zuhri, Abd Al-Rahman bin Abdullah bin Kaab bin Malik told me that Abdullah bin Kaab bin Malik, who was Kaab’s leader from his sons when he went blind, said: I heard Kaab bin Malik narrating his story when he stayed behind from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a campaign he fought except in the campaign of Tabuk, except that I stayed behind in the campaign of Badr and no one was reprimanded for staying behind from it, but the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out seeking the caravan of Quraysh until God gathered them and their enemy without an appointment, and I witnessed with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, the night of Al-Aqaba when we pledged to Islam, and I would not like to have the scene of Badr in it, even though Badr is more famous and more famous among the people. And from my story when I stayed behind from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the campaign of Tabuk, I was never stronger And it was not easier for me than when I stayed behind from him in that raid. By God, I had never gathered two camels before that until I gathered them in that raid. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, rarely wanted to go on a raid without covering it with another one until that raid happened. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went on it in intense heat and faced a long journey and deserts, and faced a large enemy, so he left the matter to the Muslims to prepare as their enemy would prepare. He informed them of the direction he wanted, and the Muslims were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, many, and no one would gather them in a book of Hafiz - meaning the register - Ka’b said: Few men wanted to go on an absence except that they thought that it would be hidden from them unless a revelation was sent down from God Almighty about it. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went on that raid when the fruits and shade were good and I was heading towards it, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the believers with him prepared for it, so I began to go out in order to prepare with them and I returned without having completed anything of my preparation, so I said to myself I am able to do that if I want, and that continued. He continued with me until he had rolled up his sleeves with the people. Then the Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) set out in the morning, and the Muslims were with him, and I had not prepared anything from my equipment. I said, I will prepare myself after a day or two, then I will catch up with him. So I went out after they had departed to prepare, but I returned, but I had not prepared anything from my equipment. Then I went out and returned, but I had not prepared anything. This continued with me until they hurried and the invasion was over. I intended to set out and catch up with them, and I wish I had done so. But that was not destined for me. Whenever I went out among the people after the Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him), it saddened me that I did not see anyone except a man who was accused of hypocrisy or someone whom God the Almighty had excused. The Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) did not mention me until he reached Tabuk. He said while he was sitting with the people in Tabuk, What did Ka`b ibn Malik do? A man from Banu Salamah said, O Messenger of God, his cloak and looking at his sides held him back. Mu`adh ibn Jabal said, "What you said is bad. By God, O Messenger of God, we know nothing but good about him." Then the Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) was silent. Ka`b ibn Malik said: When I heard that the Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) had set out on his way back from Tabuk, my grief overcame me and I began to remember the lie and say, How can I escape his wrath tomorrow? I sought help in that from every wise man among my family. When it was said that the Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) was about to return, falsehood was removed from me and I knew that I would never escape from it. I decided to believe him. The Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) became the morning. When he returned from a journey, he would start by going to the mosque and pray two rak`ahs, then sit for the people. When he had done that, those who had stayed behind came to him and began to apologize to him and swear to him. They were eighty-odd men. The Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) would accept their outward expressions and seek forgiveness for them, and entrust their secrets to God the Most High. Then I came. When I greeted him, he smiled the smile of someone angry. Then he said to me, Come. So I came walking until I sat in front of him. He said to me, What kept you back? Didn't you buy a back? I said, O Messenger of God, if I had sat with anyone other than you from the people of this world, I would have seen... To get out of his anger with an excuse, I have been given an argument, but by God I knew that if I told you today a false story that would please you about me, God would soon make you angry with me, and if I told you the truth that you would find fault with me for, I hope for the consequences of that from God Almighty, and by God I had no excuse, and by God I have never been freer or more comfortable than when I stayed behind from you. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: As for this one, he has told the truth, so stand up until God decides about you. So I got up and some men from Banu Salamah came to me and followed me and said to me: By God, we did not know that you had committed a sin before this, and you were unable to do anything except apologize to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with the same apologies that those who stayed behind used, for it would have been sufficient for you for your sin that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked forgiveness for you. He said: By God, they continued to rebuke me until I wanted to go back and lie to myself. He said: Then I said to them, has anyone encountered this with me? They said: Yes, two men met him with you and said the same as you said, and they were told the same as you were told. I said: Who are they? They said: Murarah ibn al-Rabi' al-'Amiri and Hilal ibn Umayyah al-Waqfi. They mentioned to me two righteous men who had witnessed Badr and in whom I had an example. He said: So I went when they mentioned them to me. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade the Muslims from speaking to us, O three, from among those who stayed behind from him. So the people avoided us and changed towards us until the land became strange to me and was not the land that I used to know. We remained in that state for fifty nights. As for my two companions, they submitted and sat in their homes weeping. As for me, I was the most steadfast and patient of the people. I would attend the prayer with the Muslims and go around the markets and no one would speak to me. I would come to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was sitting after the prayer, and I would greet him and I would say to myself: Should he move his lips to return my greeting or not? Then I would pray close to him and steal glances at him. When I turned to pray, he would look at me, and when I turned towards him, he would turn away from me. When this estrangement from the Muslims had become too long for me, I walked until I climbed over the wall of Abu Qatada, who was my cousin and the dearest person to me. I greeted him, but by God, he did not return my greeting. So I said to him, O Abu Qatada, I ask you by God, do you know that I love God and His Messenger? He said, So he was silent. I went back to him and asked him, but he was silent. I went back to him and asked him, but he was silent. He said, God and His Messenger know best. He said: My eyes welled up and I turned away until I climbed over the wall. While I was walking in the market of the city, I saw a Nabataean from the Nabataeans of Ash-Sham who had come with food to sell in the city. He said: Who will guide me to Ka`b ibn Malik? The people began to point him out to me until he came and gave me a letter from the King of Ghassan, and I was a scribe. It said: As for what follows, it has reached us that your companion has treated you harshly, and God has not placed you in a house of humiliation or loss, so come to us and we will console you. He said: So I said when I read it: This is also a calamity. He said: So I went to the oven with it and lit it with it until forty nights of the fifty had passed, and then the messenger of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to me saying: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, orders you to separate from your wife. I said: Should I divorce her or what should I do? He said: Rather, stay away from her and do not come near her. He said: And he sent to my companion the same. He said: So I said to my wife: Go to your family and stay with them until God decides in this matter what He wills. He said: So the wife of Hilal bin Umayya came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, Hilal is an old, weak man who does not have a servant. Would you mind if I serve him? He said: No, but he should not come near you. She said: By God, he has no movement at all, and by God, he has not stopped crying since what happened to him until this day. He said: One of my family said to me: Why don’t you ask the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, for permission to have intercourse with your wife, for he has given permission to the wife of Hilal bin Umayya to serve him. He said: So I said: By God, I will not ask the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, for her, and I do not know what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would say about her if I ask his permission and I am a young man. He said: So we stayed for ten nights, and fifty nights were completed for us from the time he forbade us from speaking. He said: Then I prayed the dawn prayer on the morning of fifty nights on the roof of one of our houses. While I was sitting in the state that God Almighty mentioned about us, my soul was constricted and the earth was constricted for me despite its vastness, I heard a cry from Awfa on Mount Sala’ saying at the top of his voice: Be glad, O Ka’b bin Malik. He said: So I fell down in prostration and knew that relief had come from God Almighty through repentance for us. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, announced God’s repentance for us when he prayed the dawn prayer. So the people went to give us good report and my companion went before me, giving me good report. A man ran towards me on a horse and Aslam and Awfa ran on the mountain, but the voice was faster than the horse. So when the one whose voice I heard giving me good report came to me, I took off my garment and covered him with his good report. By God, I did not own anything else that day. I borrowed two garments and put them on and set off to lead the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the people met me in groups congratulating me on my repentance. God, they say, may God’s repentance be upon you, until I entered the mosque, and if the Messenger of God, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, is sitting in the mosque and the people are around him, then Talha bin Ubaidullah ran to me until he shook my hand and congratulated me, and by God, no man from the Muhajireen stood up to me except him, he said: Ka’b would not forget that for Talha, Ka’b said: So when I greeted the Messenger of God, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, he said while his face was shining with joy, Be glad for the best day that has passed for you since your mother gave birth to you. He said: I said, Is it from the Messenger of God with you or from God? He said: No, rather it is from God. He said: When the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) was happy, his face would light up until it was like a piece of the moon so that it could be known from him. So when I sat in front of him, I said: O Messenger of God, part of my repentance is that I give up my wealth as charity to God and His Messenger. He said: Keep some of your wealth for yourself, for it is better for you. I said: Then I keep my share that is in Khaybar and I said: O Messenger of God, God has only saved me because of truthfulness, and part of my repentance is that I will not speak anything but the truth as long as I live. He said: By God, I do not know of anyone among the Muslims whom God has blessed with truthfulness in speech since I mentioned that to the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) better than God Almighty has blessed me. By God, I have not deliberately told a lie since I said that to the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) until this day, and I hope that God the Almighty will protect me for what remains. He said And God Almighty revealed: “God has certainly forgiven the Prophet and the Muhajireen and the Ansar who followed him in the hour of hardship after the hearts of a party of them had almost deviated. Then He turned to them in forgiveness. Indeed, He is to them Kind and Merciful. And to the three who were left behind until, when the earth became strait for them, vast as it is, and their souls became strait for them and they perceived that there is no refuge from God except in Him. Then He turned to them in forgiveness that they might repent. Indeed, God is the Accepter of Repentance, the Merciful. O you who have believed, fear God and be with the truthful.” to the end of the verses. Ka'b said: By God, God has never bestowed upon me a greater blessing after He guided me to Islam than my truthfulness to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on that day, so that I would not have lied about him and perished as those who lied about him perished. God Almighty said to those who lied about him when He sent down the revelation the worst thing He has ever said to anyone. God Almighty said: "They will swear to you by God when you return to them to turn away from them, so turn away from them. Indeed, they are unclean, and their refuge is Hell as recompense for what they used to earn. They swear to you so that you may be pleased with them. But if you are pleased with them, then indeed, God is not pleased with the wicked people." He said: And we, the three who were left behind, were not responsible for the matter of those whom the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, accepted when they swore, so he pledged allegiance to them and asked forgiveness for them, and the Messenger of God postponed our matter until God decided on it. Therefore, God Almighty said: And concerning the three who were left behind. His leaving us behind and postponing our matter that was mentioned from what we left behind was not our staying behind from the conquest, but rather it was regarding the one who swore to him and apologized to him and he accepted from him. This is a sound and authentic hadith, the authenticity of which is agreed upon. It was narrated by the two authors of the Sahihs, al-Bukhari and Muslim, from the hadith of al-Zuhri in a similar manner. This hadith includes the interpretation of this noble verse in the best and simplest ways. It was also narrated from more than one of the early Muslims in its interpretation, as al-A’mash narrated from Abu Sufyan from Jabir ibn Abdullah regarding the words of God the Almighty: And concerning the three who were left behind, he said: They are Ka’b ibn Malik, Hilal ibn Umayya, and Murarah ibn al-Rabi’, and all of them were from the Ansar. This is what Mujahid, al-Dahhak, Qatadah, al-Suddi, and more than one said, and all of them said Murarah ibn Rabi’ah. This is also in Muslim ibn Rabi’ah in some of its versions, and in some of them Murarah ibn al-Rabi’, and in a narration from al-Dahhak Murarah ibn al-Rabi’ as it appears in the two Sahihs, which is correct. His saying, They named two men who witnessed Badr, it was said that this was a mistake by al-Zuhri, because it is not known that any of these three witnessed Badr. And God knows best. And when God Almighty mentioned the distress and anguish He relieved these three from because of the Muslims abandoning them for about fifty nights and days, and their souls became tight for them and the earth became tight for them with all its vastness, meaning despite its vastness the paths and ways were corrupted for them so they could not find guidance in what they should do, so they were patient for the command of God and submitted to the command of God and remained steadfast until God relieved them because of their truthfulness to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in their absence, and that it was without an excuse so they were punished for that for this period then God repented to them, so the consequence of their truthfulness was good for them and repentance for them, and for this reason He said, O you who believe, fear God and be with the truthful, meaning be truthful and adhere to truthfulness so that you will be among its people and be saved from destruction, and He will make for you a way out of your affairs and a way out. Imam Ahmad said: Abu Mu’awiyah told us, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Shuqaiq, on the authority of Abdullah, who is Ibn Mas’ud, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Adhere to truthfulness, for truthfulness leads to righteousness. And righteousness leads to Paradise, and a man continues to tell the truth and seeks to be truthful until he is recorded with God as truthful. And beware of lying, for lying leads to immorality and immorality leads to the Fire, and a man continues to lie and seeks to lie until he is recorded with God as a liar.” Narrated by Al-Bukhari and Muslim in their Sahihs. Shu’bah said on the authority of Amr ibn Murrah: He heard Abu Ubaidah narrating on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, may God be pleased with him, that he said: Lying is not appropriate in seriousness or jest. Read if you wish, O you who believe, fear God and be with those who are truthful. This is how he read it, then he said, Do you find anyone who has an excuse for it? And on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr, regarding his statement, Fear God and be with those who are truthful, he said, “With Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions.” Ad-Dahhak said, With Abu Bakr, Umar and their companions. And Al-Hasan Al-Basri said, If you want to be with those who are truthful, then you must be ascetic in this world and refrain from the people of the religion.

He continued with me until he had rolled up his sleeves with the people. Then the Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) set out in the morning, and the Muslims were with him, and I had not prepared anything from my equipment. I said, I will prepare myself after a day or two, then I will catch up with him. So I went out after they had departed to prepare, but I returned, but I had not prepared anything from my equipment. Then I went out and returned, but I had not prepared anything. This continued with me until they hurried and the invasion was over. I intended to set out and catch up with them, and I wish I had done so. But that was not destined for me. Whenever I went out among the people after the Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him), it saddened me that I did not see anyone except a man who was accused of hypocrisy or someone whom God the Almighty had excused. I said, O Messenger of God, if I had sat with anyone other than you from the people of this world, I would have seen...
