Then I would pray close to him and steal glances at him. When I turned to pray, he would look at me, and when I turned towards him, he would turn away from me. When this estrangement from the Muslims had become too long for me, I walked until I climbed over the wall of Abu Qatada, who was my cousin and the dearest person to me. I greeted him, but by God, he did not return my greeting. So I said to him, O Abu Qatada, I ask you by God, do you know that I love God and His Messenger? He said, So he was silent. I went back to him and asked him, but he was silent. I went back to him and asked him, but he was silent. He said, God and His Messenger know best. He said: My eyes welled up and I turned away until I climbed over the wall. While I was walking in the market of the city, I saw a Nabataean from the Nabataeans of Ash-Sham who had come with food to sell in the city. He said: Who will guide me to Ka`b ibn Malik? The people began to point him out to me until he came and gave me a letter from the King of Ghassan, and I was a scribe. It said: As for what follows, it has reached us that your companion has treated you harshly, and God has not placed you in a house of humiliation or loss, so come to us and we will console you. He said: So I said when I read it: This is also a calamity. He said: So I went to the oven with it and lit it with it until forty nights of the fifty had passed, and then the messenger of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to me saying: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, orders you to separate from your wife. I said: Should I divorce her or what should I do? He said: Rather, stay away from her and do not come near her. He said: And he sent to my companion the same. He said: So I said to my wife: Go to your family and stay with them until God decides in this matter what He wills. He said: So the wife of Hilal bin Umayya came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, Hilal is an old, weak man who does not have a servant. Would you mind if I serve him? He said: No, but he should not come near you. She said: By God, he has no movement at all, and by God, he has not stopped crying since what happened to him until this day. He said: One of my family said to me: Why don’t you ask the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, for permission to have intercourse with your wife, for he has given permission to the wife of Hilal bin Umayya to serve him. He said: So I said: By God, I will not ask the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, for her, and I do not know what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would say about her if I ask his permission and I am a young man. He said: So we stayed for ten nights, and fifty nights were completed for us from the time he forbade us from speaking. He said: Then I prayed the dawn prayer on the morning of fifty nights on the roof of one of our houses. While I was sitting in the state that God Almighty mentioned about us, my soul was constricted and the earth was constricted for me despite its vastness, I heard a cry from Awfa on Mount Sala’ saying at the top of his voice: Be glad, O Ka’b bin Malik. He said: So I fell down in prostration and knew that relief had come from God Almighty through repentance for us. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, announced God’s repentance for us when he prayed the dawn prayer. So the people went to give us good report and my companion went before me, giving me good report. A man ran towards me on a horse and Aslam and Awfa ran on the mountain, but the voice was faster than the horse. So when the one whose voice I heard giving me good report came to me, I took off my garment and covered him with his good report. By God, I did not own anything else that day. I borrowed two garments and put them on and set off to lead the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the people met me in groups congratulating me on my repentance. God, they say, may God’s repentance be upon you, until I entered the mosque, and if the Messenger of God, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, is sitting in the mosque and the people are around him, then Talha bin Ubaidullah ran to me until he shook my hand and congratulated me, and by God, no man from the Muhajireen stood up to me except him, he said: Ka’b would not forget that for Talha, Ka’b said: So when I greeted the Messenger of God, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, he said while his face was shining with joy, Be glad for the best day that has passed for you since your mother gave birth to you. He said: I said, Is it from the Messenger of God with you or from God? He said: No, rather it is from God. He said: When the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) was happy, his face would light up until it was like a piece of the moon so that it could be known from him. So when I sat in front of him, I said: O Messenger of God, part of my repentance is that I give up my wealth as charity to God and His Messenger. He said: Keep some of your wealth for yourself, for it is better for you. I said: Then I keep my share that is in Khaybar and I said: O Messenger of God, God has only saved me because of truthfulness, and part of my repentance is that I will not speak anything but the truth as long as I live. He said: By God, I do not know of anyone among the Muslims whom God has blessed with truthfulness in speech since I mentioned that to the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) better than God Almighty has blessed me. By God, I have not deliberately told a lie since I said that to the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) until this day, and I hope that God the Almighty will protect me for what remains. He said And God Almighty revealed: “God has certainly forgiven the Prophet and the Muhajireen and the Ansar who followed him in the hour of hardship after the hearts of a party of them had almost deviated. Then He turned to them in forgiveness. Indeed, He is to them Kind and Merciful. And to the three who were left behind until, when the earth became strait for them, vast as it is, and their souls became strait for them and they perceived that there is no refuge from God except in Him. Then He turned to them in forgiveness that they might repent. Indeed, God is the Accepter of Repentance, the Merciful. O you who have believed, fear God and be with the truthful.” to the end of the verses. Ka'b said: By God, God has never bestowed upon me a greater blessing after He guided me to Islam than my truthfulness to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on that day, so that I would not have lied about him and perished as those who lied about him perished. God Almighty said to those who lied about him when He sent down the revelation the worst thing He has ever said to anyone. God Almighty said: "They will swear to you by God when you return to them to turn away from them, so turn away from them. Indeed, they are unclean, and their refuge is Hell as recompense for what they used to earn. They swear to you so that you may be pleased with them. But if you are pleased with them, then indeed, God is not pleased with the wicked people." He said: And we, the three who were left behind, were not responsible for the matter of those whom the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, accepted when they swore, so he pledged allegiance to them and asked forgiveness for them, and the Messenger of God postponed our matter until God decided on it. Therefore, God Almighty said: And concerning the three who were left behind. His leaving us behind and postponing our matter that was mentioned from what we left behind was not our staying behind from the conquest, but rather it was regarding the one who swore to him and apologized to him and he accepted from him. This is a sound and authentic hadith, the authenticity of which is agreed upon. It was narrated by the two authors of the Sahihs, al-Bukhari and Muslim, from the hadith of al-Zuhri in a similar manner. This hadith includes the interpretation of this noble verse in the best and simplest ways. It was also narrated from more than one of the early Muslims in its interpretation, as al-A’mash narrated from Abu Sufyan from Jabir ibn Abdullah regarding the words of God the Almighty: And concerning the three who were left behind, he said: They are Ka’b ibn Malik, Hilal ibn Umayya, and Murarah ibn al-Rabi’, and all of them were from the Ansar. This is what Mujahid, al-Dahhak, Qatadah, al-Suddi, and more than one said, and all of them said Murarah ibn Rabi’ah. This is also in Muslim ibn Rabi’ah in some of its versions, and in some of them Murarah ibn al-Rabi’, and in a narration from al-Dahhak Murarah ibn al-Rabi’ as it appears in the two Sahihs, which is correct. His saying, They named two men who witnessed Badr, it was said that this was a mistake by al-Zuhri, because it is not known that any of these three witnessed Badr. And God knows best. And when God Almighty mentioned the distress and anguish He relieved these three from because of the Muslims abandoning them for about fifty nights and days, and their souls became tight for them and the earth became tight for them with all its vastness, meaning despite its vastness the paths and ways were corrupted for them so they could not find guidance in what they should do, so they were patient for the command of God and submitted to the command of God and remained steadfast until God relieved them because of their truthfulness to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in their absence, and that it was without an excuse so they were punished for that for this period then God repented to them, so the consequence of their truthfulness was good for them and repentance for them, and for this reason He said, O you who believe, fear God and be with the truthful, meaning be truthful and adhere to truthfulness so that you will be among its people and be saved from destruction, and He will make for you a way out of your affairs and a way out. Imam Ahmad said: Abu Mu’awiyah told us, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Shuqaiq, on the authority of Abdullah, who is Ibn Mas’ud, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Adhere to truthfulness, for truthfulness leads to righteousness. And righteousness leads to Paradise, and a man continues to tell the truth and seeks to be truthful until he is recorded with God as truthful. And beware of lying, for lying leads to immorality and immorality leads to the Fire, and a man continues to lie and seeks to lie until he is recorded with God as a liar.” Narrated by Al-Bukhari and Muslim in their Sahihs. Shu’bah said on the authority of Amr ibn Murrah: He heard Abu Ubaidah narrating on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, may God be pleased with him, that he said: Lying is not appropriate in seriousness or jest. Read if you wish, O you who believe, fear God and be with those who are truthful. This is how he read it, then he said, Do you find anyone who has an excuse for it? And on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr, regarding his statement, Fear God and be with those who are truthful, he said, “With Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions.” Ad-Dahhak said, With Abu Bakr, Umar and their companions. And Al-Hasan Al-Basri said, If you want to be with those who are truthful, then you must be ascetic in this world and refrain from the people of the religion.
9:120: The Blessed and Exalted admonishes those who stayed behind from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the Battle of Tabuk from the people of Medina and the surrounding Arab tribes, and their desire for themselves rather than to console him in the hardship that befell him, for they diminished their reward because they are not afflicted by thirst which is thirst nor fatigue which is exhaustion nor hunger which is famine nor do they tread a path that enrages the disbelievers meaning they do not enter a place that terrifies their enemy nor do they attain from it victory and dominance over it except that it is written for them for these deeds that are not within their capacity but rather are the result of their actions, righteous deeds and a great reward Indeed, God does not allow the reward of those who do good to be lost as He says Indeed, We do not allow the reward of anyone who does good to be lost.
9:121: God the Almighty says: And they do not spend these warriors in the way of God a small or large expenditure meaning little or much nor do they cross a valley meaning in marching to the enemies except that it is recorded for them and He did not say here that, because these are actions that come from them, and for this reason He said: That God may reward them with the best of what they used to do and the Commander of the Faithful Uthman ibn Affan, may God be pleased with him, obtained a great share and a great portion of this noble verse, and that is because he spent great expenditures and abundant money in this raid, as Abdullah ibn al-Imam Ahmad said: Abu Musa al-Ghanzi told us, Abd al-Samad ibn Abd al-Warith told us, Sulayman ibn al-Mughira told me, al-Walid ibn Abi Hisham told me, on the authority of Farqad Abu Talha, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Khabab al-Salami, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave a sermon and urged the army of hardship, so Uthman ibn Affan, may God be pleased with him, said: I owe one hundred camels with their saddles and saddlebags, he said then he urged, so Uthman said: I owe another one hundred camels With their saddles and saddlebags, he said then he descended a step from the pulpit and urged, so Uthman bin Affan said: I have another hundred with their saddles and saddlebags. He said: I saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, move his hand like this, and Abdul Samad extended his hand as if in amazement, What does Uthman do after this? Abdullah also said: Harun bin Maruf told us, Damrah told us, Abdullah bin Shawdhab told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Qasim, on the authority of Katheer, the freed slave of Abdul Rahman bin Samrah, on the authority of Abdul Rahman bin Samrah, he said: Uthman, may God be pleased with him, came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, with a thousand dinars in his garment until the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, equipped the Army of Difficulty, he said: So he poured it into the lap of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I saw the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, turning it over in his hand and saying: What does Ibn Affan do after today will not harm him, repeating it repeatedly. Qatada said about the words of God, the Most High: And they do not cross a valley but that it is recorded for them verse. A people do not increase in distance from their families in the cause of God except that they increase in closeness to God.
9:122: This is a statement from God Almighty regarding what He wanted from the neighborhoods to go out with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the Battle of Tabuk. A group of the Salaf believed that it was obligatory for every Muslim to go out when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, set out. For this reason, God Almighty said: Go forth, whether light or heavy. And He said: It was not for the people of Medina and those around them of the desert Arabs verse. He said that this was abrogated by this verse. It may be said that this is a statement of what God Almighty meant by the mobilization of all the tribes and a group from each tribe if they did not all go out, so that those who went out with the Messenger would understand what was revealed to him and warn their people if they returned to them about what happened with the enemy, so that both matters would come together for them in this specific mobilization, and after him, may God bless him and grant him peace, the group that went out from the tribe would either be for understanding or for jihad, for it is a communal obligation upon the tribes. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse And it is not for the believers to go out all together meaning: the believers would not go out all together and leave the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, alone. Why should not a party from every division of them go out meaning a group, meaning the raiding parties, and they would not go out except with his permission, so when the raiding parties returned and the Qur’an had been revealed after them, those who stayed with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would learn it, and they would say: God has revealed a Qur’an to your Prophet and we have learned it, so the raiding parties would remain learning what God revealed to their Prophet after them and other raiding parties would be sent out, so that is His saying: So that they may understand In religion, he says: So that they may learn what God has revealed to their Prophet and so that they may know the raids when they return to them, “so that they may beware. Mujahid said: This verse was revealed about some of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who went out into the desert and found favor among the people, and some of the fertility from which they benefited, and they called whomever they found among the people to guidance, so the people said to them: We see you only leaving your companions and coming to us? They felt embarrassed by this and came all of them from the desert until they entered upon the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. God Almighty said: Why should not a party from every division of them go forth seeking good to gain understanding in religion and to listen to what is in the people and what God has revealed, so he excused them and to warn their people all the people when they return to them that they may beware. Qatada said about the verse: This is when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sends out armies, God commands them to go on a raid with His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and a party stays with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gaining understanding in religion, and a party sets out to call their people and warn them of God’s events with those who came before them. Ad-Dahhak said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out on a military expedition himself, it was not permissible for any of the Muslims to stay behind him except those who had excuses. When he stood up and took the raiding parties captive, it was not permissible for them to set out except with his permission. When a man was taken captive, the Qur’an was revealed after him and the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited it to his companions who were sitting with him. When the raiding party returned, those who had stayed with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would say to them: God has revealed a Qur’an to His Prophet after you, so that they may recite it to them and instruct them in the religion. This is His statement: And it is not for the believers to go forth all at once. He said when the Messenger of God set out, Why should not a party from every division of them go forth? He meant by that that it is not appropriate for the Muslims to go forth all at once while the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sitting. However, when the Prophet of God sat, the raiding parties would depart and most of the people would sit with him. Ali bin Abi Talha also said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse, his saying, And it is not for the believers to go forth all together, that it is not about jihad, but when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called for years against Mudar, their land became barren and the tribe of them came in its entirety, until they settled in Medina from the hardship and claimed Islam while they were lying, so they made things difficult for the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and exhausted them, so God Almighty revealed informing His Messenger that they were not believers, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned them to their clans and warned their people not to do what they did, so that is what His saying, And that they may warn their people when they return to them, the verse. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding this verse: A group would set out from every Arab tribe and come to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and ask him about what they wanted regarding their religious affairs and learn about their religion, and they would say to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: What do you command us to do? And he told us what we should order our tribes to do when we come to them. He said: The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, orders them to obey God and His Messenger and sends them to their people with prayer and zakat. When they come to their people, they say: Whoever accepts Islam is one of us. They warn them, until a man leaves his father and mother. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, informs them and warns them of their people. When they return to them, they call them to Islam and warn them of the Fire and give them glad tidings of Paradise. Ikrimah said when this verse was revealed: If you do not go forth, He will punish you with a painful punishment and It is not for the people of Medina the verse, the hypocrites said: The people of the desert who stayed behind from Muhammad and did not go forth with him are destroyed. Some of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out to the desert to their people to teach them, so God Almighty revealed: It is not for the believers to go forth all together the verse, and it was revealed: And those who dispute about God after He has been answered - their argument is worthless with God. Their Lord has wrath upon them, and they will have a severe punishment.” Al-Hasan al-Basri said about the verse: So that those who went out may understand what God has shown them of victory over the polytheists and support, and warn their people when they return to them.
9:123: God the Almighty ordered the believers to fight the infidels first, then the closest, then the closest, then the closest to the domain of Islam. For this reason, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, began fighting the polytheists in the Arabian Peninsula. When he finished with them and God opened for him Mecca, Medina, Taif, Yemen, Yamamah, Hajar, Khaybar, Hadhramaut, and other regions of the Arabian Peninsula, and people from all the tribes of the Arabs entered the religion of God in droves, he began fighting the People of the Book. He prepared to invade the Romans, who were the closest people to the Arabian Peninsula and the most deserving of calling to Islam because they were the People of the Book. He reached Tabuk and then returned because of the people’s hardship, the drought in the country, and the tightness of the situation. This was in the ninth year of his migration, peace be upon him. Then he was busy in the tenth year with the Farewell Pilgrimage, then death overtook him, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, eighty-one days after his pilgrimage. God chose him for what He had, and his minister, friend, and successor Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him, took charge of the matter after him. The religion had deviated to a point that it almost vanished. Then God Almighty strengthened him through him, so he strengthened the foundations and fixed the pillars, and returned the straying religion despite his reluctance, and returned the apostates to Islam, and took the zakat from those tyrants who prevented it, and explained the truth to those who were ignorant of it, and fulfilled what the Messenger was charged with, then he began to equip the Islamic armies against the Romans, the cross-worshippers, and against the Persians, the fire-worshippers, so God, by the blessing of his embassy, opened the countries, and humiliated the noses of Khosrau and Caesar and those of the servants who obeyed them. He spent their treasures in the way of God as the Messenger of God had informed us, and the completion of the matter was at the hands of his successor after him, and his crown prince, the Faruq al-Awab, the Martyr of the Pulpit, Abu Hafs Omar bin al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, so God humiliated the noses of the infidel atheists through him, and suppressed the tyrants and hypocrites and seized the kingdoms east and west. And the treasuries of money were brought to him from all the regions, far and near, so he distributed them in the lawful manner and the acceptable way. Then when he died as a martyr, he had lived a praiseworthy life. The companions of the Muhajireen and the Ansar agreed on the caliphate of the Commander of the Faithful, Uthman ibn Affan, may God be pleased with him, the martyr of the house. Islam clothed his leadership in a complete garment. God's conclusive proof extended over the necks of the servants in all regions. Islam appeared in the East and West of the earth. God's word was elevated and His religion appeared. The pure faith achieved its ultimate goal against the enemies of God. And whenever a nation rises, they move on to those who come after them, then to those who follow them from the rebellious and wicked, in compliance with the words of God Almighty: O you who believe, fight those of the disbelievers who are near you and His words: And let them find in you harshness meaning let the disbelievers among you find harshness in your fighting them, for the perfect believer is the one who is kind to his believing brother and harsh with his disbelieving enemy, as God Almighty says: Then God will bring forth a people whom He loves and who love Him, humble toward the believers, mighty against the disbelievers and His words: Muhammad is the Messenger of God, and those with him are forceful against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves and His words: O Prophet, fight the disbelievers and the hypocrites and be harsh with them and in the hadith: that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I am the one who laughs and fights meaning that he laughs in the face of his friend and fights the head of his enemy, and His words: And know that God is with the righteous meaning fight the disbelievers and put your trust in God and know that God is with you if You feared Him and obeyed Him, and this is how it was when the three generations who are the best of this nation were at the peak of righteousness and obedience to God the Almighty, they did not cease to be victorious over their enemy. And the conquests did not cease to be many and the enemies did not cease to be in humiliation and loss, then when the seditions, whims and differences occurred between the kings, the enemies coveted the outskirts of the countries and advanced towards them, but they did not prevent it because the kings were busy with each other, then they advanced into the domain of Islam and took many countries from the outskirts, then they did not cease until they took control of many of the lands of Islam, and God is the command before and after, so whenever a king of the kings of Islam rose and obeyed the commands of God and put his trust in God, God opened for him lands and he took back from the enemies according to his ability and to the extent of his guardianship of God. And God is the one we ask and hope for, that He will enable the Muslims to control the forelocks of His disbelieving enemies and that He will raise their word in all regions, for He is Generous and Noble.
9:124: God the Almighty says: And when a surah is revealed from the hypocrites some say to each other, Which of you has this increased in faith? meaning some of them say to each other, Which of you has this surah increased in faith?" God the Almighty says: "But as for those who believe, it has increased them in faith, and they rejoice." This verse is one of the greatest proofs that faith increases and decreases, as is the doctrine of most of the early and later scholars. In fact, more than one person has narrated the consensus on this. This issue was discussed in detail at the beginning of Al-Bukhari’s commentary, may God have mercy on him: As for those in whose hearts is disease, it will increase their filth upon their filth, meaning it will increase their doubt upon their doubt and their suspicion upon their suspicion, as God Almighty said: And We send down of the Qur’an that which is healing, and God Almighty said: “Say: It is, for those who believe, a guide and a healing. But those who do not believe - in their ears is deafness, and it is, for them, blindness. Those are being called from a distant place.” This is part of their misery, that what guides the hearts is a cause of their misguidance and destruction, just as if someone with a bad temperament were to be nourished with it, it would only increase his confusion and deficiency.
9:125: God the Almighty says: "And when a surah is revealed from the hypocrites some say to each other, Which of you has this increased in faith? meaning some of them say to each other, Which of you has this surah increased in faith? God the Almighty says: But as for those who believe, it has increased them in faith, and they rejoice. This verse is one of the greatest proofs that faith increases and decreases, as is the doctrine of most of the early and later scholars. In fact, more than one person has narrated the consensus on this. This issue was discussed in detail at the beginning of Al-Bukhari’s commentary, may God have mercy on him: As for those in whose hearts is disease, it will increase their filth upon their filth, meaning it will increase their doubt upon their doubt and their suspicion upon their suspicion, as God Almighty said: And We send down of the Qur’an that which is healing, and God Almighty said: “Say: It is, for those who believe, a guide and a healing. But those who do not believe - in their ears is deafness, and it is, for them, blindness. Those are being called from a distant place.” This is part of their misery, that what guides the hearts is a cause of their misguidance and destruction, just as if someone with a bad temperament were to be nourished with it, it would only increase his confusion and deficiency.
9:126: He says: The Most High, do these hypocrites not see that they are tested once or twice every year, then they do not repent nor do they remember, meaning they do not repent from their past sins nor do they remember in their future circumstances. Mujahid said that they are tested by famine and hunger, and Qatadah said that they are tested by war once or twice every year. Sharik said on the authority of Jabir: He is Al-Ja’fi on the authority of Abu Al-Duha on the authority of Hudhayfah regarding His statement: Or do they not see that they are tested once or twice every year? He said: We used to hear a lie or two every year, and many groups of people would go astray because of them. Narrated by Ibn Jarir. In the hadith on the authority of Anas: The matter only increases in severity and people only increase in miserliness, and there is no year except that the one after it is worse than it. I heard it from your Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. His statement: “And when a surah is revealed, some of them look at others: Does anyone see you? Then they turn away. God has turned their hearts away because they are a people who do not understand.” This is also a report. Regarding the hypocrites, when a surah was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, they would look at one another meaning they would turn around does anyone see you? Then they would turn away, meaning they would turn away from the truth and depart from it. This is their state in religion, they do not remain steadfast in the truth, nor do they accept it, nor do they understand it, as God the Almighty says: So why do they turn away from the reminder? As if they were frightened donkeys, Fleeing from a lion. And God the Almighty says: Then what is wrong with those who disbelieved before you, running away, to the right and to the left, in a state of humiliation? Meaning what is wrong with these people, that they turn away from you, to the right and to the left, fleeing from the truth and going to falsehood? And His statement: Then they turned away, God turned their hearts away, as He says: So when they deviated, God made their hearts deviate, “because they are a people who do not understand,” meaning they do not understand God’s speech, nor do they intend to understand it, nor do they want it, rather they are preoccupied with it and averse to it, so this is why they have become what they have become.
9:127: He says: The Most High, do these hypocrites not see that they are tested once or twice every year, then they do not repent nor do they remember, meaning they do not repent from their past sins nor do they remember in their future circumstances. Mujahid said that they are tested by famine and hunger, and Qatadah said that they are tested by war once or twice every year. Sharik said on the authority of Jabir: He is Al-Ja’fi on the authority of Abu Al-Duha on the authority of Hudhayfah regarding His statement: Or do they not see that they are tested once or twice every year? He said: We used to hear a lie or two every year, and many groups of people would go astray because of them. Narrated by Ibn Jarir. In the hadith on the authority of Anas: The matter only increases in severity and people only increase in miserliness, and there is no year except that the one after it is worse than it. I heard it from your Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. His statement: “And when a surah is revealed, some of them look at others: Does anyone see you? Then they turn away. God has turned their hearts away because they are a people who do not understand.” This is also a report. Regarding the hypocrites, when a surah was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, they would look at one another meaning they would turn around does anyone see you? Then they would turn away, meaning they would turn away from the truth and depart from it. This is their state in religion, they do not remain steadfast in the truth, nor do they accept it, nor do they understand it, as God the Almighty says: So why do they turn away from the reminder? As if they were frightened donkeys, Fleeing from a lion. And God the Almighty says: Then what is wrong with those who disbelieved before you, running away, to the right and to the left, in a state of humiliation? Meaning what is wrong with these people, that they turn away from you, to the right and to the left, fleeing from the truth and going to falsehood? And His statement: Then they turned away, God turned their hearts away, as He says: So when they deviated, God made their hearts deviate, “because they are a people who do not understand,” meaning they do not understand God’s speech, nor do they intend to understand it, nor do they want it, rather they are preoccupied with it and averse to it, so this is why they have become what they have become.
9:128: The Almighty says, thanking the believers for sending to them a Messenger from among themselves, that is, from their kind and in their language, as Abraham, peace be upon him, said: Our Lord, and send among them a Messenger from among themselves. And the Almighty said: God has conferred a great favor upon the believers when He sent among them a Messenger from among themselves. And the Almighty said: There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves, that is, from you and in your language, as Ja’far ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, said to the Negus and Al-Mughira ibn Shu’ba to the Messenger of Kisra: God has sent among us a Messenger from among us, we know his lineage, description, entrance and exit, his truthfulness and trustworthiness. And he mentioned the hadith. And Sufyan ibn Uyaynah said on the authority of Ja’far ibn Muhammad on the authority of his father regarding the Almighty’s statement: There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves, he said: Nothing of the birth of the Age of Ignorance affected him, and the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: I came out of wedlock and I did not come out of fornication. And this was transmitted from another source, as Al-Hafiz Abu Muhammad Al-Hasan ibn Abd Al-Rahman Al-Ramharmuzi said in his book Al-Fasil Bayn Al-Rawi Wal-Wa’i: Abu Ahmad told us. Yusuf bin Harun bin Ziyad narrated to us Ibn Abi Omar narrated to us Muhammad bin Jaafar bin Muhammad said: I bear witness on the authority of my father who narrated to me on the authority of his father on the authority of his grandfather on the authority of Ali who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I came from marriage and not from fornication from the time of Adam until my father and mother gave birth to me. Nothing of the fornication of the Age of Ignorance touched me.” And the Almighty’s saying: Hard for Him is that which you suffer means that it is hard for Him to do something that would cause His nation suffering and be difficult for them. For this reason it came in the hadith narrated through various chains of transmission on his authority that he said: I was sent with the easy-going Hanafi school. And in the Sahih: This religion is easy and its entire law is easy, easy, complete, and simple for whomever God Almighty makes it easy for. “He is keen on you” meaning that He is keen on your guidance and the attainment of worldly and otherworldly benefits to you. Al-Tabarani said: Muhammad bin Abdullah Al-Hadrami narrated to us Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Yazid Al-Muqri narrated to us Sufyan bin Uyaynah on the authority of Fatin on the authority of Abu Al-Tufayl on the authority of Abu Dharr who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, left us and there was not a bird flapping its wings in the air except that he would mention to us some of it. Knowledge said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is nothing left that brings one closer to Paradise and distances one from Hell except that it has been made clear to you. Imam Ahmad said: Fatin told us, Al-Masoudi told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Saad, on the authority of Abdah Al-Hudhali, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God did not forbid anything except that He knew that someone from you would see it. Beware, I am holding you back lest you rush into Hell like moths or flies.” Imam Ahmad said: Hasan bin Musa told us, Hammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Ali bin Zaid bin Jud’an, on the authority of Yusuf bin Mihran, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that two angels came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a dream. One of them sat at his feet and the other at his head. The one at his feet said to the one at his head: Give an example of this and his nation. He said: His example and that of his nation is like that of a group of travelers who reached the top of a desert and did not have enough provisions to cross the desert or bring back. While they were like that, a man in a fine garment came to them and said: Tell me, if I bring you to lush meadows and fertile ponds, will you follow me? They said: Yes. He said: So he set off with them and led them to lush meadows and fertile ponds. They ate and drank and became fat. He said to them: Did I not find you in that state and you promised me that if I bring you to lush meadows and fertile ponds, you would follow me? They said: Yes. He said: There are gardens before you that are greener than these and ponds that are more irrigated than these, so follow me. A group said: He has spoken the truth, by God, we will follow him. A group said: We are satisfied with this and will remain on it. Al-Bazzar said: Salamah bin Shabib and Ahmad bin Mansour told us: Ibrahim bin Al-Hakam bin Abaan told us: My father told us: Ikrimah told us: Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, that a Bedouin came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, asking for his help in something. Ikrimah said: I think he said: About blood. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave him something and then said: I have been kind to you. The Bedouin said: No, nor have I been kind. Some of the Muslims became angry and wanted to go to him, but the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, motioned to them to stop. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, got up and reached his house, he called the Bedouin to the house and said: You only came to us to ask us, so we gave you, and you said what you said. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave him something and said: Did I do well to you? The Bedouin said: Yes, may God reward you with good in family and tribe. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “You came to us and asked us, and we gave you, and you said what you said. My companions have something against you because of that, so when you come back, say in their presence what you said in my presence, until it disappears from their hearts.” He said: Yes. So when the Bedouin came, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Your companion came and asked us, and we gave him, and he said what he said. We invited him and gave him, and he claimed that he was satisfied. Is that so, O Bedouin?” The Bedouin said: Yes, and may God reward you with good from your family and tribe. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “My example and that of this Bedouin is like that of a man who had a she-camel that ran away from him, so the people pursued it, but they only made it more averse. The owner of the she-camel said to them, ‘Leave me alone with my she-camel, for I am gentler with her and I know her better.’ So he went to her, took some of the dirt from the ground, called her until she came and responded, and he saddled her. If I had obeyed you in what he said, I would have entered the Fire.” Al-Bazzar narrated it, then he said: We do not know of it being narrated except from this source. I said: It is weak, as is the case with Ibrahim ibn al-Hakam ibn Abaan, and God knows best. His statement: To the believers, Most Kind, Most Merciful is like His statement: “And lower your wing to those who follow you among the believers. But if they disobey you, then say, ‘Indeed, I am innocent of what you do.’ And put your trust in the Almighty, the Most Merciful.” This is what God Almighty commanded him in this noble verse, which is His statement: But if they turn away, meaning they turn away from what you have brought of the great, pure, complete, and comprehensive Shari’ah, “then say, ‘God is sufficient for me. There is no god except Him.’” That is, God is sufficient, there is no god except Him. In Him I have put my trust, as God Almighty said: My Lord, the Lord of the worlds. “The East and the West, there is no god but Him, so take Him as Disposer of affairs.” And He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne, meaning He is the Owner of everything and its Creator, because He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne, which is the roof of creation, and all creation from the heavens and the earths and what is in them and what is between them is under the Throne, subdued by the power of God the Most High, and His knowledge encompasses everything and His power is effective in everything, and He is Disposer of affairs over everything. Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr told us, Bishr ibn Umar told us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Ali ibn Zayd, on the authority of Yusuf ibn Mihran, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, on the authority of Ubayy ibn Ka’b, who said: The last verse to be revealed from the Qur’an was this verse: There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves, to the end of the surah. Abdullah ibn Imam Ahmad said: Ruh ibn Abd al-Mu’min told us, Umar ibn Shaqiq told us, Abu Ja’far al-Razi told us, on the authority of al-Rabi’ ibn Anas, on the authority of Abu al-A’aliyah, on the authority of Ubayy ibn Ka’b, may God be pleased with them, that they collected the Qur’an in copies during the caliphate of Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, and there were men who wrote and Ubayy ibn Ka’b dictated to them. When they reached this verse from Surat Bara’ah, Then they turned away, God turned their hearts away, the verse, so they thought that this was the last thing they would do. A part of the Qur’an was revealed, so Abi bin Ka’b said to them: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited to me two verses after that: There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves to the end of the surah. He said: This is the last part of the Qur’an that was revealed, so it ended with what it began with: With God, there is no god but Him, which is the saying of God Almighty: And We did not send before you any messenger except that We revealed to him, ‘There is no god but Me, so worship Me.’ This is also strange. Ahmad said: Ali bin Bahr told us, Ali bin Muhammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ishaq, on the authority of Yahya bin Ibad, on the authority of his father Ibad bin Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr, may God be pleased with him, who said: Al-Harith bin Khuzaymah came with these two verses from the end of Bara’ah: There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves to Umar bin Al-Khattab and said: Who is with you on this? He said: I do not know, by God, I testify that I heard it from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I memorized it and memorized it. Omar said: And I testify that I heard it from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then he said: If there were three verses, I would have made them a separate surah. So look for a surah from the Qur’an and put it in it. So they put it at the end of Bara’ah. The discussion has already been presented that Omar bin Al-Khattab was the one who advised Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with them both, to collect the Qur’an, so he ordered Zaid bin Thabit to collect it, and Omar was present while they were writing that. In the Sahih, Zaid said: I found the end of Surat Bara’ah with Khuzaymah bin Thabit or Abu Khuzaymah. We have already presented that a group of the Companions mentioned that to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as Khuzaymah bin Thabit said when he began it with them, and God knows best. Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Yazid bin Muhammad on the authority of Abd Al-Razzaq bin Omar - and he said: He was one of the trustworthy Muslims among the devout - on the authority of Mudrik bin Sa’d. Yazid, a trustworthy sheikh, on the authority of Yunus bin Maysarah on the authority of Umm Al-Darda’ on the authority of Abu Al-Darda’, who said: Whoever says in the morning and in the evening: Sufficient for me is God, there is no god. Except in Him I have put my trust, and He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne. Seven times, except that God will suffice him in what concerns him. Ibn Asakir narrated it in the biography of Abd al-Razzaq on the authority of Umar. This is from the narration of Abu Zur’ah al-Dimashqi on his authority on the authority of Abu Sa’d Mudrik ibn Abi Sa’d al-Fazari on the authority of Yunus ibn Maysarah ibn Halis on the authority of Umm al-Darda’ who heard Abu al-Darda’ say: There is no servant who says: God is sufficient for me, there is no god but Him, in Him I have put my trust, and He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne seven times, whether he was telling the truth or lying, except that God will suffice him in what concerns him. This is a strange addition. Then he narrated it in the biography of Abd al-Razzaq Abu Muhammad on the authority of Ahmad ibn Abdullah ibn Abd al-Razzaq on the authority of his grandfather Abd al-Razzaq ibn Umar with his chain of transmission, so he raised it and mentioned something similar with the addition, and this is strange, and God knows best.
